
===== FILE: \cmake\PS3RecompBootImage.cmake =====
# Configure a port runner to use its PPU image without a launch-time file arg.
# Windows builds embed the image as RCDATA; other platforms keep the configured
# path as the runner default because their executable resource formats differ.
function(ps3recomp_configure_boot_image target source_dir)
    cmake_parse_arguments(PARSE_ARGV 2 ARG "" "" "CANDIDATES")

    set(PORT_PPU_ELF "" CACHE FILEPATH
        "PPU ELF used to initialize guest memory (embedded in Windows builds)")

    set(boot_image "${PORT_PPU_ELF}")
    if(NOT boot_image)
        foreach(candidate IN LISTS ARG_CANDIDATES)
            if(EXISTS "${candidate}")
                set(boot_image "${candidate}")
                break()
            endif()
        endforeach()
    endif()

    if(NOT boot_image)
        message(STATUS "No default PPU image found; pass an ELF path at launch")
        return()
    endif()

    get_filename_component(boot_image "${boot_image}" ABSOLUTE
                           BASE_DIR "${source_dir}")
    if(NOT EXISTS "${boot_image}")
        message(WARNING "Configured PPU image does not exist: ${boot_image}")
        return()
    endif()

    if(WIN32)
        file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${boot_image}" boot_image_native)
        string(REPLACE "\\" "\\\\" boot_image_rc "${boot_image_native}")
        set(PS3RECOMP_BOOT_IMAGE_RC_PATH "${boot_image_rc}")
        set(resource_file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/ps3recomp_boot_image.rc")
        configure_file(
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_FUNCTION_LIST_DIR}/ps3recomp_boot_image.rc.in"
            "${resource_file}" @ONLY)
        set_source_files_properties("${resource_file}" PROPERTIES
            OBJECT_DEPENDS "${boot_image}")
        target_sources(${target} PRIVATE "${resource_file}")
        set_property(SOURCE "${source_dir}/main.cpp" APPEND PROPERTY
            COMPILE_DEFINITIONS PS3RECOMP_EMBED_PPU_ELF=1)
        message(STATUS "Embedded PPU boot image: ${boot_image}")
    else()
        set_property(SOURCE "${source_dir}/main.cpp" APPEND PROPERTY
            COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "PS3RECOMP_DEFAULT_PPU_ELF=\"${boot_image}\"")
        message(STATUS "Default PPU boot image: ${boot_image}")
    endif()
endfunction()


===== FILE: \cmake\PS3RecompSPU.cmake =====
# Generate all discovered SPU ELF programs from explicitly supplied input files.
# The helper runs at configure time so the source list belongs to this exact
# generation. Input/tool changes trigger reconfiguration before compilation.
function(ps3recomp_generate_spu output_dir)
    find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter REQUIRED)
    set(command "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}" "${PS3RECOMP_DIR}/tools/build_spu_workloads.py"
        --lifted "${output_dir}" --out "${output_dir}/spu_workloads.c" --constructor)
    foreach(input IN LISTS ARGN)
        get_filename_component(input "${input}" ABSOLUTE BASE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}")
        list(APPEND command --input "${input}")
        set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${input}")
    endforeach()
    foreach(tool IN ITEMS build_spu_workloads.py spu_program_pipeline.py spu_elf.py
                          extract_spu_images.py spu_lifter.py find_spu_functions.py spu_disasm.py)
        set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${PS3RECOMP_DIR}/tools/${tool}")
    endforeach()
    execute_process(COMMAND ${command} RESULT_VARIABLE result OUTPUT_VARIABLE output ERROR_VARIABLE error)
    if(NOT result EQUAL 0)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "SPU generation incomplete. Inspect ${output_dir}/inventory.json.\n${output}\n${error}")
    endif()
    include("${output_dir}/sources.cmake")
    set(SPU_GENERATED_SOURCES "${SPU_GENERATED_SOURCES}" PARENT_SCOPE)
endfunction()

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
# Keep in step with the changelog in README.md. This sat at 0.3.0 until August
# 2026 while the project shipped 0.6.x through 0.8.0, so every build printed
# "ps3recomp runtime v0.3.0" and was believed. v0.9.0 is the first TAGGED one.
project(ps3recomp_runtime
    VERSION 0.11.0
    LANGUAGES C CXX
    DESCRIPTION "ps3recomp - Static recompilation runtime for PS3 games"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standards
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Options
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
option(PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS "Build unit tests" OFF)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collect source files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# HLE library sources
file(GLOB_RECURSE HLE_SOURCES
    "libs/system/*.c"
    "libs/filesystem/*.c"
    "libs/input/*.c"
    "libs/audio/*.c"
    "libs/video/*.c"
    "libs/network/*.c"
    "libs/spurs/*.c"
    "libs/sync/*.c"
    "libs/codec/*.c"
    "libs/font/*.c"
    "libs/misc/*.c"
    "libs/hardware/*.c"
    "runtime/diag/*.c"      # yz_frontier_trace, used by the live draw engine
)
# Exclude test harnesses (e.g. libs/video/tests/*): they define their own main().
list(FILTER HLE_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "/tests/")

# The Vulkan RSX backend is opt-in while it grows (stage V0: clear + present).
# It loads libvulkan at run time, so building needs only the Vulkan headers --
# no target-architecture libvulkan, which keeps cross-compiling simple.
option(PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN "Build the Vulkan RSX backend (Linux)" OFF)
list(FILTER HLE_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "rsx_vulkan_backend\\.c$")
if(PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN)
    if(WIN32 OR APPLE)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN is Linux-only for now")
    endif()
    find_path(PS3RECOMP_VULKAN_INCLUDE_DIR vulkan/vulkan.h)
    if(NOT PS3RECOMP_VULKAN_INCLUDE_DIR)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "Vulkan headers not found. Debian/Ubuntu: "
            "libvulkan-dev, Fedora: vulkan-headers -- or pass "
            "-DPS3RECOMP_VULKAN_INCLUDE_DIR=<dir containing vulkan/vulkan.h>")
    endif()
    list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_vulkan_backend.c")
    # HLSL -> SPIR-V for guest programs: a stub unless glslang is found below.
    list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_shader_spirv.cpp")
endif()

# The Metal backend is Objective-C and Apple-only, so it is added explicitly
# rather than globbed. It needs no platform #ifdef of its own as a result.
if(APPLE)
    enable_language(OBJC)
    list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_metal_backend.m")
endif()
# The HLSL -> MSL translator is C++ (it drives glslang's C++ API) and compiles
# to a stub wherever the shader tools are absent, so it is part of the
# library everywhere. See the "Guest shaders on Metal" section below.
list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_shader_msl.cpp")
# cellAtrac decodes with FFmpeg's ATRAC3plus decoder as extracted by PPSSPP
# (LGPL-2.1, kept separate in third_party/at3_standalone -- see its README).
file(GLOB AT3_SOURCES "third_party/at3_standalone/*.cpp")
set_source_files_properties(${AT3_SOURCES} PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-w")  # upstream code
list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES ${AT3_SOURCES})

# Runtime core (syscalls, PPU, SPU, memory)
file(GLOB_RECURSE RUNTIME_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "runtime/*.c"
    "runtime/*.cpp"
)
# Exclude:
#  - test harnesses (runtime/*/tests/*): they have their own main() and #include
#    per-game generated headers (spu_recomp.h) that a plain library build lacks.
#  - the PPU boot scaffold (runtime/ppu/, runtime/host/): these are compiled
#    per-game against the lifter-generated ppu_recomp.h (and the game's RSX/D3D12
#    backend), not as part of the game-agnostic runtime library. See
#    docs/PPU_RECOMP.md.
#  - spu_dispatch_mt.c: the musttail SPU indirect-branch fast path. It uses
#    __attribute__((musttail)), which MSVC cannot parse, and it must be compiled
#    *inside the game build* by clang so the tail call is guaranteed -- a plain
#    call leaks one resolver frame per guest loop iteration. A port adds it to
#    its own target; see templates/project/CMakeLists.txt.
list(FILTER RUNTIME_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "/tests/|/runtime/ppu/|/runtime/host/|/spu_dispatch_mt\.c$")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Static library
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(ps3recomp_runtime STATIC
    ${HLE_SOURCES}
    ${RUNTIME_SOURCES}
)

target_include_directories(ps3recomp_runtime PUBLIC
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include"
)

# HLE modules include their own headers
target_include_directories(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/system"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/filesystem"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/input"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/audio"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/network"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/spurs"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/sync"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/codec"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/font"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/misc"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/spu"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include"
)

# Platform-specific link libraries
if(WIN32)
    # SDL GameController adds native support for DualSense and other HID pads.
    # Keep XInput as the no-extra-dependency fallback for Xbox controllers.
    find_package(SDL2 QUIET)
    if(SDL2_FOUND)
        if(TARGET SDL2::SDL2-static)
            set(PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET SDL2::SDL2-static)
        elseif(TARGET SDL2::SDL2)
            set(PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET SDL2::SDL2)
        endif()

        if(PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET)
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ${PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET})
            get_target_property(_ps3recomp_sdl2_type ${PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET} TYPE)
            if(_ps3recomp_sdl2_type STREQUAL "SHARED_LIBRARY")
                get_target_property(_ps3recomp_sdl2_runtime
                    ${PS3RECOMP_SDL2_TARGET} IMPORTED_LOCATION)
                set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY PS3RECOMP_SDL2_RUNTIME
                    "${_ps3recomp_sdl2_runtime}")
            endif()
        else()
            target_include_directories(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ${SDL2_INCLUDE_DIRS})
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ${SDL2_LIBRARIES})
        endif()
        target_compile_definitions(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE PS3RECOMP_PAD_USE_SDL2=1)
        message(STATUS "  SDL2:         found (Xbox and DualSense GameController input enabled)")
    else()
        message(STATUS "  SDL2:         not found (using XInput; install SDL2 for direct DualSense input)")
    endif()

    target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
        ws2_32      # Winsock for network modules
        ole32       # COM for WASAPI audio
        bcrypt      # BCryptGenRandom for SSL RNG
        dxguid      # IID_IDXGIFactory6 used by the D3D12 backend
    )
else()
    # cellPad and cellAudio select their SDL2 backends unconditionally off
    # Windows (see PAD_BACKEND_SDL2 / AUDIO_BACKEND_SDL2), so SDL2 is required
    # here -- docs/BUILDING.md already lists it as the Linux/macOS dependency.
    find_package(SDL2 QUIET)

        if(TARGET SDL2::SDL2)
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE SDL2::SDL2)
        else()
            target_include_directories(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ${SDL2_INCLUDE_DIRS})
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ${SDL2_LIBRARIES})
        endif()
        message(STATUS "  SDL2:         found (input + audio backends enabled)")
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "SDL2 not found. It provides the cellPad and cellAudio backends on "
            "non-Windows hosts.\n"
            "  macOS:  brew install sdl2\n"
            "  Debian: apt install libsdl2-dev\n"
            "If SDL2 is installed in a non-standard prefix, pass "
            "-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<prefix>.")
    endif()

    find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
    target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE Threads::Threads)

# cellVdec decodes H.264 / MPEG-2 through FFmpeg when this is on. libavcodec
# is loaded at run time (dlopen / LoadLibrary), never linked, so building needs
# only the FFmpeg headers, and a binary run where FFmpeg is absent -- or with
# PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG=0 -- keeps the callback-only decoders. FFmpeg stays a
# separate, user-supplied LGPL library. See libs/codec/ffmpeg_runtime.h.
option(PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME "Decode media through FFmpeg loaded at run time (needs the FFmpeg headers)" OFF)
if(PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME)
    find_path(PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR libavcodec/avcodec.h)
    if(NOT PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "FFmpeg headers not found. Debian/Ubuntu: "
            "libavcodec-dev, Fedora: ffmpeg-free-devel, MSYS2: mingw-w64-x86_64-ffmpeg "
            "-- or pass -DPS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR=<dir containing libavcodec/avcodec.h>")
    endif()
    target_include_directories(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE "${PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR}")
    target_compile_definitions(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME)
    target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PUBLIC ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS})
    message(STATUS "  FFmpeg:       run-time loaded (headers in ${PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR})")
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guest shaders on Metal: HLSL -> SPIR-V -> MSL
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The RSX decompilers emit HLSL for the D3D12 backend. Metal cannot compile
# that, so libs/video/rsx_shader_msl.cpp lowers it with glslang (HLSL ->
# SPIR-V) and spirv-cross (SPIR-V -> MSL). Both are optional: without them the
# module compiles to a stub, rsx_hlsl_to_msl_available() says so, and the
# Metal backend stays on its fixed-function path. The translation has no GPU
# in it, so it is built and tested on Linux as well -- that is where the
# decompilers' HLSL meets glslang's front end on every push.
#
#   macOS:  brew install glslang spirv-cross
#   Debian: apt install glslang-dev glslang-tools spirv-tools \
#                       libspirv-cross-c-shared-dev
#           (glslang-tools only because the packaged CMake config declares
#           the standalone binary as an imported target and fails to load
#           without it)
set(PS3RECOMP_MSL_TRANSLATION OFF)
if(UNIX)
    find_package(glslang CONFIG QUIET)

    # spirv-cross's C API. Debian ships it as a shared library and Homebrew as
    # a static one, under different pkg-config names -- and pkg-config itself
    # is not a given on a Mac, so fall back to a plain header + library search.
    set(SPVC_OK OFF)
    find_package(PkgConfig QUIET)
    if(PkgConfig_FOUND)
        pkg_check_modules(SPVC QUIET spirv-cross-c-shared)
        if(NOT SPVC_FOUND)
            pkg_check_modules(SPVC QUIET spirv-cross-c)
        endif()
        if(SPVC_FOUND)
            set(SPVC_INC     ${SPVC_INCLUDE_DIRS})
            set(SPVC_LIBS    ${SPVC_LINK_LIBRARIES})
            set(SPVC_LIBDIRS ${SPVC_LIBRARY_DIRS})
            set(SPVC_OK ON)
        endif()
    endif()
    if(NOT SPVC_OK)
        find_path(SPVC_INC_DIR spirv_cross_c.h PATH_SUFFIXES spirv_cross)
        find_library(SPVC_LIB NAMES spirv-cross-c-shared spirv-cross-c)
        if(SPVC_INC_DIR AND SPVC_LIB)
            set(SPVC_INC  ${SPVC_INC_DIR})
            set(SPVC_LIBS ${SPVC_LIB})
            get_filename_component(SPVC_LIBDIRS "${SPVC_LIB}" DIRECTORY)
            set(SPVC_OK ON)
        endif()
    endif()

    if(glslang_FOUND AND SPVC_OK
       AND TARGET glslang::glslang AND TARGET glslang::SPIRV)
        add_library(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE)
        target_compile_definitions(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE
            PS3RECOMP_HAVE_MSL_TRANSLATION=1)
        target_include_directories(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE ${SPVC_INC})
        target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE
            glslang::glslang glslang::SPIRV ${SPVC_LIBS})
        if(TARGET glslang::glslang-default-resource-limits)
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE
                glslang::glslang-default-resource-limits)
        endif()
        # A static spirv-cross C API (Homebrew's) needs the backends it was
        # built from, and neither pkg-config nor the library name says so:
        # pick up the static siblings next to it. The shared one carries
        # its own.
        if(SPVC_LIBS MATCHES "\\.a$")
            foreach(part msl glsl hlsl cpp reflect util core)
                find_library(SPVC_PART_${part} NAMES spirv-cross-${part}
                    HINTS ${SPVC_LIBDIRS} NO_DEFAULT_PATH)
                if(SPVC_PART_${part})
                    target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_msl_translation INTERFACE
                        ${SPVC_PART_${part}})
                endif()
            endforeach()
        endif()
        target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE ps3recomp_msl_translation)
        set(PS3RECOMP_MSL_TRANSLATION ON)
        message(STATUS "  Shaders:      guest programs translated to MSL (glslang ${glslang_VERSION}, ${SPVC_LIBS})")
    else()
        message(STATUS "  Shaders:      glslang/spirv-cross not found; Metal backend stays fixed-function")
    endif()
endif()

# Guest shaders on Vulkan: HLSL -> SPIR-V. glslang only -- Vulkan consumes
# SPIR-V, so spirv-cross is not needed. Without glslang
# libs/video/rsx_shader_spirv.cpp is a stub and the Vulkan backend stays on
# its fixed-function path.
if(PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN)
    if(glslang_FOUND AND TARGET glslang::glslang AND TARGET glslang::SPIRV)
        set_source_files_properties(
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_shader_spirv.cpp"
            PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS PS3RECOMP_HAVE_SPIRV_TRANSLATION=1)
        target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE glslang::glslang glslang::SPIRV)
        if(TARGET glslang::glslang-default-resource-limits)
            target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
                glslang::glslang-default-resource-limits)
        endif()
        set(PS3RECOMP_SPIRV_TRANSLATION ON)
        message(STATUS "  Vulkan:       guest programs available (glslang ${glslang_VERSION}); "
                       "opt in with PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1")
    else()
        message(STATUS "  Vulkan:       glslang not found; guest programs unavailable")
    endif()
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compiler flags
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang|GNU")
    target_compile_options(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
        -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter
        -fno-strict-aliasing
        # No spontaneous fused multiply-add. MSVC never contracts, and x86-64
        # without -mfma has nothing to contract into, so every validated
        # result came from separate multiplies and adds; arm64 has FMA in
        # the base ISA and Clang fuses by default there. A PPC fmadd is
        # spelt as one where the lifter means one.
        -ffp-contract=off
        # Explicit, because the per-config defaults cannot be trusted: this
        # tree's caches carry CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE="" and CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE="",
        # and clang-cl with no /O flag compiles at /Od -- a "Release" runtime
        # was unoptimised without a word. Duplicating a default -O2 is harmless.
        $<$<CONFIG:Release,RelWithDebInfo>:-O2>
    )
    # SSE4.1 (any x86-64 since ~2008): pshufb/blendv for spu_shufb, the
    # hottest SPU op in lifted audio code. Probed rather than assumed: recent
    # Apple clang rejects the flag outright for arm64 ("unsupported option
    # '-msse4.1'"), which stops the whole runtime from building there.
    include(CheckCCompilerFlag)
    check_c_compiler_flag(-msse4.1 PS3RECOMP_HAS_MSSE41)
    if(PS3RECOMP_HAS_MSSE41)
        target_compile_options(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE -msse4.1)
    endif()
elseif(MSVC)
    # Real cl.exe -- clang-cl reports its id as Clang and is handled above.
    #
    # This does not currently build. The runtime and the lifted output use GCC/
    # Clang builtins that cl has no equivalent for, and the failure lands as a
    # wall of errors in whichever file the build happens to reach first rather
    # than as anything that names the cause. Say it here instead.
    message(WARNING
        "Building with cl.exe (MSVC). This is not currently supported.\n"
        "  The runtime uses __atomic_* builtins, __int128 and __builtin_bswap*, "
        "and the lifted output uses __int128 for the PPC 64x64 multiplies. "
        "cl has none of them.\n"
        "  Use clang-cl instead -- it consumes the MSVC headers and libraries, "
        "so nothing else about a Visual Studio build changes:\n"
        "    cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja "
        "-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl\n"
        "  See docs/BUILDING.md. Porting the intrinsics to cl is a welcome "
        "contribution; nothing else stands in the way.")
    target_compile_options(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
        /W3 /wd4100 /wd4244 /wd4267 /wd4996
        /Zc:__cplusplus
        /experimental:c11atomics   # Enable C11 <stdatomic.h> support
    )
    target_compile_definitions(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE
        _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS
    )
endif()

if(NOT MSVC AND NOT WIN32)
    # dladdr/Dl_info (runtime/platform/win32_backtrace.h) are GNU extensions
    # that glibc hides unless _GNU_SOURCE is set. g++ defines it implicitly,
    # so the C++ boot scaffold never noticed; a C file including the same
    # shim does not get it for free.
    target_compile_definitions(ps3recomp_runtime PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS)
    include(CTest)
    # sync_stress is written directly against the Win32 threading API
    # (WaitForMultipleObjects, joinable HANDLEs, Interlocked*, CRITICAL_SECTION).
    # Off Windows all of that comes from runtime/platform/win32_compat.h, so
    # the suite runs everywhere -- and is the arm64 memory-model regression
    # net for the lv2 sync primitives.
    add_subdirectory(tests/sync_stress)
    # cellFiber switches contexts with Windows fibers on Windows and ucontext
    # everywhere else. Apple deprecated the ucontext routines and gates both
    # them and the shape of ucontext_t on _XOPEN_SOURCE, so whether that path
    # works on arm64 is a question to answer rather than assume.
    add_subdirectory(tests/fiber_switch)
    # Syscall 14's address/flags classification as a plain unit test: the
    # check is pure, so the test links one runtime translation unit
    # (lv2_lock_line.c) and nothing else.
    add_subdirectory(tests/syscalls)
    # cellVdec through its guest API: the callback-only decoder always, and
    # real H.264 / MPEG-2 decode when FFmpeg is on (libs/codec/tests).
    add_subdirectory(libs/codec/tests)
    # cellGcm's FIFO walker without a backend: where GET_REPORT writes for
    # each report DMA context. Links the runtime like the POSIX host below.
    if(UNIX)
        add_subdirectory(tests/gcm_reports)
    endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PPU boot smoke title
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The one target that LINKS AND RUNS the PPU boot scaffold. runtime/ppu/ is the
# game-agnostic boot path every port is built on, and nothing here has ever
# built it: it #includes the lifter's per-game ppu_recomp.h, so
# tools/check_ppu_scaffold.py compiles it against a stub header and stops
# there. Compiling is not running, and on POSIX the loader, the NID bridge, the
# lv2 syscalls, guest threads, the frame clock and the RSX backend had never
# once run together.
#
# runtime/ppu/tests/smoke/ supplies what was missing: a hand-written program in
# the lifter's ABI, and tools/make_smoke_elf.py writes both the PPU ELF it is
# loaded from and the ppu_recomp.h it compiles against -- the header from
# ppu_lifter.py's own HEADER_PREAMBLE, so the synthetic title cannot drift away
# from the ABI a real one gets.
#
# The HLE NID table is generated exactly as a port generates it, so the smoke
# title's firmware imports resolve through the same bridge a game's do.
if(UNIX)
    find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter QUIET)
    if(NOT Python3_Interpreter_FOUND)
        message(STATUS "  Boot smoke:   no python3; ps3recomp_boot_smoke not built")
    else()
        set(SMOKE_GEN "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/smoke")

        add_custom_command(
            OUTPUT "${SMOKE_GEN}/smoke.elf" "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_recomp.h"
            COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/make_smoke_elf.py"
                    --out    "${SMOKE_GEN}/smoke.elf"
                    --header "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_recomp.h"
            DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/make_smoke_elf.py"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/ppu_lifter.py"
            COMMENT "Generating the smoke title's image and ppu_recomp.h")

        add_custom_command(
            OUTPUT "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_hle_nids.cpp"
            COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/gen_hle_nids.py"
                    --out "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_hle_nids.cpp" --all
            DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/gen_hle_nids.py"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/nid_database.py"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hle_special_exports.json"
            COMMENT "Generating the HLE NID -> handler table")

        add_executable(ps3recomp_boot_smoke
            runtime/ppu/tests/boot_main.cpp
            runtime/ppu/tests/smoke/smoke_recomp.c
            runtime/ppu/ppu_loader.cpp
            runtime/ppu/ppu_hle.cpp
            runtime/ppu/ppu_fs.cpp
            runtime/ppu/ppu_sysprx.cpp
            "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_hle_nids.cpp"
            "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_recomp.h"
        )
        target_include_directories(ps3recomp_boot_smoke PRIVATE
            "${SMOKE_GEN}"                                  # the generated ppu_recomp.h
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/ppu"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/spu"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/memory"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/syscalls"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/platform"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video"
        )
        target_link_libraries(ps3recomp_boot_smoke PRIVATE ps3recomp_runtime)
        set_target_properties(ps3recomp_boot_smoke PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE CXX)

        # Where the runnable image lands, so CI and a developer both say
        #   ./build/ps3recomp_boot_smoke build/smoke/smoke.elf
        message(STATUS "  Boot smoke:   ps3recomp_boot_smoke + smoke/smoke.elf")

        # The same lift again, arranged the way a port's own tree arranges one:
        # the generated ppu_recomp.h and the lifted source in one directory,
        # which is what templates/project wants for -DRECOMP_DIR. The header is
        # generated into the build tree and the source lives in the repository,
        # so a directory holding both has to be made rather than pointed at.
        #
        # This is what lets CI build the project template against a real lift
        # and run it -- the check that a port started from templates/project
        # still boots, on a platform where it can be run.
        set(SMOKE_LIFT "${SMOKE_GEN}/lift")
        set(SMOKE_LIFT_SRC
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/runtime/ppu/tests/smoke/smoke_recomp.c")
        add_custom_command(
            OUTPUT "${SMOKE_LIFT}/ppu_recomp.h" "${SMOKE_LIFT}/smoke_recomp.c"
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E make_directory "${SMOKE_LIFT}"
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_if_different
                    "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_recomp.h" "${SMOKE_LIFT}/ppu_recomp.h"
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_if_different
                    "${SMOKE_LIFT_SRC}" "${SMOKE_LIFT}/smoke_recomp.c"
            DEPENDS "${SMOKE_GEN}/ppu_recomp.h" "${SMOKE_LIFT_SRC}"
            COMMENT "Staging the smoke title's lift as a RECOMP_DIR")
        add_custom_target(ps3recomp_smoke_lift ALL
            DEPENDS "${SMOKE_LIFT}/ppu_recomp.h" "${SMOKE_LIFT}/smoke_recomp.c")
        message(STATUS "  Smoke lift:   smoke/lift (a RECOMP_DIR for templates/project)")
    endif()
endif()

===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellDaisy.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellDaisy HLE implementation
 *
 * SPURS Daisy Chain — lock-free FIFO queues.
 * Stub — pipes accept data and deliver it immediately (no SPU involvement).
 * Uses a simple ring buffer for each pipe.
 */

#include "cellDaisy.h"
#include "../../runtime/ppu/ppu_memory.h"   /* GUEST_PTR, vm_write*: guest EA -> host pointer */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Internal state */

typedef struct {
    int  in_use;
    u32  direction;
    u32  entrySize;
    u32  depth;
    u32  head;     /* read index */
    u32  tail;     /* write index */
    u32  count;
    u8*  ring;     /* ring buffer */
} DaisyPipeSlot;

static DaisyPipeSlot s_pipes[CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES];

static int daisy_alloc(void)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES; i++) {
        if (!s_pipes[i].in_use) return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

/* API */

s32 cellDaisyPipeAttributeInitialize(CellDaisyPipeAttribute* attr,
                                     u32 direction, u32 entrySize, u32 depth)
{
    attr = GUEST_PTR(attr, CellDaisyPipeAttribute*);
    if (!attr) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    if (entrySize == 0 || depth == 0 || depth > CELL_DAISY_MAX_DEPTH)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    memset(attr, 0, sizeof(*attr));
    attr->direction = direction;
    attr->entrySize = entrySize;
    attr->depth = depth;
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyCreatePipe(void* spurs, CellDaisyPipe* pipe,
                        const CellDaisyPipeAttribute* attr,
                        void* buffer, u32 bufferSize)
{
    attr = GUEST_PTR(attr, const CellDaisyPipeAttribute*);
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    (void)spurs; (void)buffer; (void)bufferSize;
    printf("[cellDaisy] CreatePipe(entrySize=%u, depth=%u)\n",
           attr ? attr->entrySize : 0, attr ? attr->depth : 0);

    if (!pipe || !attr) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    int slot = daisy_alloc();
    if (slot < 0) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;

    DaisyPipeSlot* p = &s_pipes[slot];
    p->in_use = 1;
    p->direction = attr->direction;
    p->entrySize = attr->entrySize;
    p->depth = attr->depth;
    p->head = 0;
    p->tail = 0;
    p->count = 0;

    /* Allocate ring buffer */
    p->ring = (u8*)malloc(attr->entrySize * attr->depth);
    if (!p->ring) {
        p->in_use = 0;
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    }
    memset(p->ring, 0, attr->entrySize * attr->depth);

    vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)pipe, (u32)slot);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyDestroyPipe(CellDaisyPipe* pipe)
{
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    if (!pipe) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    u32 slot = *pipe;
    if (slot >= CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES || !s_pipes[slot].in_use)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    printf("[cellDaisy] DestroyPipe(%u)\n", slot);
    free(s_pipes[slot].ring);
    memset(&s_pipes[slot], 0, sizeof(DaisyPipeSlot));
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyPipePush(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, const void* data)
{
    data = GUEST_PTR(data, const void*);
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    if (!pipe || !data) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    u32 slot = *pipe;
    if (slot >= CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES || !s_pipes[slot].in_use)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    DaisyPipeSlot* p = &s_pipes[slot];
    if (p->count >= p->depth)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_QUEUE_FULL;

    memcpy(p->ring + (p->tail * p->entrySize), data, p->entrySize);
    p->tail = (p->tail + 1) % p->depth;
    p->count++;
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyPipeTryPush(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, const void* data)
{
    return cellDaisyPipePush(pipe, data);
}

s32 cellDaisyPipePop(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, void* data)
{
    data = GUEST_PTR(data, void*);
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    if (!pipe || !data) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    u32 slot = *pipe;
    if (slot >= CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES || !s_pipes[slot].in_use)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    DaisyPipeSlot* p = &s_pipes[slot];
    if (p->count == 0)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_QUEUE_EMPTY;

    memcpy(data, p->ring + (p->head * p->entrySize), p->entrySize);
    p->head = (p->head + 1) % p->depth;
    p->count--;
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyPipeTryPop(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, void* data)
{
    return cellDaisyPipePop(pipe, data);
}

s32 cellDaisyPipeGetCount(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, u32* count)
{
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    if (!pipe || !count) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    u32 slot = *pipe;
    if (slot >= CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES || !s_pipes[slot].in_use)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)count, s_pipes[slot].count);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellDaisyPipeGetFreeCount(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, u32* count)
{
    pipe = GUEST_PTR(pipe, CellDaisyPipe*);
    if (!pipe || !count) return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    u32 slot = *pipe;
    if (slot >= CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES || !s_pipes[slot].in_use)
        return (s32)CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)count, s_pipes[slot].depth - s_pipes[slot].count);
    return CELL_OK;
}


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellDaisy.h =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellDaisy HLE
 *
 * SPURS Daisy Chain — lock-free FIFO queues for producer-consumer patterns
 * between PPU and SPU. Used for streaming data pipelines.
 * Stub — queue management works, data passes through immediately.
 */

#ifndef PS3RECOMP_CELL_DAISY_H
#define PS3RECOMP_CELL_DAISY_H

#include "ps3emu/ps3types.h"
#include "ps3emu/error_codes.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Error codes */
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED     0x80410B01
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_ALREADY_INITIALIZED 0x80410B02
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT    0x80410B03
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY       0x80410B04
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_QUEUE_FULL          0x80410B05
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_QUEUE_EMPTY         0x80410B06
#define CELL_DAISY_ERROR_BUSY                0x80410B07

/* Pipe depth limits */
#define CELL_DAISY_MAX_PIPES     32
#define CELL_DAISY_MAX_DEPTH     256

/* Pipe direction */
#define CELL_DAISY_DIRECTION_PPU_TO_SPU   0
#define CELL_DAISY_DIRECTION_SPU_TO_PPU   1
#define CELL_DAISY_DIRECTION_SPU_TO_SPU   2

/* Opaque handles */
typedef u32 CellDaisyPipe;

/* Pipe attributes */
typedef struct CellDaisyPipeAttribute {
    u32 direction;
    u32 entrySize;
    u32 depth;
    u32 flags;
    u32 reserved[4];
} CellDaisyPipeAttribute;

/* Functions */
s32 cellDaisyPipeAttributeInitialize(CellDaisyPipeAttribute* attr,
                                     u32 direction, u32 entrySize, u32 depth);

s32 cellDaisyCreatePipe(void* spurs, CellDaisyPipe* pipe,
                        const CellDaisyPipeAttribute* attr,
                        void* buffer, u32 bufferSize);
s32 cellDaisyDestroyPipe(CellDaisyPipe* pipe);

s32 cellDaisyPipePush(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, const void* data);
s32 cellDaisyPipeTryPush(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, const void* data);
s32 cellDaisyPipePop(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, void* data);
s32 cellDaisyPipeTryPop(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, void* data);

s32 cellDaisyPipeGetCount(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, u32* count);
s32 cellDaisyPipeGetFreeCount(CellDaisyPipe* pipe, u32* count);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* PS3RECOMP_CELL_DAISY_H */


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellFiber.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellFiber HLE implementation
 *
 * The SDK's scheduler-based PPU fibers (see cellFiber.h). RunFibers runs on the calling PPU thread and switches to one
 * fiber at a time; a fiber runs the guest entry through the PPU thread trampoline on its own host stack with its own
 * ppu_context, whose r1 points into the guest stack the caller passed to CreateFiber. A fiber hands control back to
 * RunFibers when it blocks (WaitSignal, JoinFiber), yields or ends.
 *
 * Not modelled: the scheduler attribute and fiber attribute contents (both are zeroed on initialisation and ignored),
 * and the fiber context-switch trace/ufiber utilities of the SDK.
 */

/* Darwin gates the ucontext routines AND the shape of ucontext_t itself on _XOPEN_SOURCE, so this has to come before
 * the first system header any include below reaches -- see the static assertion further down for what defining it
 * late costs. Nothing above this line. */
#if defined(__APPLE__) && !defined(_XOPEN_SOURCE)
#  define _XOPEN_SOURCE 600
#  define _DARWIN_C_SOURCE 1   /* and back: _XOPEN_SOURCE alone hides MAP_ANONYMOUS, which vm.h uses */
#endif

#include "cellFiber.h"
#include "../../runtime/ppu/ppu_memory.h"   /* vm_base, vm_write32, vm_memset: guest EA -> host */
#include "../../runtime/syscalls/sys_ppu_thread.h"   /* ppu_context, g_ppu_thread_entry_trampoline */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#ifdef _WIN32
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <pthread.h>
#include <ucontext.h>

#if defined(__APPLE__)
/* getcontext() points uc_mcontext at ucontext_t's own __mcontext_data member and writes uc_mcsize (816) bytes there.
 * That member is declared only when _XOPEN_SOURCE was defined before <sys/_types/_ucontext.h> was first pulled in;
 * without it the struct is the 64-byte header alone and every getcontext, swapcontext and makecontext writes 752
 * bytes off the end of it. The define above is the fix; this is the tripwire, because moving an #include up here
 * would silently undo it. */
_Static_assert(sizeof(ucontext_t) > 64,
               "ucontext_t has no embedded machine state: _XOPEN_SOURCE was "
               "defined too late and getcontext will write past the struct");
#endif
#endif

extern PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;

/* Host stack of each fiber. The guest stack is separate: it holds the guest's own frames, this one the host frames of
 * the lifted code and of the trampoline. */
#define FIBER_HOST_STACK   (4u * 1024u * 1024u)
/* Smallest guest stack CreateFiber accepts. */
#define FIBER_MIN_STACK    0x400u
/* Guest stack bytes kept free above the initial r1 (the ABI's back chain and register save area). */
#define FIBER_STACK_TOP_PAD 0x100u
/* r3 for the fiber's thread id when it is created outside a PPU thread. */
#define FIBER_FALLBACK_THREAD_ID 0x7FFF0000ull

/* The retail cellFiber PPU scheduler API is different from the small
 * CellFiber handle API below. A guest fiber is a PPU function running on a
 * host fiber: switching the host fiber preserves the recompiled C call stack
 * and its live ppu_context while cellFiberPpuYield switches back to the guest
 * scheduler. */
typedef struct PpuFiberSlot {
    int in_use;
    u32 scheduler_ea;
    u32 fiber_ea;
    u32 entry_opd;
    u64 arg;
    u32 priority;
    u32 guest_stack_ea;
    u32 guest_stack_size;
    u32 on_exit_opd;
    u64 on_exit_arg;
    s32 exit_status;
    int exit_status_set;
    int exit_callback_called;
    int state;                 /* 0 ready, 1 running, 2 waiting, 3 terminated */
    int wait_target;
    u32 run_epoch;
    int force_resume;
#ifdef _WIN32
    LPVOID native_fiber;
#else
    ucontext_t context;
    u8* host_stack;
    size_t host_stack_size;
#endif
} PpuFiberSlot;

typedef struct PpuSchedulerSlot {
    int in_use;
    u32 scheduler_ea;
    u32 epoch;
} PpuSchedulerSlot;

#define CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS 256
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_MAX_SCHEDULERS 8
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_HOST_STACK_SIZE (1024u * 1024u)
static PpuFiberSlot s_ppu_fibers[CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS];
static PpuSchedulerSlot s_ppu_schedulers[CELL_FIBER_PPU_MAX_SCHEDULERS];
#ifdef _WIN32
static __declspec(thread) LPVOID s_ppu_scheduler_host = NULL;
static __declspec(thread) int s_ppu_running_slot = -1;
static __declspec(thread) u32 s_ppu_running_scheduler = 0;
#else
static _Thread_local ucontext_t s_ppu_scheduler_host;
static _Thread_local int s_ppu_running_slot = -1;
static _Thread_local u32 s_ppu_running_scheduler = 0;
#endif

extern u64 ppu_guest_call_on_stack(u32 opd_addr, u32 guest_sp,
                                   u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3,
                                   u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7);
extern u64 ppu_guest_call(u32 opd_addr, u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3,
                          u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7);
extern void ps3_hle_register_ctx(u32 nid, const char* name,
                                void (*fn)(ppu_context*));
extern PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;

static PpuSchedulerSlot* ppu_scheduler_find(u32 scheduler_ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_FIBER_PPU_MAX_SCHEDULERS; i++)
        if (s_ppu_schedulers[i].in_use &&
            s_ppu_schedulers[i].scheduler_ea == scheduler_ea)
            return &s_ppu_schedulers[i];
    return NULL;
}

static int ppu_fiber_find(u32 fiber_ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS; i++)
        if (s_ppu_fibers[i].in_use && s_ppu_fibers[i].fiber_ea == fiber_ea)
            return i;
    return -1;
}

static void ppu_fiber_finish(PpuFiberSlot* f)
{
    if (!f->exit_status_set) {
        f->exit_status = 0;
        f->exit_status_set = 1;
    }
    if (f->on_exit_opd && !f->exit_callback_called) {
        f->exit_callback_called = 1;
        (void)ppu_guest_call(f->on_exit_opd, f->on_exit_arg,
                             (u64)(s64)f->exit_status, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    }
    f->state = 3;
    s_ppu_running_slot = -1;
    s_ppu_running_scheduler = 0;
#ifdef _WIN32
    SwitchToFiber(s_ppu_scheduler_host);
#else
    setcontext(&s_ppu_scheduler_host);
#endif
}

#ifdef _WIN32
static VOID CALLBACK ppu_fiber_trampoline(LPVOID param)
{
    PpuFiberSlot* f = (PpuFiberSlot*)param;
    int slot = (int)(f - s_ppu_fibers);
    s_ppu_running_slot = slot;
    s_ppu_running_scheduler = f->scheduler_ea;
    /* Reserve the PPC64 caller frame below the end of the allocation.
     * A callee saves LR at entry SP + 0x10; using the allocation end as SP
     * would overwrite the next heap chunk's free-list links. */
    u32 guest_sp = ((f->guest_stack_ea + f->guest_stack_size) & ~15u) - 0x70u;
    vm_write64(guest_sp, 0); /* terminate the guest stack backchain */
    u64 result = ppu_guest_call_on_stack(
        f->entry_opd, guest_sp, f->arg, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    f->exit_status = (s32)(u32)result;
    f->exit_status_set = 1;
    ppu_fiber_finish(f);
}
#else
static void ppu_fiber_trampoline(int slot)
{
    PpuFiberSlot* f = &s_ppu_fibers[(u32)slot];
    s_ppu_running_slot = slot;
    s_ppu_running_scheduler = f->scheduler_ea;
    u32 guest_sp = ((f->guest_stack_ea + f->guest_stack_size) & ~15u) - 0x70u;
    vm_write64(guest_sp, 0);
    u64 result = ppu_guest_call_on_stack(
        f->entry_opd, guest_sp, f->arg, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    f->exit_status = (s32)(u32)result;
    f->exit_status_set = 1;
    ppu_fiber_finish(f);
}
#endif

static void ppu_fiber_switch_to_host(PpuFiberSlot* f)
{
    ppu_context* scheduler_ctx = g_active_ctx;
    int slot = (int)(f - s_ppu_fibers);
    f->state = 1;
    s_ppu_running_slot = slot;
    s_ppu_running_scheduler = f->scheduler_ea;
#ifdef _WIN32
    SwitchToFiber(f->native_fiber);
#else
    swapcontext(&s_ppu_scheduler_host, &f->context);
#endif
    g_active_ctx = scheduler_ctx;
    s_ppu_running_slot = -1;
    s_ppu_running_scheduler = 0;
}

static void ppu_fiber_suspend_to_host(PpuFiberSlot* f)
{
    /* Native fibers share thread-local storage. Restore this fiber's guest
     * context on resume so reservation checks use its own lwarx state. */
    ppu_context* fiber_ctx = g_active_ctx;
#ifdef _WIN32
    SwitchToFiber(s_ppu_scheduler_host);
#else
    swapcontext(&f->context, &s_ppu_scheduler_host);
#endif
    g_active_ctx = fiber_ctx;
}

static int ppu_scheduler_pick(PpuSchedulerSlot* scheduler, u32 epoch)
{
    int best = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS; i++) {
        PpuFiberSlot* f = &s_ppu_fibers[i];
        if (!f->in_use || f->scheduler_ea != scheduler->scheduler_ea ||
            f->state != 0 || (f->run_epoch == epoch && !f->force_resume))
            continue;
        if (best < 0 || f->priority < s_ppu_fibers[best].priority)
            best = i;
    }
    return best;
}

static void ppu_scheduler_wake_joiners(u32 scheduler_ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS; i++) {
        PpuFiberSlot* f = &s_ppu_fibers[i];
        if (!f->in_use || f->scheduler_ea != scheduler_ea || f->state != 2)
            continue;
        if (f->wait_target >= 0 && f->wait_target < CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS &&
            s_ppu_fibers[f->wait_target].in_use &&
            s_ppu_fibers[f->wait_target].state == 3) {
            f->state = 0;
            f->force_resume = 1;
        }
    }
}

/* Give each runnable fiber one turn per epoch. Yielded fibers run again after
 * the other ready fibers have had a turn; a JoinFiber waiter resumes after its
 * target completes. */
static int ppu_scheduler_run_pass(PpuSchedulerSlot* scheduler)
{
    if (!scheduler) return 0;
    int ran = 0;
    u32 epoch = ++scheduler->epoch;
    if (!epoch) epoch = ++scheduler->epoch;
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!s_ppu_scheduler_host) {
        s_ppu_scheduler_host = ConvertThreadToFiber(NULL);
        if (!s_ppu_scheduler_host && GetLastError() == ERROR_ALREADY_FIBER)
            s_ppu_scheduler_host = GetCurrentFiber();
    }
    if (!s_ppu_scheduler_host) return 0;
#else
    getcontext(&s_ppu_scheduler_host);
#endif
    for (;;) {
        ppu_scheduler_wake_joiners(scheduler->scheduler_ea);
        int slot = ppu_scheduler_pick(scheduler, epoch);
        if (slot < 0) {
            int more_ready = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < CELL_FIBER_MAX_FIBERS; i++) {
                PpuFiberSlot* f = &s_ppu_fibers[i];
                if (f->in_use && f->scheduler_ea == scheduler->scheduler_ea &&
                    f->state == 0) {
                    more_ready = 1;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!more_ready) break;
            epoch = ++scheduler->epoch;
            if (!epoch) epoch = ++scheduler->epoch;
            continue;
        }
        PpuFiberSlot* f = &s_ppu_fibers[slot];
        f->run_epoch = epoch;
        f->force_resume = 0;
        ppu_fiber_switch_to_host(f);
        ran++;
    }
    return ran;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * State
 *
 * One lock covers all of it, and one condition variable wakes everyone who waits on it: a RunFibers loop with nothing
 * to run (its fibers wait for a signal another thread sends), and JoinFiber callers outside any fiber. Guest
 * addresses name fibers and schedulers, never host pointers, so a waiter that wakes after FinalizeScheduler finds the
 * object gone instead of freed memory.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

enum { F_READY, F_RUNNING, F_WAIT_SIGNAL, F_WAIT_JOIN, F_DONE };

typedef struct Sched Sched;
typedef struct Fiber Fiber;

struct Fiber {
    Fiber*  next;                /* every fiber of every scheduler */
    Sched*  sched;
    u32     ea;                  /* the guest CellFiberPpu */
    u32     opd;
    u32     priority;
    u32     stack_ea;
    u32     stack_size;
    u64     arg;
    u64     seq;                 /* position in the run queue: creation order, then the last yield */
    int     state;
    int     signal_pending;      /* a SendSignal arrived before the WaitSignal */
    u32     join_ea;             /* F_WAIT_JOIN: the fiber waited for */
    s32     status;
#ifdef _WIN32
    void*   host_fiber;
#else
    ucontext_t uc;
    void*   host_stack;
#endif
    ppu_context ctx;
};

struct Sched {
    Sched*  next;
    u32     ea;                  /* the guest CellFiberPpuScheduler */
    int     running;             /* a thread is inside RunFibers */
#ifdef _WIN32
    void*   back;                /* RunFibers' fiber while it runs one */
#else
    ucontext_t back;             /* RunFibers' context while it runs one */
#endif
};

static Sched* s_scheds;
static Fiber* s_fibers;
static u64    s_seq;

/* Lifecycle events only: no logging or environment lookup on fiber switches.
 * Call with s_lock held, including the one-time environment lookup. */
static int fiber_lifecycle_trace(void)
{
    static int enabled = -1;
    if (enabled < 0) {
        const char* value = getenv("PPU_FIBER_TRACE");
        enabled = value && *value && strcmp(value, "0") != 0;
    }
    return enabled;
}

/* The fiber running on this host thread, if any. */
static PPU_THREAD_LOCAL Fiber* t_cur;

#ifdef _WIN32
static SRWLOCK            s_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static CONDITION_VARIABLE s_cv   = CONDITION_VARIABLE_INIT;
#  define LOCK()    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_lock)
#  define UNLOCK()  ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_lock)
#  define WAIT()    SleepConditionVariableSRW(&s_cv, &s_lock, INFINITE, 0)
#  define WAKE()    WakeAllConditionVariable(&s_cv)
#else
static pthread_mutex_t s_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t  s_cv   = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;
#  define LOCK()    pthread_mutex_lock(&s_lock)
#  define UNLOCK()  pthread_mutex_unlock(&s_lock)
#  define WAIT()    pthread_cond_wait(&s_cv, &s_lock)
#  define WAKE()    pthread_cond_broadcast(&s_cv)
#endif

/* Lookups; the lock is held. */
static Sched* find_sched(u32 ea)
{
    for (Sched* s = s_scheds; s; s = s->next)
        if (s->ea == ea) return s;
    return NULL;
}

static Fiber* find_fiber(u32 ea)
{
    for (Fiber* f = s_fibers; f; f = f->next)
        if (f->ea == ea) return f;
    return NULL;
}

/* The READY fiber of the scheduler with the lowest priority number; creation (or last yield) order among equals. */
static Fiber* pick_runnable(const Sched* s)
{
    Fiber* best = NULL;
    for (Fiber* f = s_fibers; f; f = f->next) {
        if (f->sched != s || f->state != F_READY) continue;
        if (!best || f->priority < best->priority ||
            (f->priority == best->priority && f->seq < best->seq))
            best = f;
    }
    return best;
}

/* Every fiber of the scheduler has ended (or it has none). */
static int all_done(const Sched* s)
{
    for (const Fiber* f = s_fibers; f; f = f->next)
        if (f->sched == s && f->state != F_DONE) return 0;
    return 1;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Host context switching: ucontext on POSIX, fibers on Windows. RunFibers' own context is the "back" one every fiber
 * returns to when it blocks, yields or ends.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

static void fiber_body(Fiber* f);

#ifdef _WIN32
static VOID CALLBACK fiber_entry(void* p)
{
    fiber_body((Fiber*)p);
}

static int host_create(Fiber* f)
{
    f->host_fiber = CreateFiberEx(0, FIBER_HOST_STACK, 0, fiber_entry, f);
    return f->host_fiber != NULL;
}

/* Releases the host stack. The fiber must not be the one running, nor be resumed again. */
static void host_destroy(Fiber* f)
{
    if (f->host_fiber) DeleteFiber(f->host_fiber);
    f->host_fiber = NULL;
}

/* RunFibers -> fiber. The calling thread becomes a fiber itself on first use. */
static void host_resume(Sched* s, Fiber* f)
{
    if (!IsThreadAFiber()) ConvertThreadToFiber(NULL);
    s->back = GetCurrentFiber();
    SwitchToFiber(f->host_fiber);
}

static void host_yield(Fiber* f)
{
    SwitchToFiber(f->sched->back);
}
#else
static void fiber_entry(unsigned hi, unsigned lo)
{
    fiber_body((Fiber*)(((uintptr_t)hi << 32) | lo));
}

static int host_create(Fiber* f)
{
    f->host_stack = malloc(FIBER_HOST_STACK);
    if (!f->host_stack) return 0;
    getcontext(&f->uc);
    f->uc.uc_stack.ss_sp   = f->host_stack;
    f->uc.uc_stack.ss_size = FIBER_HOST_STACK;
    f->uc.uc_link          = NULL;
    uintptr_t p = (uintptr_t)f;
    makecontext(&f->uc, (void (*)(void))fiber_entry, 2, (unsigned)(p >> 32), (unsigned)(p & 0xFFFFFFFFu));
    return 1;
}

/* Releases the host stack. The fiber must not be the one running, nor be resumed again. */
static void host_destroy(Fiber* f)
{
    free(f->host_stack);
    f->host_stack = NULL;
}

static void host_resume(Sched* s, Fiber* f)
{
    swapcontext(&s->back, &f->uc);
}

static void host_yield(Fiber* f)
{
    swapcontext(&f->uc, &f->sched->back);
}
#endif

/* The fiber has ended with `status`: record it and make the fibers that joined it runnable. The lock is held. */
static void fiber_finish_locked(Fiber* f, s32 status)
{
    f->status = status;
    f->state  = F_DONE;
    if (fiber_lifecycle_trace())
        fprintf(stderr, "[fiber-life] finish ea=%08X entry=%08X status=%08X\n",
                f->ea, f->opd, (u32)status);
    for (Fiber* g = s_fibers; g; g = g->next)
        if (g->state == F_WAIT_JOIN && g->join_ea == f->ea) g->state = F_READY;
}

/* Leaves the fiber for good, back into RunFibers. */
static void fiber_leave(Fiber* f)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    SwitchToFiber(f->sched->back);
#else
    setcontext(&f->sched->back);
#endif
    abort();                     /* an ended fiber is never resumed */
}

/* The fiber's first and last frame, on its own host stack. */
static void fiber_body(Fiber* f)
{
    f->ctx.gpr[1] = (f->stack_ea + f->stack_size - FIBER_STACK_TOP_PAD) & ~0xFull;
    f->ctx.gpr[3] = f->arg;
    f->ctx.cia    = f->opd;
    if (g_ppu_thread_entry_trampoline)
        g_ppu_thread_entry_trampoline(&f->ctx);   /* runs the entry to completion; its r3 is the status */

    LOCK();
    fiber_finish_locked(f, (s32)f->ctx.gpr[3]);
    UNLOCK();
    WAKE();
    fiber_leave(f);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Initialisation
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

s32 _cellFiberPpuInitialize(void)
{
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 _cellFiberPpuSchedulerAttributeInitialize(CellFiberPpuSchedulerAttribute* attr, u32 sdkVersion)
{
    (void)sdkVersion;
    if (!attr) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;
    vm_memset((u32)(uintptr_t)attr, 0, CELL_FIBER_PPU_SCHEDULER_ATTRIBUTE_SIZE);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 _cellFiberPpuAttributeInitialize(CellFiberPpuAttribute* attr, u32 sdkVersion)
{
    (void)sdkVersion;
    if (!attr) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;
    vm_memset((u32)(uintptr_t)attr, 0, CELL_FIBER_PPU_ATTRIBUTE_SIZE);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler(CellFiberPpuScheduler* scheduler, const CellFiberPpuSchedulerAttribute* attr)
{
    (void)attr;
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)scheduler;
    if (!ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;
    if (ea % CELL_FIBER_PPU_SCHEDULER_ALIGN) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_ALIGN;

    LOCK();
    s32 rc = CELL_OK;
    if (find_sched(ea)) {
        rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT;
    } else {
        Sched* s = (Sched*)calloc(1, sizeof *s);
        if (!s) {
            rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NOMEM;
        } else {
            s->ea   = ea;
            s->next = s_scheds;
            s_scheds = s;
        }
    }
    UNLOCK();
    return rc;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuFinalizeScheduler(CellFiberPpuScheduler* scheduler)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)scheduler;
    if (!ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;

    LOCK();
    Sched* s = find_sched(ea);
    s32 rc = CELL_OK;
    if (!s) {
        rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL;
    } else if (s->running) {
        rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT;
    } else {
        /* Fibers that never ran to their end are dropped with their host stacks. Nothing resumes them: RunFibers is
         * not running, and a JoinFiber waiting for one finds it gone and fails with INVAL. */
        for (Fiber** pf = &s_fibers; *pf;) {
            Fiber* f = *pf;
            if (f->sched == s) {
                *pf = f->next;
                host_destroy(f);
                free(f);
            } else {
                pf = &f->next;
            }
        }
        for (Sched** ps = &s_scheds; *ps; ps = &(*ps)->next) {
            if (*ps == s) { *ps = s->next; break; }
        }
        free(s);
    }
    UNLOCK();
    WAKE();
    return rc;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(CellFiberPpuScheduler* scheduler, CellFiberPpu* fiber, u32 entry, u64 arg,
                            u32 priority, void* eaStack, u32 sizeStack, const CellFiberPpuAttribute* attr)
{
    (void)attr;
    const u32 sched_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)scheduler;
    const u32 fiber_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)fiber;
    const u32 stack_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)eaStack;
    if (!sched_ea || !fiber_ea || !entry || !stack_ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;
    if (fiber_ea % CELL_FIBER_PPU_ALIGN) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_ALIGN;
    if (sizeStack < FIBER_MIN_STACK) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL;

    Fiber* f = (Fiber*)calloc(1, sizeof *f);
    if (!f) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NOMEM;
    f->ea         = fiber_ea;
    f->opd        = entry;
    f->arg        = arg;
    f->priority   = priority;
    f->stack_ea   = stack_ea;
    f->stack_size = sizeStack;
    f->state      = F_READY;

    /* r13 stays the creator's, so the fiber's TLS is the creating thread's (0 lets the trampoline pick a block). */
    const ppu_context* parent = g_active_ctx;
    f->ctx.gpr[13]   = parent ? parent->gpr[13] : 0;
    f->ctx.thread_id = parent ? parent->thread_id : FIBER_FALLBACK_THREAD_ID;

    if (!host_create(f)) {
        free(f);
        return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NOMEM;
    }

    LOCK();
    Sched* s = find_sched(sched_ea);
    s32 rc = CELL_OK;
    if (!s) {
        rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL;
    } else if (find_fiber(fiber_ea)) {
        Fiber* previous = find_fiber(fiber_ea);
        fprintf(stderr, "[fiber-life] create rejected ea=%08X entry=%08X "
                "previous_state=%d previous_entry=%08X previous_status=%08X\n",
                fiber_ea, entry, previous->state, previous->opd, (u32)previous->status);
        rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT;
    } else {
        f->sched = s;
        f->seq   = s_seq++;
        f->next  = s_fibers;
        s_fibers = f;
        if (fiber_lifecycle_trace())
            fprintf(stderr, "[fiber-life] create ea=%08X entry=%08X arg=%llX "
                    "stack=%08X+%X scheduler=%08X\n", fiber_ea, entry,
                    (unsigned long long)arg, stack_ea, sizeStack, sched_ea);
    }
    UNLOCK();
    if (rc != CELL_OK) {
        host_destroy(f);
        free(f);
        return rc;
    }
    WAKE();
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Running
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

s32 cellFiberPpuRunFibers(CellFiberPpuScheduler* scheduler)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)scheduler;
    if (!ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;

    LOCK();
    Sched* s = find_sched(ea);
    if (!s) { UNLOCK(); return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL; }
    if (s->running || t_cur) { UNLOCK(); return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT; }
    s->running = 1;

    for (;;) {
        Fiber* f = pick_runnable(s);
        if (!f) {
            if (all_done(s)) break;
            WAIT();              /* its fibers wait for a signal, or a join, that another thread delivers */
            continue;
        }
        f->state = F_RUNNING;
        UNLOCK();

        ppu_context* saved_active = g_active_ctx;
        t_cur        = f;
        g_active_ctx = &f->ctx;
        host_resume(s, f);       /* back here when f blocks, yields or ends */
        g_active_ctx = saved_active;
        t_cur        = NULL;

        LOCK();
        if (f->state == F_DONE)
            host_destroy(f);     /* off its stack now; the Fiber stays for JoinFiber's status */
    }
    s->running = 0;
    UNLOCK();
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuWaitSignal(void)
{
    Fiber* f = t_cur;
    if (!f) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_PERM;

    LOCK();
    if (f->signal_pending) {
        f->signal_pending = 0;
        UNLOCK();
        return CELL_OK;
    }
    f->state = F_WAIT_SIGNAL;
    UNLOCK();
    host_yield(f);               /* RunFibers runs the others until SendSignal makes this one ready */
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuSendSignal(CellFiberPpu* fiber, u32* numWorker)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)fiber;
    if (!ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;

    LOCK();
    Fiber* f = find_fiber(ea);
    if (!f) { UNLOCK(); return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL; }
    if (f->state == F_WAIT_SIGNAL)  f->state = F_READY;
    else if (f->state != F_DONE)    f->signal_pending = 1;
    UNLOCK();
    WAKE();
    if (numWorker) vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)numWorker, 0);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuYield(void)
{
    Fiber* f = t_cur;
    if (!f) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_PERM;

    LOCK();
    f->state = F_READY;
    f->seq   = s_seq++;          /* behind the other fibers of its priority */
    UNLOCK();
    host_yield(f);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellFiberPpuExit(s32 status)
{
    Fiber* f = t_cur;
    if (!f) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_PERM;

    LOCK();
    fiber_finish_locked(f, status);
    UNLOCK();
    WAKE();
    fiber_leave(f);
    return CELL_OK;              /* not reached */
}

CellFiberPpu* cellFiberPpuSelf(void)
{
    const Fiber* f = t_cur;
    return (CellFiberPpu*)(uintptr_t)(f ? f->ea : 0);
}

/* Waits for the fiber to end and returns its exit status. Called from a fiber it hands control back to RunFibers
 * meanwhile (blocking the host thread would stop the scheduler that has to run the fiber waited for); from any other
 * thread it blocks. */
s32 cellFiberPpuJoinFiber(CellFiberPpu* fiber, s32* status)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)fiber;
    if (!ea) return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;

    Fiber* self = t_cur;
    LOCK();
    Fiber* f = find_fiber(ea);
    if (!f || f == self) { UNLOCK(); return (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL; }
    if (self && f->state != F_DONE) {
        self->state   = F_WAIT_JOIN;
        self->join_ea = ea;
        UNLOCK();
        host_yield(self);        /* ready again once the fiber has ended */
        LOCK();
        self->join_ea = 0;
    }
    while ((f = find_fiber(ea)) != NULL && f->state != F_DONE)
        WAIT();
    s32 rc = CELL_OK;
    if (!f) rc = (s32)CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL;      /* the scheduler was finalized under the join */
    else if (status) vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)status, (u32)f->status);
    if (fiber_lifecycle_trace())
        fprintf(stderr, "[fiber-life] join ea=%08X rc=%08X state=%d\n",
                ea, (u32)rc, f ? f->state : -1);
    UNLOCK();
    return rc;
}


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellFiber.h =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellFiber HLE
 *
 * The SDK's PPU fibers: cooperative user-level threads that a scheduler runs on
 * one PPU thread. A scheduler (cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler) owns a set of
 * fibers (cellFiberPpuCreateFiber), cellFiberPpuRunFibers runs them until every
 * one has ended, and fibers block on each other with WaitSignal / SendSignal /
 * JoinFiber. Each fiber has its own guest stack (the caller's eaStack) and its
 * own host stack: ucontext on POSIX, Windows fibers on Windows.
 *
 * Every pointer argument is a guest address, like in the other HLE libraries; the
 * structs are opaque to the host and only have the SDK's size and alignment.
 */

#define PS3RECOMP_CELL_FIBER_H

#include "ps3emu/error_codes.h"

extern "C" {
#endif

 * Error codes (the SDK's, module 0x8076)
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_INVAL             0x80760002
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NOMEM             0x80760004
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_DEADLK            0x80760008
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_PERM              0x80760009
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_BUSY              0x8076000A
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_ABORT             0x8076000C
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT              0x8076000F
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_ALIGN             0x80760010
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NULL_POINTER      0x80760011
#define CELL_FIBER_ERROR_NOSYSINIT         0x80760020

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Guest structures: size and alignment as the SDK lays them out
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_SCHEDULER_ATTRIBUTE_SIZE   256
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_ATTRIBUTE_SIZE             256
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_SCHEDULER_SIZE             512
#define CELL_FIBER_PPU_SIZE                       896

===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellSpurs.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellSpurs HLE implementation
 *
 * Provides the SPURS management API so games can call SPU task/workload
 * functions without crashing.  Full SPU execution requires recompiling
 * SPU programs; this layer provides the scheduling and management APIs.
 *
 * Tasks and workloads are tracked.  If a game provides PPU fallback
 * callbacks, those can be invoked through the task submission path.
 */

#include "cellSpurs.h"
#include "../../runtime/platform/win32_compat.h"
#include "../../runtime/ps3_log.h"
#include "spu_workload.h"   /* SPU image -> lifted-entry dispatch (runtime/spu) */
#include "spurs_taskset.h"  /* REAL BE CellSpursTaskset layout builders (fork Option-B) */
#include "../../runtime/ppu/ppu_memory.h"   /* vm_base (guest mem) */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>   /* getenv -- an implicit decl returns int, truncating the pointer */
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include "ps3emu/log_first.h"

/* Bridge the real (BE) taskset EA + selected taskId from CreateTask to the image-22
 * SPU dispatch (spu_workload.c), so spurs_pm_build_context can build the leaf's
 * SpursTasksetContext from the real taskset. Set right before dispatch_async (the PPU
 * create path is sequential here). Gated by YDKJ_REAL_TASKSET in the dispatch. */
uint32_t g_ydkj_real_taskset_ea = 0;
uint32_t g_ydkj_real_taskid     = 0;
uint32_t g_ydkj_real_spurs_ea   = 0;   /* real CellSpurs instance EA (for the taskset-policy handoff) */

/* Generic HLE adapter passes GUEST addresses; translate pointer args. CellSpurs
 * is treated opaquely by the game (passed back as a handle), so translating the
 * pointer is enough here. */
#define GUEST_PTR(p, T) ((T)((p) ? (void*)(vm_base + (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)(p)) : (void*)0))

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <pthread.h>
#include <time.h>
#endif

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Internal workload tracking
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

typedef struct {
    int         in_use;
    const void* pm;            /* policy-module image EA (guest) */
    u32         sizePm;
    u64         data;          /* workload data (e.g. joblist EA) */
    u32         spurs_ea;      /* owning CellSpurs instance EA */
    u8          priority[CELL_SPURS_MAX_SPU];
    u32         minContention;
    u32         maxContention;
    u32         readyCount;
    int         started;       /* its SPU program has been dispatched        */
} SpursWorkload;

typedef struct {
    int         in_use;
    u32         id;
    int         active;
    int         completed;
    s32         exitCode;
    void*       entryPoint;
    u64         argA;
} SpursTask;

/* Global workload table (per-SPURS instance in a real system, simplified) */
static SpursWorkload s_workloads[CELL_SPURS_MAX_WORKLOAD];
static SpursTask     s_tasks[CELL_SPURS_MAX_TASK];
static u32           s_next_task_id = 0;

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Event flag sync side table
 *
 * The CellSpursEventFlag itself is 128 bytes of GAME-owned guest memory in
 * the REAL big-endian kernel layout (see EF_* offsets below) — the SPU side
 * (lifted task-library code) reads/writes it with DMA + atomics, so the PPU
 * HLE must operate on the same guest bytes, never a host struct. This side
 * table (keyed by guest EA) only adds the host mutex + condvar used to block
 * and wake PPU waiters.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
#define MAX_EVENT_FLAGS 64

typedef struct {
    uint32_t            ea;      /* guest EA of the 128-byte flag */
#ifdef _WIN32
    CRITICAL_SECTION    cs;
    CONDITION_VARIABLE  cv;
#else
    pthread_mutex_t     mtx;
    pthread_cond_t      cond;
#endif
    int                 initialized;
} EventFlagSync;

static EventFlagSync s_ef_sync[MAX_EVENT_FLAGS];

/* PPU threads inside cellSpursEventFlagWait. The SPU sets a flag with
 * GETLLAR/PUTLLC on the guest struct, which never touched the waiter's
 * condition variable, so every wait ran out its 2 ms poll: FMOD's mixer waits
 * on its SPU task once or twice per 5.3 ms audio block, fell behind, and
 * GH3's songs played ~60% silence (heard as static). */
static volatile long s_ef_ppu_waiters;
static void ef_line_committed(uint32_t line)
{
    if (!s_ef_ppu_waiters) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_EVENT_FLAGS; i++) {
        EventFlagSync* s = &s_ef_sync[i];
        if (!s->initialized || (s->ea & ~127u) != line) continue;
        /* Take the waiter's lock so the wake cannot fall between its check of
         * the flag and its sleep. Caller holds no lock-line lock. */
#ifdef _WIN32
        EnterCriticalSection(&s->cs); WakeAllConditionVariable(&s->cv); LeaveCriticalSection(&s->cs);
#else
        pthread_mutex_lock(&s->mtx); pthread_cond_broadcast(&s->cond); pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->mtx);
#endif
    }
}

static EventFlagSync* ef_sync_find(uint32_t ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_EVENT_FLAGS; i++) {
        if (s_ef_sync[i].initialized && s_ef_sync[i].ea == ea)
            return &s_ef_sync[i];
    }
    return NULL;
}

static EventFlagSync* ef_sync_alloc(uint32_t ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_EVENT_FLAGS; i++) {
        if (!s_ef_sync[i].initialized) {
            s_ef_sync[i].ea = ea;
            { extern void (*g_spu_line_commit_hook)(uint32_t);
              g_spu_line_commit_hook = ef_line_committed; }
#ifdef _WIN32
            InitializeCriticalSection(&s_ef_sync[i].cs);
            InitializeConditionVariable(&s_ef_sync[i].cv);
#else
            pthread_mutex_init(&s_ef_sync[i].mtx, NULL);
            pthread_cond_init(&s_ef_sync[i].cond, NULL);
#endif
            s_ef_sync[i].initialized = 1;
            return &s_ef_sync[i];
        }
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* Lenient lookup: a flag touched before we saw its Initialize (alternate init
 * paths, e.g. taskset2) still gets a sync slot instead of an error. */
static EventFlagSync* ef_sync_get(uint32_t ea)
{
    EventFlagSync* s = ef_sync_find(ea);
    if (!s) {
        s = ef_sync_alloc(ea);
        if (s)
            fprintf(stderr, "[cellSpurs] event flag 0x%08X used before Initialize "
                            "-- sync slot auto-allocated\n", ea);
    }
    return s;
}

static void ef_sync_free(EventFlagSync* sync)
{
    if (!sync) return;
#ifdef _WIN32
    DeleteCriticalSection(&sync->cs);
    /* CONDITION_VARIABLE has no destroy on Windows */
#else
    pthread_mutex_destroy(&sync->mtx);
    pthread_cond_destroy(&sync->cond);
#endif
    sync->ea = 0;
    sync->initialized = 0;
}

static inline void ef_lock(EventFlagSync* s)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    EnterCriticalSection(&s->cs);
#else
    pthread_mutex_lock(&s->mtx);
#endif
}

static inline void ef_unlock(EventFlagSync* s)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    LeaveCriticalSection(&s->cs);
#else
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->mtx);
#endif
}

/* Returns 1 if signaled, 0 if it timed out after `ms`. */
static inline int ef_wait_timed(EventFlagSync* s, unsigned ms)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    return SleepConditionVariableCS(&s->cv, &s->cs, ms) ? 1 : 0;
#else
    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);
    ts.tv_sec += ms / 1000; ts.tv_nsec += (long)(ms % 1000) * 1000000L;
    if (ts.tv_nsec >= 1000000000L) { ts.tv_sec++; ts.tv_nsec -= 1000000000L; }
    return pthread_cond_timedwait(&s->cond, &s->mtx, &ts) == 0 ? 1 : 0;
#endif
}

static inline void ef_broadcast(EventFlagSync* s)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    WakeAllConditionVariable(&s->cv);
#else
    pthread_cond_broadcast(&s->cond);
#endif
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * REAL CellSpursEventFlag guest layout (128 bytes, big-endian; RPCS3
 * cellSpurs.h is the reference). The SPU task library manipulates this exact
 * layout with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, so every PPU-side access goes through vm_*.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
#define EF_EVENTS            0x00u  /* be u16: the event bits */
#define EF_SPU_PENDING_RECV  0x02u  /* be u16: slot bits with met conditions */
#define EF_PPU_WAIT_MASK     0x04u  /* be u16: blocked PPU thread's mask */
#define EF_PPU_WAIT_SLOTMODE 0x06u  /* u8: hi4 = wait slot, lo4 = wait mode */
#define EF_PPU_PENDING_RECV  0x07u  /* u8: 1 when the PPU waiter's cond met */
#define EF_SPU_USED_SLOTS    0x08u  /* be u16: wait slots in use (bit 0x8000>>s) */
#define EF_SPU_WAIT_MODE     0x0Au  /* be u16: per-slot mode (1 = AND) */
#define EF_SPU_PORT          0x0Cu  /* u8 */
#define EF_IS_IWL            0x0Du  /* u8: addr is a wkl instead of taskset */
#define EF_DIRECTION         0x0Eu  /* u8: CELL_SPURS_EVENT_FLAG_* direction */
#define EF_CLEAR_MODE        0x0Fu  /* u8: 0 = AUTO, 1 = MANUAL */
#define EF_SPU_WAIT_MASK_ARR 0x10u  /* be u16 [16]: per-slot wait masks */
#define EF_PENDING_RECV_EVT  0x30u  /* be u16 [16]: events handed to waiters */
#define EF_WAITING_TASK_ID   0x50u  /* u8 [16]: waiting task ids */
#define EF_WAITING_WKL_ID    0x60u  /* u8 [16]: waiting workload ids */
#define EF_ADDR              0x70u  /* be u64: taskset EA (isIwl=0) */
#define EF_EVENT_PORT_ID     0x78u  /* be u32 */
#define EF_EVENT_QUEUE_ID    0x7Cu  /* be u32 */
#define EF_GUEST_SIZE        0x80u

/* Layer-2 hook: wake an SPU task that registered a wait slot and slept via
 * the taskset syscall. Implemented in runtime/spu (task park/wake); the
 * event-flag core only reports WHO must wake. */
extern void spu_taskset_signal_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);

/* RPCS3_REFERENCE_REVIEWED: this locally expressed event-flag protocol follows
 * documented RPCS3/kernel behavior; targeted review did not establish a
 * copied function body.
 * This is provenance context, not license clearance. See
 * docs/RPCS3_LICENSE_AUDIT.md.
 * Core Set protocol on the guest struct (sync lock held). Mirrors the real
 * kernel/RPCS3 semantics: satisfy registered SPU-task wait slots (slot s uses
 * bit 0x8000>>s in the used/pending/mode words), hand each its received
 * events, auto-clear consumed bits, then signal the tasks. PPU waiters are
 * poll-based here (ef_wait_timed ticks re-check EF_EVENTS), so no PPU
 * wait-slot registration is needed — and deliberately NOT written, so the
 * SPU-side lifted Set code takes its "no PPU waiter" path and simply ORs
 * bits that our poll then observes. */
/* The flag struct is ONE 128-byte line the SPU task library updates with
 * GETLLAR/PUTLLC. A PPU read-modify-write of it must hold the lock-line lock
 * for its whole span, or a PUTLLC landing between the read and the write is
 * silently undone: an SPU wait registered there is lost, nothing ever signals
 * the task, and its PPU partner blocks for good (GH3: FMOD's mixer deadlocked
 * at boot in 1 run of ~4). Raw accesses inside: vm_write16 would take the
 * same (non-recursive) lock. The end notifies reserving SPUs, under the lock
 * as spu_coh_notify_write expects. */
extern void spu_lockline_lock(void);
extern void spu_lockline_unlock(void);
extern int  spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t);
extern void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t);
static inline u16 ef_r16(uint32_t a) { const uint8_t* p = vm_base + a; return (u16)((p[0] << 8) | p[1]); }
static inline void ef_w16(uint32_t a, u16 v) { uint8_t* p = vm_base + a; p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[1] = (uint8_t)v; }
static inline void ef_line_end(uint32_t ea)
{
    if (spu_coh_is_reserved(ea & ~127u)) spu_coh_notify_write(ea & ~127u);
    spu_lockline_unlock();
}

static void spurs_ef_set_locked(uint32_t ea, u16 bits)
{
    spu_lockline_lock();
    u16 events        = ef_r16(ea + EF_EVENTS);
    u16 used          = (u16)(ef_r16(ea + EF_SPU_USED_SLOTS) &
                              ~ef_r16(ea + EF_SPU_PENDING_RECV));
    u16 waitmode      = ef_r16(ea + EF_SPU_WAIT_MODE);
    u16 eventsToClear = 0;
    u16 pendingRecv   = 0;

    for (int s = 0; s < CELL_SPURS_EVENT_FLAG_MAX_WAIT_SLOTS; s++) {
        u16 bit = (u16)(0x8000u >> s);
        if (!(used & bit)) continue;
        u16 mask = ef_r16(ea + EF_SPU_WAIT_MASK_ARR + 2u * s);
        u16 rel  = (u16)((events | bits) & mask);
        int mode_and = (waitmode & bit) != 0;
        if ((mask & ~rel) == 0 || (!mode_and && rel != 0)) {
            eventsToClear |= rel;
            pendingRecv   |= bit;
            ef_w16(ea + EF_PENDING_RECV_EVT + 2u * s, rel);
        }
    }

    events = (u16)(events | bits);
    if (pendingRecv) {
        ef_w16(ea + EF_SPU_PENDING_RECV,
               (u16)(ef_r16(ea + EF_SPU_PENDING_RECV) | pendingRecv));
        if (vm_read8(ea + EF_CLEAR_MODE) == CELL_SPURS_EVENT_FLAG_CLEAR_AUTO)
            events = (u16)(events & ~eventsToClear);
    }
    ef_w16(ea + EF_EVENTS, events);
    ef_line_end(ea);   /* before signalling: signal_task takes its own locks */

    for (int s = 0; s < CELL_SPURS_EVENT_FLAG_MAX_WAIT_SLOTS; s++) {
        if (pendingRecv & (0x8000u >> s)) {
            uint32_t taskset_ea = (uint32_t)vm_read64(ea + EF_ADDR);
            u32 taskId = vm_read8(ea + EF_WAITING_TASK_ID + s);
            if (ps3_log_verbose())
                fprintf(stderr, "[cellSpurs] EventFlagSet 0x%08X satisfies SPU task "
                        "slot %d (taskset=0x%08X task=%u)\n", ea, s, taskset_ea, taskId);
            spu_taskset_signal_task(taskset_ea, taskId);
        }
    }

    /* SPURS_EF_WAKE_PARKED: a task that parked in WAIT_SIGNAL WITHOUT registering
     * a wait slot in this flag is unreachable by the loop above, which only
     * signals slots present in `used`. YDKJ CRI tasks do exactly that, so a
     * PPU->SPU Set (direction 2) delivered nothing and they slept forever. Same
     * failure class canersaka documented for SPURS queues in Yakuza Dead Souls:
     * the HLE woke only its host condvar, which lifted SPU tasks never wait on.
     * Signalling a task that was not waiting on THIS flag is safe -- signals are
     * latched in guest state and every wait loop re-checks its own predicate. */
    /* Record the bits this Set owes the task waiting on (flag - 0x80),
     * unconditionally. Gating this on EF_DIRECTION made delivery depend on
     * Initialize having already run, and the CRI flags are Set before that --
     * so the post silently never happened. An unclaimed post is harmless: it is
     * only ever consumed by a task that names this exact object in its wait. */
    if (ea > 0x80u) {
        uint32_t obj = ea - 0x80u;
