===== FILE: \libs\spurs\cellSpursJq.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellSpursJq HLE implementation
 *
 * SPURS Job Queue — manages job submission and tracking.
 * Bounded asynchronous worker pool for lifted SPU job descriptors.
 * A single worker is the conservative default; concurrent lanes require
 * explicit opt-in until other SPU runtime global state is audited.
 */

#include "cellSpursJq.h"
#include "../../runtime/ppu/ppu_memory.h"   /* GUEST_PTR, vm_write*: guest EA -> host pointer */
#include "../../runtime/spu/spu_workload.h"
#include "../system/sysPrxForUser.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
# include <windows.h>
#else
# include <pthread.h>
#endif

/* All queue, port, job-id, and pending-job state is protected by the pool
 * mutex, including in synchronous-compatibility mode. Never hold it while
 * calling lifted SPU code or guest memory callbacks. */
#define JQ_WORKER_MAX 6
#define CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS 64

typedef struct JqTask JqTask;
struct JqTask {
    JqTask* next;
    u32 queue_slot, tag, id, job_ea, descriptor_size, binary_size;
    uint64_t tag_serial;
    uint8_t descriptor[256];
    uint8_t* binary;
};
typedef struct {
    int in_use, accepting, copy_sync_active;
    u32 handle_ea, maxJobs, jobCount, nextJobId, submitCount, completeCount;
    u32 completedIds[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS];
    s32 completionCodes[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS];
    u32 completedHead;
    JqTask* pending[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS];
} JqState;
typedef struct { int in_use; u32 port_ea, queue_slot; } JqPortState;

static JqState s_queues[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES];
static JqPortState s_ports[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS];
static atomic_uint s_active_job_dispatches;
static atomic_int s_queue_shutdown_requested;
static atomic_uint_fast64_t s_tag_submitted[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES][32];
static atomic_uint_fast64_t s_tag_completed[CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES][32];
static JqTask* s_task_head;
static JqTask* s_task_tail;
static int s_pool_workers, s_pool_stopping;
#ifdef _WIN32
static SRWLOCK s_jq_mutex = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static CONDITION_VARIABLE s_jq_cond = CONDITION_VARIABLE_INIT;
static HANDLE s_jq_threads[JQ_WORKER_MAX];
static void jq_lock(void) { AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_jq_mutex); }
static void jq_unlock(void) { ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_jq_mutex); }
static void jq_notify(void) { WakeAllConditionVariable(&s_jq_cond); }
static void jq_await(void) { SleepConditionVariableSRW(&s_jq_cond, &s_jq_mutex, INFINITE, 0); }
#else
static pthread_mutex_t s_jq_mutex = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t s_jq_cond = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_t s_jq_threads[JQ_WORKER_MAX];
static void jq_lock(void) { pthread_mutex_lock(&s_jq_mutex); }
static void jq_unlock(void) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&s_jq_mutex); }
static void jq_notify(void) { pthread_cond_broadcast(&s_jq_cond); }
static void jq_await(void) { pthread_cond_wait(&s_jq_cond, &s_jq_mutex); }
#endif

static void jq_trace_port2(const char* op, u32 port_ea, u32 queue_ea,
                           u32 job_ea, u32 descriptor_size,
                           u32 descriptor_pool_size, u32 tag,
                           int slot, s32 rc)
{
    static atomic_uint emitted;
    if (!getenv("SPURS_JQ_TRACE")) return;
    if (atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&emitted, 1, memory_order_relaxed) >= 64) return;
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[spurs-jq] %s port=%08X align=%u queue=%08X job=%08X "
            "desc=%u pool=%u tag=%u slot=%d rc=%08X\n",
            op, port_ea, port_ea & (CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_ALIGN - 1u),
            queue_ea, job_ea, descriptor_size, descriptor_pool_size, tag,
            slot, (u32)rc);
}

static int jq_requested_workers(void)
{
    /* Opt out with 0; 1 is an asynchronous PPU/offload lane. Multiple lanes
     * may expose other titles' non-thread-safe SPU globals: opt in deliberately. */
    static int cached = -1;
    if (cached < 0) {
        const char* e = getenv("SPURS_JQ_WORKERS");
        int n = e ? atoi(e) : 1;
        if (n < 0) n = 0;
        if (n > JQ_WORKER_MAX) n = JQ_WORKER_MAX;
        cached = n;
    }
    return cached;
}
static s32 jq_status_for_id(const JqState* q, u32 id)
{
    for (u32 i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS; ++i)
        if (q->completedIds[i] == id) return q->completionCodes[i];
    return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_JOB_NOT_FOUND;
}
static int jq_pending_id(const JqState* q, u32 id)
{
    for (u32 i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS; ++i)
        if (q->pending[i] && q->pending[i]->id == id) return 1;
    return 0;
}
static int jq_pending_tag_before(u32 slot, u32 mask, const uint64_t target[32])
{
    const JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
    for (u32 i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS; ++i) {
        const JqTask* t = q->pending[i];
        if (t && (mask & (1u << t->tag)) && t->tag_serial <= target[t->tag])
            return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Both sync and async completions use this path under the lock. */
static void jq_finish_locked(JqTask* t, s32 status)
{
    JqState* q = &s_queues[t->queue_slot];
    for (u32 i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS; ++i)
        if (q->pending[i] == t) { q->pending[i] = NULL; break; }
    q->completedIds[q->completedHead] = t->id;
    q->completionCodes[q->completedHead] = status;
    q->completedHead = (q->completedHead + 1u) % CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS;
    q->completeCount++;
    if (q->jobCount) q->jobCount--;
    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&s_tag_completed[t->queue_slot][t->tag], 1,
                              memory_order_release);
    atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&s_active_job_dispatches, 1,
                              memory_order_acq_rel);
    jq_notify();
}
static void jq_free_task(JqTask* t)
{
    if (!t) return;
    free(t->binary);
    free(t);
}
static s32 jq_execute(JqTask* t)
{
    /* The generated SPU code gets a fresh local store. Descriptor/binary reads
     * performed by the runner are from immutable copies; DMA payload EAs remain
     * guest-owned and must remain valid until completion. */
    return spu_workload_dispatch_job_snapshot(t->binary, t->binary_size,
                                               t->job_ea, t->descriptor_size,
                                               t->descriptor)
        ? CELL_OK : (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_JOB_NOT_FOUND;
}
#ifdef _WIN32
static DWORD WINAPI jq_worker_main(LPVOID arg)
#else
static void* jq_worker_main(void* arg)
#endif
{
    u32 worker_no = (u32)(uintptr_t)arg;
#ifdef _WIN32
    { ULONG guard = 256u * 1024u; SetThreadStackGuarantee(&guard); }
#endif
    spurs_job_set_spu_num(worker_no);
    for (;;) {
        jq_lock();
        while (!s_task_head && !s_pool_stopping) jq_await();
        if (!s_task_head && s_pool_stopping) { jq_unlock(); break; }
        JqTask* t = s_task_head;
        s_task_head = t->next;
        if (!s_task_head) s_task_tail = NULL;
        t->next = NULL;
        jq_unlock();
        s32 result = jq_execute(t);
        jq_lock();
        jq_finish_locked(t, result);
        jq_unlock();
        jq_free_task(t);
    }
    spu_workload_job_cache_thread_cleanup();
#ifdef _WIN32
    return 0;
#else
    return NULL;
#endif
}
/* Called with the lock. On thread creation failure, run synchronously instead
 * of losing a queued job; partially started workers remain available. */
static int jq_pool_start_locked(void)
{
    if (s_pool_workers) return 1;
    int requested = jq_requested_workers();
    if (!requested) return 0;
    s_pool_stopping = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < requested; ++i) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        HANDLE h = CreateThread(NULL, 1u << 20, jq_worker_main,
                                (void*)(uintptr_t)i, 0, NULL);
        if (!h) break;
        s_jq_threads[i] = h;
#else
        if (pthread_create(&s_jq_threads[i], NULL, jq_worker_main,
                           (void*)(uintptr_t)i) != 0) break;
#endif
        s_pool_workers++;
    }
    if (!s_pool_workers) return 0;
    fprintf(stderr, "[spurs-jq] async pool: %d worker(s) (requested %d)\n",
            s_pool_workers, requested);
    return 1;
}
static void jq_wait_for_dispatches(void)
{
    jq_lock();
    while (atomic_load_explicit(&s_active_job_dispatches, memory_order_acquire))
        jq_await();
    jq_unlock();
}
/* PushSync snapshots the selected tags' submissions, so later pushes cannot
 * keep it waiting; a completed COUNT alone is incorrect with out-of-order
 * workers, so inspect the pending serials instead. */
static void jq_wait_for_tag_mask(u32 slot, u32 mask)
{
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES || !mask) return;
    uint64_t target[32] = {0};
    jq_lock();
    for (u32 tag = 0; tag < 32; ++tag)
        if (mask & (1u << tag))
            target[tag] = atomic_load_explicit(&s_tag_submitted[slot][tag],
                                                 memory_order_acquire);
    while (jq_pending_tag_before(slot, mask, target)) jq_await();
    jq_unlock();
}
static void jq_wait_for_queue_dispatches(u32 slot)
{
    jq_wait_for_tag_mask(slot, UINT32_MAX);
}
static int jq_alloc(void)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES; i++) {
        if (!s_queues[i].in_use) return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

static int jq_find_handle(u32 handle_ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES; i++)
        if (s_queues[i].in_use && s_queues[i].handle_ea == handle_ea)
            return i;
    return -1;
}

static int jq_create_state(u32 handle_ea, u32 max_jobs)
{
    if (!vm_base || !handle_ea || handle_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return -1;
    jq_lock();
    int slot = jq_find_handle(handle_ea);
    if (slot < 0) slot = jq_alloc();
    if (slot >= 0 && !s_queues[slot].in_use) {
        JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
        memset(q, 0, sizeof(*q));
        q->in_use = q->accepting = 1;
        q->handle_ea = handle_ea;
        q->maxJobs = max_jobs ? max_jobs : CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS;
        q->nextJobId = 1;
        atomic_store_explicit(&s_queue_shutdown_requested, 0, memory_order_release);
        for (u32 tag = 0; tag < 32; ++tag) {
            atomic_store(&s_tag_submitted[slot][tag], 0);
            atomic_store(&s_tag_completed[slot][tag], 0);
        }
    }
    jq_unlock();
    if (slot >= 0) vm_write32(handle_ea, (u32)slot);
    return slot;
}

static int jq_port_slot(u32 port_ea)
{
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u) return -1;
    jq_lock();
    int result = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS; ++i) {
        if (s_ports[i].in_use && s_ports[i].port_ea == port_ea) {
            u32 slot = s_ports[i].queue_slot;
            if (slot < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES && s_queues[slot].in_use)
                result = (int)slot;
            break;
        }
    }
    jq_unlock();
    return result;
}
static s32 jq_register_port(u32 port_ea, u32 queue_slot)
{
    jq_lock();
    if (queue_slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES || !s_queues[queue_slot].in_use) {
        jq_unlock();
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    }
    const u32 queue_ea = s_queues[queue_slot].handle_ea;
    int free_slot = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS; ++i) {
        if (s_ports[i].in_use && s_ports[i].port_ea == port_ea) {
            s_ports[i].queue_slot = queue_slot;
            free_slot = -2;
            break;
        }
        if (!s_ports[i].in_use && free_slot < 0) free_slot = i;
    }
    if (free_slot == -1) {
        jq_unlock();
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    }
    if (free_slot >= 0) {
        s_ports[free_slot].in_use = 1;
        s_ports[free_slot].port_ea = port_ea;
        s_ports[free_slot].queue_slot = queue_slot;
    }
    jq_unlock();

    /* SDK Port2 layout: self EA at +0, atomic job counters at +0x10,
     * queue EA at +0x18, and the queue handle at +0x1C. */
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x00, port_ea);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x10, 0);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x14, 0);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x18, queue_ea);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x1C, queue_slot);
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* API */

s32 cellSpursJobQueueAttributeInitialize(CellSpursJobQueueAttribute* attr)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)attr;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(*attr))
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    memset(vm_base + ea, 0, sizeof(*attr));
    vm_write32(ea + 0, 64);
    vm_write32(ea + 4, 1);
    /* Default priority: normal on all SPUs */
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)
        vm_write8(ea + 8 + (u32)i, CELL_SPURS_JQ_PRIORITY_NORMAL);

    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueAttributeSetMaxGrab(CellSpursJobQueueAttribute* attr, u32 maxGrab)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)attr;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(*attr))
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    vm_write32(ea + 4, maxGrab);
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* This import's ABI is not documented in the local headers. Keep it as a
 * permissive success stub; no attribute fields are changed. */
u64 cellSpursJobQueueAttributeSetDoBusyWaiting(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a0; (void)a1; (void)a2; (void)a3;
    (void)a4; (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_OK;
}

/* SDK ABI: revision and internal-version arguments precede CellSpurs and the
 * queue handle, placing those pointers in the third and fourth saved slots.
 * This inline HLE registers queue state without an asynchronous pool. */
u64 _cellSpursCreateJobQueueWithJobDescriptorPool(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a0; (void)a1; (void)a4; (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 spurs_ea = (u32)a2;
    const u32 jq_ea = (u32)a3;
    if (!vm_base || !spurs_ea || !jq_ea || jq_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    int slot = jq_create_state(jq_ea, CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursCreateJobQueue(void* spurs, CellSpursJobQueue* jq,
                            const CellSpursJobQueueAttribute* attr,
                            void* buffer, u32 bufferSize)
{
    const u32 attr_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)attr;
    const u32 jq_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    (void)spurs; (void)buffer; (void)bufferSize;
    printf("[cellSpursJq] CreateJobQueue()\n");

    if (!vm_base || !jq_ea || !attr_ea ||
        jq_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u || attr_ea > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(*attr))
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    const u32 max_jobs = vm_read32(attr_ea + 0);
    if (!max_jobs || max_jobs > CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;

    int slot = jq_create_state(jq_ea, max_jobs);
    if (slot < 0) return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursDestroyJobQueue(CellSpursJobQueue* jq)
{
    const u32 jq_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !jq_ea || jq_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    u32 slot = vm_read32(jq_ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
    if (!q->in_use || q->handle_ea != jq_ea) {
        jq_unlock(); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    }
    q->accepting = 0;
    while (q->jobCount) jq_await();
    q->in_use = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS; ++i)
        if (s_ports[i].in_use && s_ports[i].queue_slot == slot)
            s_ports[i].in_use = 0;
    jq_unlock();
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursShutdownJobQueue(void)
{
    atomic_store_explicit(&s_queue_shutdown_requested, 1, memory_order_release);
    jq_wait_for_dispatches();
    jq_lock();
    s_pool_stopping = 1;
    jq_notify();
    int n = s_pool_workers;
    jq_unlock();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        WaitForSingleObject(s_jq_threads[i], INFINITE);
        CloseHandle(s_jq_threads[i]);
        s_jq_threads[i] = NULL;
#else
        pthread_join(s_jq_threads[i], NULL);
#endif
    }
    jq_lock();
    s_pool_workers = 0;
    s_pool_stopping = 0;
    jq_unlock();
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursJoinJobQueue(void)
{
    jq_wait_for_dispatches();
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* Prepare immutable job header+image at submission time. DMA payload buffers
 * remain guest-owned and may be mutated by the title; hardware likewise
 * requires titles to synchronize those buffers with job execution. */
static JqTask* jq_prepare(u32 job_ea, u32 descriptor_size)
{
    if (!vm_base || !job_ea ||
        (descriptor_size != 128u && descriptor_size != 256u) ||
        job_ea > UINT32_MAX - descriptor_size) return NULL;
    JqTask* t = (JqTask*)calloc(1, sizeof(*t));
    if (!t) return NULL;
    /* Snapshot FIRST, then decode its fields. Otherwise a concurrent guest
     * rewrite between header reads and memcpy could make the worker overread
     * the captured binary. */
    memcpy(t->descriptor, vm_base + job_ea, descriptor_size);
    const uint8_t* h = t->descriptor;
    u64 ea64 = 0;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i) ea64 = (ea64 << 8) | h[i];
    ea64 &= ~1ull;
    const u32 binary_size = (((u32)h[8] << 8) | h[9]) << 4;
    if (ea64 > UINT32_MAX || ea64 == 0 || binary_size == 0 ||
        binary_size > 0x40000u || ea64 > UINT32_MAX - binary_size) {
        free(t);
        return NULL;
    }
    t->binary = (uint8_t*)malloc(binary_size);
    if (!t->binary) { free(t); return NULL; }
    t->binary_size = binary_size;
    t->job_ea = job_ea;
    t->descriptor_size = descriptor_size;
    memcpy(t->binary, vm_base + (u32)ea64, binary_size);
    return t;
}

static s32 jq_push_slot_mode(u32 slot, u32 job_ea, u32 jobSize,
                             u32 tag, u32 id_ea, int copy_push)
{
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES || tag >= 32u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    JqTask* t = jq_prepare(job_ea, jobSize);
    if (!t) return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
    /* CopyPush promises its caller can reuse the original guest descriptor
     * immediately. The lifted code may DMA from JC_EA_JOB_DESCRIPTOR, whose
     * guest EA we cannot virtualize here. Drain this queue, execute CopyPush
     * synchronously, and exclude younger submissions until it returns. */
    while (q->in_use && q->accepting &&
           (q->copy_sync_active || (copy_push && q->jobCount)))
        jq_await();
    if (!q->in_use || !q->accepting ||
        atomic_load_explicit(&s_queue_shutdown_requested, memory_order_acquire)) {
        jq_unlock(); jq_free_task(t); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ABORT;
    }
    if (q->jobCount >= q->maxJobs || q->jobCount >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS) {
        jq_unlock(); jq_free_task(t); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_QUEUE_FULL;
    }
    u32 free_slot;
    for (free_slot = 0; free_slot < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS; ++free_slot)
        if (!q->pending[free_slot]) break;
    if (free_slot == CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS) {
        jq_unlock(); jq_free_task(t); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_QUEUE_FULL;
    }
    if (copy_push) q->copy_sync_active = 1;
    t->queue_slot = slot;
    t->tag = tag;
    t->id = q->nextJobId++;
    if (q->nextJobId == 0) q->nextJobId = 1;
    t->tag_serial = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&s_tag_submitted[slot][tag], 1,
                                               memory_order_acq_rel) + 1u;
    q->pending[free_slot] = t;
    q->jobCount++;
    q->submitCount++;
    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&s_active_job_dispatches, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);
    if (id_ea) vm_write32(id_ea, t->id);
    int asynchronous = !copy_push && jq_pool_start_locked();
    if (asynchronous) {
        if (s_task_tail) s_task_tail->next = t;
        else s_task_head = t;
        s_task_tail = t;
        jq_notify();
        jq_unlock();
        return CELL_OK;
    }
    jq_unlock();
    /* SPURS_JQ_WORKERS=0 is the legacy synchronous ABI/diagnostic mode. */
    spurs_job_set_spu_num(0);
    s32 result = jq_execute(t);
    jq_lock();
    jq_finish_locked(t, result);
    if (copy_push) { q->copy_sync_active = 0; jq_notify(); }
    jq_unlock();
    jq_free_task(t);
    return result;
}

static s32 jq_push_slot(u32 slot, u32 job_ea, u32 jobSize,
                        u32 tag, u32 id_ea)
{
    return jq_push_slot_mode(slot, job_ea, jobSize, tag, id_ea, 0);
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueuePush(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, const void* job,
                          u32 jobSize, u32 tag, CellSpursJobId* id)
{
    const u32 jq_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    const u32 id_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)id;
    if (!vm_base || !jq_ea || jq_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    return jq_push_slot(vm_read32(jq_ea), (u32)(uintptr_t)job,
                        jobSize, tag, id_ea);
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueuePushJob(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, const CellSpursJob256* job,
                             u32 tag, CellSpursJobId* id)
{
    return cellSpursJobQueuePush(jq, job, 256, tag, id);
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueuePort2Create(CellSpursJobQueuePort* port, CellSpursJobQueue* jq)
{
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)port;
    const u32 jq_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !jq_ea || !port_ea || jq_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u ||
        port_ea > UINT32_MAX - CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_SIZE) {
        jq_trace_port2("create", port_ea, jq_ea, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT);
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    }
    if (port_ea & (CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_ALIGN - 1u)) {
        jq_trace_port2("create", port_ea, jq_ea, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALIGN);
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALIGN;
    }

    /* Port creation may be the first HLE entry reached for a guest queue. */
    int slot = jq_create_state(jq_ea, CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_JOBS);
    if (slot < 0) {
        jq_trace_port2("create", port_ea, jq_ea, 0, 0, 0, 0, slot,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    }
    s32 rc = jq_register_port(port_ea, (u32)slot);
    jq_trace_port2("create", port_ea, jq_ea, 0, 0, 0, 0, slot, rc);
    return rc;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueuePort2Destroy(CellSpursJobQueuePort* port)
{
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)port;
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_SIZE)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    if (port_ea & (CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_ALIGN - 1u))
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALIGN;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_PORTS; i++)
        if (s_ports[i].in_use && s_ports[i].port_ea == port_ea)
            memset(&s_ports[i], 0, sizeof(s_ports[i]));
    jq_unlock();
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x00, 0);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x18, 0);
    vm_write32(port_ea + 0x1C, 0);
    return CELL_OK;
}

u64 cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushSync(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    /* SDK ABI: port, job-tag mask, DMA tag, flags. The tag mask is a value,
     * not a guest pointer; only matching jobs on this port's queue are joined. */
    (void)a2; (void)a3; (void)a4; (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)a0;
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED;
    jq_wait_for_tag_mask((u32)slot, (u32)a1);
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* Flush joins all jobs submitted on this queue before the call. */
u64 cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushFlush(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a1; (void)a2; (void)a3; (void)a4;
    (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)a0;
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED;
    jq_wait_for_queue_dispatches((u32)slot);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueSendSignal(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, CellSpursJobId id)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const u32 slot = vm_read32(ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES) return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    s32 result = s_queues[slot].in_use ? jq_status_for_id(&s_queues[slot], id)
                                        : (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_unlock();
    return result;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueWait(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, CellSpursJobId id)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u || id == 0)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const u32 slot = vm_read32(ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
    if (!q->in_use) { jq_unlock(); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; }
    while (jq_pending_id(q, id)) jq_await();
    s32 result = jq_status_for_id(q, id);
    jq_unlock();
    return result;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueTryWait(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, CellSpursJobId id)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u || id == 0)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const u32 slot = vm_read32(ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    JqState* q = &s_queues[slot];
    s32 result = !q->in_use ? (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT :
                 jq_pending_id(q, id) ? (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_BUSY :
                 jq_status_for_id(q, id);
    if (result == (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_JOB_NOT_FOUND && !q->submitCount)
        result = (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_BUSY;
    jq_unlock();
    return result;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueGetCount(CellSpursJobQueue* jq, u32* count)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq, ce = (u32)(uintptr_t)count;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || !ce || ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u || ce > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    u32 slot = vm_read32(ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    if (!s_queues[slot].in_use) { jq_unlock(); return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; }
    u32 n = s_queues[slot].jobCount;
    jq_unlock();
    vm_write32(ce, n);
    return CELL_OK;
}

s32 cellSpursJobQueueSemaphoreTryAcquire(CellSpursJobQueue* jq)
{
    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)jq;
    if (!vm_base || !ea || ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    u32 slot = vm_read32(ea);
    if (slot >= CELL_SPURS_JQ_MAX_QUEUES)
        return (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    jq_lock();
    s32 result = !s_queues[slot].in_use ? (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT :
                 s_queues[slot].jobCount ? (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_BUSY : CELL_OK;
    jq_unlock();
    return result;
}

u64 cellSpursJobQueuePort2Sync(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a1; (void)a2; (void)a3; (void)a4;
    (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)a0;
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - 4u)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED;
    jq_wait_for_queue_dispatches((u32)slot);
    return CELL_OK;
}

u64 _cellSpursJobQueuePort2CopyPushJobBody(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)a0;
    const u32 job_ea = (u32)a1;
    const u32 descriptor_size = (u32)a2;
    const u32 descriptor_pool_size = (u32)a3;
    const u32 tag = (u32)a4;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (getenv("GFD_QUEUE_TRACE") && slot != 1 && slot != 2) {
        static unsigned seen = 0;
        if (seen++ < 12)
            fprintf(stderr, "[gfd-copy-push] port=%08X job=%08X size=%u slot=%d\n",
                    port_ea, job_ea, descriptor_size, slot);
        fprintf(stderr, "[gfd-copy-header] binary=%016llX size16=%04X\n",
                (unsigned long long)vm_read64(job_ea), vm_read16(job_ea + 8));
    }
    if (!vm_base || !port_ea || port_ea > UINT32_MAX - CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_SIZE) {
        jq_trace_port2("copy-push", port_ea, 0, job_ea, descriptor_size,
                       descriptor_pool_size, tag, slot,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT);
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
    }
    if (port_ea & (CELL_SPURS_JQ_PORT2_ALIGN - 1u)) {
        jq_trace_port2("copy-push", port_ea, 0, job_ea, descriptor_size,
                       descriptor_pool_size, tag, slot,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALIGN);
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALIGN;
    }
    if (slot < 0) {
        jq_trace_port2("copy-push", port_ea, 0, job_ea, descriptor_size,
                       descriptor_pool_size, tag, slot,
                       (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED);
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED;
    }
    s32 rc = jq_push_slot_mode((u32)slot, job_ea, descriptor_size,
                               tag, 0, 1);
    jq_trace_port2("copy-push", port_ea, vm_read32(port_ea + 0x18), job_ea,
                   descriptor_size, descriptor_pool_size, tag, slot, rc);
    if (getenv("GFD_QUEUE_TRACE") && slot == 0)
        fprintf(stderr, "[gfd-copy-result] rc=%08X\n", (u32)rc);
    return (u64)(s64)rc;
}

u64 _cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushJobBody(
    u64 a0, u64 a1, u64 a2, u64 a3, u64 a4, u64 a5, u64 a6, u64 a7)
{
    (void)a4; (void)a5; (void)a6; (void)a7;
    const u32 port_ea = (u32)a0;
    const u32 job_ea = (u32)a1;
    const u32 descriptor_size = (u32)a2;
    const u32 tag = (u32)a3;
    const int slot = jq_port_slot(port_ea);
    if (slot < 0)
        return (u64)(s64)(s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED;
    return (u64)(s64)jq_push_slot((u32)slot, job_ea, descriptor_size, tag, 0);
}

/*
 * ps3recomp - cellSpursJq HLE
 *
 * SPURS Job Queue — advanced SPU job dispatch built on cellSpurs.
 * Provides a bounded queue model and runs submitted descriptors through the
 * runtime's lifted SPU job dispatcher when their binaries are registered.
 */

#define CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_ALREADY_INITIALIZED 0x80410A02
#define CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT    0x80410A03
#define CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY       0x80410A04

===== FILE: \libs\spurs\spurs_pm.c =====
/* spurs_pm.c -- SPURS taskset Policy Module logic (Option B, phase B3), clean-room
 * reimplementation of the parts of RPCS3 cellSpursSpu.cpp our HLE needs. Operates on
 * the BE shared-memory layout (spurs_taskset.h); all guest access via the vm_read /
 * vm_write byte-swapping accessors.
 *
 * This module is the "SPU kernel" that schedules our real lifted leaf task: it selects a
 * ready task and builds the SpursTasksetContext at LS 0x2700, then the dispatcher loads
 * the task's context and runs it. Selection logic cross-referenced vs RPCS3
 * spursTasksetProcessRequest(SELECT_TASK): readyButNotRunning = ready & ~running, scanned
 * round-robin starting after last_scheduled_task; task N occupies bitset bit (127-N).
 * RPCS3_REFERENCE_REVIEWED: this file declares a clean-room implementation
 * using RPCS3 behavior/layout as a reference. The cited comments do not
 * establish copied source; see docs/RPCS3_LICENSE_AUDIT.md.
 */
#include "spurs_taskset.h"
#include <stdint.h>

/* Select the next task to run: first task that is ready and not running, scanning
 * round-robin from (last_scheduled_task + 1). Returns the taskId (0..127) or -1 if none
 * is runnable. (The wkl_flag_wait_task exclusion is a refinement we add when needed.) */
int spurs_pm_select_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t last_scheduled_task)
{
    uint32_t ready_ea   = taskset_ea + CSTS_READY;
    uint32_t running_ea = taskset_ea + CSTS_RUNNING;
    for (uint32_t i = 1; i <= 128; i++) {
        uint32_t t = (last_scheduled_task + i) & 127;     /* round-robin, wrap at 128 */
        if (spurs_bitset_test(ready_ea, t) && !spurs_bitset_test(running_ea, t))
            return (int)t;
    }
    return -1;
}

/* Mark a task as the running one: clear ready, set running, record last_scheduled_task.
 * (RPCS3 moves the task ready->running on dispatch.) last_scheduled_task is the byte at
 * CSTS_LAST_SCHEDULED (0x73) = the low byte of the big-endian word at 0x70. */
void spurs_pm_mark_running(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId)
{
    spurs_bitset_clear(taskset_ea + CSTS_READY, taskId);
    spurs_bitset_set(taskset_ea + CSTS_RUNNING, taskId);
    uint32_t w = vm_read32(taskset_ea + 0x70);
    w = (w & 0xFFFFFF00u) | (taskId & 0xFFu);
    vm_write32(taskset_ea + 0x70, w);
}

/* Build the SpursTasksetContext at LS 0x2700 for the selected task, and DMA its TaskInfo
 * into LS 0x2780. ls = the SPU local store (256 KB). Returns the task ELF EA (low 3 bits
 * are flags, masked off for loading). */
uint64_t spurs_pm_build_context(uint8_t* ls, uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId,
                                uint32_t spuNum, uint32_t dmaTagId)
{
    /* SpursTasksetContext header fields (LS-local, written big-endian like guest mem). */
    /* taskset ptr @0x27B8 (be u64), spuNum @0x27CC, dmaTagId @0x27D0, taskId @0x27D4,
     * tasksetMgmtAddr @0x2FB8, x2FC0 cleared. We write directly into ls[] big-endian. */
    #define LS_BE32(off, v) do { uint32_t _v=(v); ls[(off)+0]=(uint8_t)(_v>>24); ls[(off)+1]=(uint8_t)(_v>>16); \
                                 ls[(off)+2]=(uint8_t)(_v>>8); ls[(off)+3]=(uint8_t)_v; } while(0)
    #define LS_BE64(off, v) do { uint64_t _w=(v); LS_BE32((off), (uint32_t)(_w>>32)); LS_BE32((off)+4,(uint32_t)_w); } while(0)

    /* Copy the CellSpursTaskset HEADER (first 0x80 bytes: the 6 bitsets, spurs@0x60,
     * args@0x68, wid@0x74, x78@0x78) from the main-memory taskset into LS 0x2700. RPCS3
     * spursTasksetStartTask reads taskset->spurs / taskset->args from LS 0x2700+0x60/0x68
     * to build the leaf's r4 = {args (d0), spurs EA (d1)}; without this the leaf gets a
     * garbage SPURS base and DMAs from a bad address. The STC fields written below sit at
     * offsets >= 0x80 (TaskInfo array region in the union view) so they don't overlap. */
    for (int o = 0; o < 0x80; o += 4)
        LS_BE32(STC_BASE + o, vm_read32(taskset_ea + o));

    LS_BE64(STC_TASKSET_PTR,  (uint64_t)taskset_ea);
    LS_BE32(STC_SPU_NUM,      spuNum);
    LS_BE32(STC_DMA_TAG_ID,   dmaTagId);
    LS_BE32(STC_TASK_ID,      taskId);
    LS_BE32(STC_TASKSET_MGMT_ADDR, STC_BASE);
    LS_BE64(STC_X2FC0, 0);
    /* Task-syscall path: a SPURS task reads syscallAddr from its context and branches to
     * it (e.g. to EXIT). The real kernel sets it to the PM's in-LS syscall entry (0xA70);
     * we don't have the PM resident, so we set the same address and INTERCEPT a branch to
     * it in spu_indirect_branch (spu_channels.c) to HLE the syscall. Without this the task
     * branches to 0 -> null call -> halt (image=7's NULL_POINTER cascade). kernelMgmtAddr
     * -> the SPURS kernel context (LS 0x100). */
    LS_BE32(STC_KERNEL_MGMT_ADDR, 0x100);
    LS_BE32(STC_SYSCALL_ADDR,     CELL_SPURS_TASKSET_PM_SYSCALL_ADDR);

    /* SPURS KERNEL context (LS 0x100..0x1FF): the SPU task library's fast-path
     * validation reads fields the real kernel + taskset PM populate there.
     * moduleId @0x1E4 must be "TK" (stamped by the taskset PM, RPCS3
     * spursTasksetInit) -- without it every task-API wait (event flag / queue)
     * fails its context check with ERROR_STAT 0x80410909: LBP's binkspu movie
     * IO task spun forever on exactly that, so BinkWait never completed and
     * the intro never produced a frame. Also plant the spurs instance ptr
     * (@0x1C0, read from the taskset header) + spuNum/dmaTagId, which the
     * library reads next to the moduleId. */
    {
        uint32_t spurs_lo = vm_read32(taskset_ea + 0x64);   /* be64 spurs @0x60 */
        LS_BE64(0x1C0, (uint64_t)spurs_lo);
        LS_BE32(0x1C8, spuNum);
        LS_BE32(0x1CC, dmaTagId);
        /* The task library's fast-path check FSMs on the halfword at 0x1E8
         * (ceqh of rotqbyi(LS[0x1E0],6), select-mask bit -> word0); stamp the
         * neighboring slots too -- they are all inside the moduleId/pad area
         * the real PM owns and nothing else reads them. */
        ls[0x1E4] = 'T'; ls[0x1E5] = 'K';
        ls[0x1E6] = 'T'; ls[0x1E7] = 'K';
        ls[0x1E8] = 'T'; ls[0x1E9] = 'K';
    }

    /* DMA the selected task's TaskInfo (48 bytes) into LS 0x2780 (the kernel temp area).
     * Read each word BE and re-store BE -> the raw bytes are preserved verbatim. */
    uint32_t ti = spurs_taskset_taskinfo_ea(taskset_ea, taskId);
    for (int o = 0; o < TI_SIZE; o += 4)
        LS_BE32(STC_TEMP_TASKINFO + o, vm_read32(ti + o));

    /* Force a FULL-COVERAGE ls pattern (TaskInfo +0x20, 128 bits). The real
     * taskset PM computes a precise bitmask of the 2KB LS blocks the task's
     * context occupies, and the SPU task library refuses any blocking wait
     * whose pattern doesn't cover the task's stack (error 0x8041090F). We run
     * each task in its OWN full 256KB local store (never sharing LS between
     * tasks), so every block IS the task's -- an all-ones pattern is the
     * accurate description of our execution model, not a fake. Without it a
     * wait-capable task (LBP's binkspu movie IO) spun forever and the intro
     * movie never decoded a frame. The game's own pattern reaches us mangled
     * anyway (its lsPattern EA arrives unaligned through the attribute ABI). */
    LS_BE32(STC_TEMP_TASKINFO + TI_LS_PATTERN + 0x0, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    LS_BE32(STC_TEMP_TASKINFO + TI_LS_PATTERN + 0x4, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    LS_BE32(STC_TEMP_TASKINFO + TI_LS_PATTERN + 0x8, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    LS_BE32(STC_TEMP_TASKINFO + TI_LS_PATTERN + 0xC, 0xFFFFFFFFu);

    return vm_read64(ti + TI_ELF);       /* caller masks elf & ~7 to load */
    #undef LS_BE32
    #undef LS_BE64
}


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\spurs_taskset.c =====
/* spurs_taskset.c -- build the real CellSpursTaskset shared-memory layout (Option B,
 * phase B2). These functions write the BE structures that the reimplemented PM (B3)
 * and the real lifted leaf task read. ALL writes go through the byte-swapping
 * vm_write32/vm_write64 accessors (see the BIG-ENDIAN WARNING in spurs_taskset.h);
 * no native struct writes. Layout cross-referenced vs RPCS3 cellSpurs.h.
 *
 * Pure layout builders -- unit-tested in tests/test_spurs_taskset_main.c. cellSpurs.c
 * (the PPU create path) and the PM dispatcher call these.
 */
#include "spurs_taskset.h"
#include <stdint.h>

/* Initialize a fresh taskset: clear all task bitsets and write the header fields.
 * spurs_ea = the CellSpurs object EA; args = taskset args doubleword; wid = workload
 * id; size = taskset size; evf1/evf2 = attached event-flag ids (0 if none). */
void spurs_taskset_init(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t spurs_ea, uint64_t args,
                        uint32_t wid, uint32_t size, uint32_t evf1, uint32_t evf2)
{
    /* clear running/ready/pending_ready/enabled/signalled/waiting (each 16 bytes) */
    for (uint32_t off = CSTS_RUNNING; off <= CSTS_WAITING; off += 0x10) {
        vm_write64(taskset_ea + off + 0, 0);
        vm_write64(taskset_ea + off + 8, 0);
    }
    vm_write64(taskset_ea + CSTS_SPURS, (uint64_t)spurs_ea); /* CellSpurs* (be u64) */
    vm_write64(taskset_ea + CSTS_ARGS,  args);
    vm_write32(taskset_ea + CSTS_WID,   wid);
    vm_write64(taskset_ea + CSTS_X78,   0);                  /* on-exit handler EA */
    vm_write32(taskset_ea + CSTS_SIZE_FIELD,     size);
    vm_write32(taskset_ea + CSTS_EVENT_FLAG_ID1, evf1);
    vm_write32(taskset_ea + CSTS_EVENT_FLAG_ID2, evf2);
}

/* Set or clear one task's bit in a taskset bitset (ready/pending/enabled at +0x10/+0x20/+0x30) from a host thread.
 *
 * These bitsets share the taskset's first 128-byte line with the SPU task library, which updates them with
 * GETLLAR/PUTLLC, and with the host's task exit (spu_taskset_task_exited). spurs_bitset_set/_clear read the word
 * with vm_read32 outside the lock-line lock and write it back with vm_write32, so a change committed between the
 * two was undone. Do the read-modify-write on the raw guest bytes under the lock-line lock (vm_write32 takes that
 * lock itself when the line is reserved, and it does not nest), then drop every reservation on the line. */
void spurs_taskset_bitset_update(uint32_t bitset_ea, uint32_t taskId, int set)
{
    extern void spu_lockline_lock(void); extern void spu_lockline_unlock(void);
    extern void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t);
    extern uint8_t* vm_base;
    uint8_t* p = vm_base + bitset_ea + taskId / 8;
    const uint8_t m = (uint8_t)(0x80u >> (taskId % 8));
    spu_lockline_lock();
    if (set) *p |= m; else *p &= (uint8_t)~m;
    spu_coh_notify_write(bitset_ea);
    spu_lockline_unlock();
}

/* Take the lowest free task id of a taskset: find the first clear bit of the enabled bitset and set it, as one
 * step under the lock-line lock, so a task exit clearing its bit at the same time is never undone and two callers
 * never get the same id. Returns `max_tasks` when every id is taken. */
uint32_t spurs_taskset_take_slot(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t max_tasks)
{
    extern void spu_lockline_lock(void); extern void spu_lockline_unlock(void);
    extern void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t);
    extern uint8_t* vm_base;
    uint8_t* en = vm_base + taskset_ea + CSTS_ENABLED;
    uint32_t slot = max_tasks;
    spu_lockline_lock();
    for (uint32_t t = 0; t < max_tasks; t++) {
        const uint8_t m = (uint8_t)(0x80u >> (t % 8));
        if (!(en[t / 8] & m)) { en[t / 8] |= m; slot = t; break; }
    }
    if (slot < max_tasks) spu_coh_notify_write(taskset_ea + CSTS_ENABLED);
    spu_lockline_unlock();
    return slot;
}

/* Register a task: write task_info[taskId] (args/elf/context/ls_pattern) and mark the
 * task enabled + ready so the PM's SELECT_TASK picks it. arg/ls_pattern may be NULL. */
void spurs_taskset_add_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId, uint64_t elf_ea,
                            uint64_t context, const uint32_t arg[4],
                            const uint32_t ls_pattern[4])
{
    uint32_t ti = spurs_taskset_taskinfo_ea(taskset_ea, taskId);
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) vm_write32(ti + TI_ARGS + i * 4, arg ? arg[i] : 0);
    vm_write64(ti + TI_ELF, elf_ea);
    vm_write64(ti + TI_CONTEXT, context);
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        vm_write32(ti + TI_LS_PATTERN + i * 4, ls_pattern ? ls_pattern[i] : 0);
    spurs_taskset_bitset_update(taskset_ea + CSTS_ENABLED, taskId, 1);
    spurs_taskset_bitset_update(taskset_ea + CSTS_READY,   taskId, 1);
}

/* Set the taskset's on-task-exit handler EA (CellSpursTaskset.x78). */
void spurs_taskset_set_exit_handler(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint64_t handler_ea)
{
    vm_write64(taskset_ea + CSTS_X78, handler_ea);
}


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\spurs_taskset.h =====
/* spurs_taskset.h -- SPURS taskset Policy-Module shared-memory layout (Option B).
 *
 * ============================ BIG-ENDIAN WARNING ============================
 * These structures live in GUEST memory and are read by REAL lifted SPU code (the
 * leaf task) and by our reimplemented PM. The guest (PPC/SPU) is BIG-ENDIAN; the
 * host (x86) is little-endian. Therefore EVERY multi-byte field MUST be accessed
 * byte-swapped. Do NOT define native C structs over guest memory and write fields
 * directly (that stores little-endian -> the SPU reads garbage) -- that mismatch is
 * exactly why our prior HLE (which memset/native-wrote simplified structs) left the
 * SPU reading zeros/garbage (docs/12 root cause).
 *
 * RULE: access taskset/context fields ONLY via the BE accessors vm_read32/vm_read64/
 * vm_write32/vm_write64 (ppu_loader.cpp -- they byte-swap), at guest_EA + the offset
 * constants below. The offsets are the source of truth (reimplemented clean from the
 * public SDK / RPCS3 cellSpurs.h contracts; no GPL code copied).
 * ===========================================================================
 */
#ifndef SPURS_TASKSET_H
#define SPURS_TASKSET_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* BE guest-memory accessors. Pull in the canonical definitions rather than
 * re-declaring them here: ppu_memory.h defines this family `static inline`, and
 * a preceding extern declaration gives them external linkage instead, so every
 * translation unit including this header emitted its own vm_read32/vm_read64/
 * vm_write32/vm_write64.
 *
 * That stayed invisible while no title linked both this and the loader's
 * same-named (64-bit EA) family -- a static library only pulls in the objects
 * it needs. Tokyo Jungle references SPURS, which drags cellSpurs.c in, and the
 * link then failed with five duplicate symbols.
 *
 * It is also a hard error on Clang, which rejects the non-static
 * re-declaration outright where MSVC accepted it -- so this is what kept
 * the tree from compiling on macOS at all. */
#include "../../runtime/ppu/ppu_memory.h"

/* ---- CellSpursTaskset (main memory, 128-byte aligned) --------------------
 * The PM reads the task bitsets to pick a ready task and the TaskInfo array for
 * its ELF/context/args. Max 128 tasks; each TaskInfo is 48 bytes. */
enum {
    CSTS_RUNNING        = 0x00,   /* atomic 128-bit bitset (4 BE u32) */
    CSTS_READY          = 0x10,
    CSTS_PENDING_READY  = 0x20,
    CSTS_ENABLED        = 0x30,
    CSTS_SIGNALLED      = 0x40,
    CSTS_WAITING        = 0x50,
    CSTS_SPURS          = 0x60,   /* be u64: CellSpurs* */
    CSTS_ARGS           = 0x68,   /* be u64 */
    CSTS_ENABLE_CLEAR_LS= 0x70,   /* u8  */
    CSTS_WKL_FLAG_WAIT  = 0x72,   /* u8  */
    CSTS_LAST_SCHEDULED = 0x73,   /* u8  */
    CSTS_WID            = 0x74,   /* be u32: workload id */
    CSTS_X78            = 0x78,   /* be u64: on-task-exit handler EA */
    CSTS_TASKINFO       = 0x80,   /* TaskInfo[128] */
    CSTS_EXC_HANDLER    = 0x1880, /* be u64 */
    CSTS_EXC_HANDLER_ARG= 0x1888, /* be u64 */
    CSTS_SIZE_FIELD     = 0x1890, /* be u32 */
    CSTS_EVENT_FLAG_ID1 = 0x1898, /* be u32 */
    CSTS_EVENT_FLAG_ID2 = 0x189C, /* be u32 */
    CSTS_STRUCT_END     = 0x1900,
};

/* CellSpursTaskset::TaskInfo (48 bytes), at CSTS_TASKINFO + taskId*48 */
enum {
    TI_SIZE       = 48,
    TI_ARGS       = 0x00,   /* CellSpursTaskArgument (16 bytes) */
    TI_ELF        = 0x10,   /* be u64: task ELF EA (low 3 bits = flags) */
    TI_CONTEXT    = 0x18,   /* be u64: context_save_storage | alloc_ls_blocks */
    TI_LS_PATTERN = 0x20,   /* CellSpursTaskLsPattern (16 bytes) */
};

static inline uint32_t spurs_taskset_taskinfo_ea(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId)
{ return taskset_ea + CSTS_TASKINFO + taskId * TI_SIZE; }

/* set/clear/test a task bit in a 128-bit bitset (bit 0 = MSB of word 0, per RPCS3
 * atomic_tasks_bitset::get_bit). bitset_ea = taskset_ea + CSTS_READY etc. */
static inline void spurs_bitset_set(uint32_t bitset_ea, uint32_t taskId)
{
    uint32_t word_ea = bitset_ea + (taskId / 32) * 4;
    uint32_t mask = (1u << 31) >> (taskId % 32);
    vm_write32(word_ea, vm_read32(word_ea) | mask);
}
static inline void spurs_bitset_clear(uint32_t bitset_ea, uint32_t taskId)
{
    uint32_t word_ea = bitset_ea + (taskId / 32) * 4;
    uint32_t mask = (1u << 31) >> (taskId % 32);
    vm_write32(word_ea, vm_read32(word_ea) & ~mask);
}
static inline int spurs_bitset_test(uint32_t bitset_ea, uint32_t taskId)
{
    uint32_t word_ea = bitset_ea + (taskId / 32) * 4;
    uint32_t mask = (1u << 31) >> (taskId % 32);
    return (vm_read32(word_ea) & mask) != 0;
}

/* ---- SpursTasksetContext (SPU local store @ 0x2700, size 0x900) ----------
 * Built by the PM in LS before/while running the leaf task. */
enum {
    STC_BASE              = 0x2700,
    STC_TEMP_TASKSET      = 0x2700, /* 0x80 scratch */
    STC_TEMP_TASKINFO     = 0x2780, /* 0x30 (DMA'd TaskInfo of the selected task) */
    STC_TASKSET_PTR       = 0x27B8, /* be u64: CellSpursTaskset EA */
    STC_KERNEL_MGMT_ADDR  = 0x27C0, /* be u32 */
    STC_SYSCALL_ADDR      = 0x27C4, /* be u32 */
    STC_SPU_NUM           = 0x27CC, /* be u32 */
    STC_DMA_TAG_ID        = 0x27D0, /* be u32 */
    STC_TASK_ID           = 0x27D4, /* be u32 */
    STC_MODULE_ID         = 0x2840, /* 16 bytes */
    STC_SAVED_LR          = 0x2C80, /* v128: entry point / saved LR */
    STC_SAVED_SP          = 0x2C90, /* v128 */
    STC_SAVED_R80_R127    = 0x2CA0, /* v128[48] */
    STC_SAVED_FPSCR       = 0x2FA0, /* v128 */
    STC_SAVED_EVENT_MASK  = 0x2FB4, /* be u32 */
    STC_TASKSET_MGMT_ADDR = 0x2FB8, /* be u32 */
    STC_X2FC0             = 0x2FC0, /* be u64 (exit-handler addr alt) */
    STC_X2FC8             = 0x2FC8, /* be u64 (exit-handler args) */
    STC_TASK_EXIT_CODE    = 0x2FD0, /* be u32 */
    STC_X2FD4             = 0x2FD4, /* be u32 */
    STC_STRUCT_END        = 0x3000,
};

/* Fixed LS addresses of the taskset Policy Module entry points (RPCS3 cellSpurs.h).
 * A SPURS task calls its taskset PM's syscall entry via the SpursTasksetContext
 * syscallAddr field (STC_SYSCALL_ADDR), which the kernel sets to this address.
 * Our HLE intercepts a branch to CELL_SPURS_TASKSET_PM_SYSCALL_ADDR (spu_channels.c)
 * to process the task syscall, since we don't have the real PM code resident in LS. */
enum {
    CELL_SPURS_TASKSET_PM_ENTRY_ADDR   = 0xA00,
    CELL_SPURS_TASKSET_PM_SYSCALL_ADDR = 0xA70,
};

/* CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_* (leaf-task `stop <code>` operand low nibble). */
enum {
    CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_EXIT          = 0,
    CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_YIELD         = 1,
    CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_WAIT_SIGNAL   = 2,
    CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_POLL          = 3,
    CELL_SPURS_TASK_SYSCALL_RECV_WKL_FLAG = 4,
};

/* ---- create-path layout builders (spurs_taskset.c, phase B2) ------------- */
void spurs_taskset_init(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t spurs_ea, uint64_t args,
                        uint32_t wid, uint32_t size, uint32_t evf1, uint32_t evf2);
void spurs_taskset_bitset_update(uint32_t bitset_ea, uint32_t taskId, int set);
uint32_t spurs_taskset_take_slot(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t max_tasks);
void spurs_taskset_add_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId, uint64_t elf_ea,
                            uint64_t context, const uint32_t arg[4],
                            const uint32_t ls_pattern[4]);
void spurs_taskset_set_exit_handler(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint64_t handler_ea);

/* ---- PM logic (spurs_pm.c, phase B3) ------------------------------------- */
int      spurs_pm_select_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t last_scheduled_task);
void     spurs_pm_mark_running(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);
uint64_t spurs_pm_build_context(uint8_t* ls, uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId,
                                uint32_t spuNum, uint32_t dmaTagId);

#endif /* SPURS_TASKSET_H */


===== FILE: \libs\spurs\tests\test_jq_sync.c =====
/* PushSync must accept a tag mask and order outstanding jobs, without
 * dispatching that mask as a descriptor or writing through spare registers. */
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#ifdef NDEBUG
#undef NDEBUG
#endif
#include <assert.h>
#include "../cellSpursJq.c"

static uint8_t guest[0x4000];
uint8_t* vm_base = guest;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
s32 sys_ppu_thread_yield(void) { SwitchToThread(); return 0; }

static HANDLE job_entered, release_job, sync_done;
static LONG dispatch_calls;
int spu_workload_dispatch_job(const uint8_t* image, uint32_t image_size,
                             uint32_t job_ea, uint32_t descriptor_size)
{
    assert(image == guest + 0x1800 && image_size == 16);
    assert(job_ea == 0x1400 && descriptor_size == 128);
    InterlockedIncrement(&dispatch_calls);
    SetEvent(job_entered);
    assert(WaitForSingleObject(release_job, 2000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0);
    return 1;
}
static DWORD WINAPI submit(void* unused)
{
    (void)unused;
    assert(cellSpursJobQueuePush((CellSpursJobQueue*)(uintptr_t)0x1000,
                               (void*)(uintptr_t)0x1400, 128, 7, NULL) == 0);
    return 0;
}
static DWORD WINAPI sync_port(void* unused)
{
    (void)unused;
    assert(cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushSync(0x1200, 1u << 7, 0,
                                        0, 0x1600, 0, 0, 0) == 0);
    SetEvent(sync_done);
    return 0;
}
int main(void)
{
    assert(cellSpursJobQueuePort2Create((CellSpursJobQueuePort*)(uintptr_t)0x1200,
                                      (CellSpursJobQueue*)(uintptr_t)0x1000) == 0);
    /* This exact three-register shape aborted P5's battle-loading worker. */
    assert(cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushSync(0x1200, 1u << 7, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) == 0);
    assert((s32)cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushSync(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) ==
           (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT);
    assert((s32)cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushSync(0x1300, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) ==
           (s32)CELL_SPURS_JQ_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED);

    job_entered = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL);
    release_job = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL);
    sync_done = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL);
    vm_write64(0x1400, 0x1800);
    vm_write16(0x1408, 1);
    vm_write32(0x1600, 0xA5A5A5A5);
    HANDLE producer = CreateThread(NULL, 0, submit, NULL, 0, NULL);
    assert(producer && WaitForSingleObject(job_entered, 1000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0);
    HANDLE waiter = CreateThread(NULL, 0, sync_port, NULL, 0, NULL);
    assert(waiter && WaitForSingleObject(sync_done, 50) == WAIT_TIMEOUT);
    SetEvent(release_job);
    assert(WaitForSingleObject(producer, 1000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0);
    assert(WaitForSingleObject(waiter, 1000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0);
    assert(dispatch_calls == 1 && vm_read32(0x1600) == 0xA5A5A5A5);
    assert(s_queues[0].submitCount == 1 && s_queues[0].completeCount == 1);
    CloseHandle(producer); CloseHandle(waiter);
    CloseHandle(job_entered); CloseHandle(release_job); CloseHandle(sync_done);
    puts("job queue sync: tag mask ABI, completion ordering, no extra job/writes PASS");
    return 0;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#ifdef _WIN32
static LARGE_INTEGER s_qpc_freq;
static int           s_qpc_init = 0;

static void ensure_qpc_init(void)
{
    if (!s_qpc_init) {
        QueryPerformanceFrequency(&s_qpc_freq);
        s_qpc_init = 1;
    }
}

static u64 get_timestamp_ns(void)
{
    LARGE_INTEGER now;
    ensure_qpc_init();
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&now);
    /* Convert to nanoseconds: (count * 1e9) / freq */
    return (u64)((double)now.QuadPart * 1000000000.0 / (double)s_qpc_freq.QuadPart);
}
#else
static u64 get_timestamp_ns(void)
{
    struct timespec ts;
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (u64)ts.tv_sec * 1000000000ULL + (u64)ts.tv_nsec;
}
#endif

/* Flip requests (each puts the status back to WAITING) and the request a
 * pending flip completion was marked for: a completion delivered late must not
 * mark DONE a flip requested after it (see ppu_gcm_pump). */
static volatile u32 s_flip_req_seq, s_flip_tick_seq;
/* The status's read-modify-write transitions (request, tick, completion) run
 * on different threads; without a lock a completion could read "no newer
 * request" just before a request stored WAITING and then overwrite it. */
#ifdef _WIN32
static volatile LONG s_flip_lock;
#define FLIP_LOCK()   do { while (InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_flip_lock, 1, 0)) YieldProcessor(); } while (0)
#define FLIP_UNLOCK() InterlockedExchange(&s_flip_lock, 0)
#else
static volatile int s_flip_lock;
#define FLIP_LOCK()   do { while (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_flip_lock, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {} } while (0)
#define FLIP_UNLOCK() __atomic_store_n(&s_flip_lock, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)
#endif

/* Count of guest flip requests (SetFlipCommand / SetPrepareFlip). The present
 * loop uses this as the frame boundary: presenting only when a flip arrived
 * keeps partially-drained frames off screen (the ticker otherwise presents on
 * a fixed 16ms clock, and a drain that catches the guest mid-frame -- e.g.
 * while it's blocked in the FIFO-wrap recycle callback -- would show a
 * clear+few-draws frame as a visible flicker). */
static volatile u32 s_flip_request_count = 0;

u32 cellGcm_flip_request_count(void)
{
    return s_flip_request_count;
}
static u32  s_debug_level = CELL_GCM_DEBUG_LEVEL0;

/* Display buffers */
static CellGcmDisplayInfo s_display_buffers[CELL_GCM_MAX_DISPLAY_BUFFER_NUM];
static int s_display_buffer_set[CELL_GCM_MAX_DISPLAY_BUFFER_NUM];
static u32 s_current_display_buffer_id = 0;
/* FIFO flips are complete as soon as the parser reaches their command; the
 * parser intentionally stops there, so get != put is normal. Direct API flips
 * have no command boundary and must wait for the current FIFO batch to drain. */
static volatile int s_flip_fifo_present_pending = 0;
static volatile int s_flip_api_present_pending = 0;
/* A flip _cellGcmSetFlipCommand queued in the FIFO: | bufferId, bit 8 = ours. */
#define GCM_FLIP_MARKER 0xFEAD0100u
/* Flips queued into the command stream by gcm_flip_into_fifo, and how many of
 * those markers the drain has reached. The RSX completes a flip when it
 * executes it; until the drain reaches the marker, the flip has not happened,
 * however many vblanks go by. */
static volatile u32 s_fifo_flips_queued = 0, s_fifo_flips_reached = 0;
static volatile u32 s_fifo_flip_events = 0;
static u32 s_fifo_flip_events_completed = 0; /* executed/skipped flips at last tick */
/* A direct API flip has no FIFO command to establish its execution boundary. */
static volatile int s_flip_direct_pending = 0;

static s32 gcm_flip_request(u32 bufferId, int in_fifo);
static int gcm_fifo_flip_execute(u32 bufferId);

/* May this beat complete a flip? Yes if the drain has executed a FIFO flip
 * since the last completion, or if a direct API flip is waiting. A flip that
 * is queued, or written but not yet flushed, does not
 * hold back the completion of one already executed: the RSX reports the flip
 * it did, not the ones still ahead of it. With no flip outstanding there is
 * nothing to complete: Twisted Metal resets the flip status, takes about a
 * second to build its next frame here, then queues the flip, and a beat in
 * between that reported a flip made it take the new one for done. It then
 * rebuilt the command segment the walker was still waiting in. */
static int gcm_flip_executed_take(void)
{
    const u32 events = s_fifo_flip_events;
    if (events != s_fifo_flip_events_completed) {
        s_fifo_flip_events_completed = events;
        return 1;
    }
    if (s_flip_direct_pending) { s_flip_direct_pending = 0; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
/* ponytail: fixed headroom, far above one frame's commands (Simpsons ~10 KB);
 * derive it from the observed per-frame volume if a title outgrows it. */
#define GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES 0x40000u

int cellGcm_take_flip_pending(void)
{
    if (s_flip_fifo_present_pending) {
        s_flip_fifo_present_pending = 0;
        return 1;
    }
    int v = s_flip_api_present_pending;
    s_flip_api_present_pending = 0;
    return v;
}

/* The flip now names this buffer. The shared draw engine presents on the
 * host's call and only learns a buffer from 0xE944 by itself, so it would
 * keep presenting display buffer 0 for a title that flips through 0xFEAD. */
static void gcm_set_current_display_buffer(u32 bufferId)
{
    s_current_display_buffer_id = bufferId;
    if (rsx_draw_engine_enabled())
        rsx_draw_engine_note_flip(bufferId);
}

 * set_offset_table/clear_offset_table keep these two host arrays in step with
 * the IO mappings, and that part was always fine. What was not: the tables
 * cellGcmGetOffsetTable hands out are indexed BY THE GUEST --
 * ioAddress[ea >> 20] and eaAddress[io >> 20] -- and it handed over 64-bit host

 * directly from guest memory. The runner sets g_gcm_driver_info_ea during

/* GCM_FLIPCB_ONTICK=1: fire the guest flip handler only when the flip

static u32 s_vblank_handler_opd   = 0;
static u32 s_user_handler_opd     = 0;
static u32 s_second_v_handler_opd = 0;
/* YDKJ_HANDLERFIX: the handler OPD's code word (*(opd)) gets clobbered to 0 by a
 * mislifted store, so g_ps3_guest_caller reads code=0 -> "not registered" and the
 * game's per-flip/vblank callback never fires -> render/advance loop stalls. We
 * capture the code at Set*Handler time (OPD still valid) and restore the OPD word
 * before each invocation if it's been clobbered. */
extern u32 vm_read32(unsigned int);
static u32 s_flip_handler_code    = 0;
static u32 s_vblank_handler_code  = 0;
static void ydkj_restore_handler_opd(u32 opd, u32 code) {
    if (!getenv("YDKJ_HANDLERFIX") || !opd || !code) return;
    extern u8* vm_base; if (!vm_base) return;
    if (vm_read32(opd) == 0) {
        u8* p = vm_base + opd; p[0]=(u8)(code>>24); p[1]=(u8)(code>>16); p[2]=(u8)(code>>8); p[3]=(u8)code;
        static int _n=0; if(PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 6)) fprintf(stderr,"[HANDLERFIX] restored clobbered OPD 0x%08X code=0x%08X\n",opd,code);
    }
}
static void gcm_update_handler_mask(void)
{
    uint32_t m = 0;
    if (s_vblank_handler_opd) m |= 0x02;
    if (s_flip_handler_opd)   m |= 0x04;
    if (s_user_handler_opd)   m |= 0x80;
    g_gcm_handler_mask = m;
    if (g_gcm_driver_info_ea)
        vm_write32(g_gcm_driver_info_ea + 0x12C0, m);
}

 * Local (0xFEED0000, the default): the s_report_data slots above, read back
 * through cellGcmGetReport* / cellGcmGetReportDataAddress. Main memory
 * (0xFEED0001, or CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT_LOCATION_MAIN 0xBAD68000): the
 * report's 24-bit offset is an IO offset, and the 16-byte report goes to
 * guest memory at gcm_io2ea(offset), where the title reads it itself.
 * Killzone 3 sets 0xFEED0001 and keeps its reports in its own frame data. */

/* GET_REPORT timestamp in nanoseconds, strictly rising: two reports in one
 * walker pass must not share a time stamp or go backwards. */
static u64 gcm_report_timestamp(void)
{
    u64 t = get_timestamp_ns();
    if (t <= s_report_last_ts) t = s_report_last_ts + 1u;
    s_report_last_ts = t;
    return t;
}

/* Label area (256 labels, each u32). Labels live in GUEST memory so the
 * recompiled game can poll them via vm_read32; cellGcmGetLabelAddress returns a
 * guest address into this window (16-byte spaced as on hardware). A host array
 * pointer would be read as a guest offset and land out of bounds. */
#define GCM_LABEL_GUEST_BASE  (VM_HLE_INJECT_BASE + 0x0000u)
#define GCM_LABEL_STRIDE      0x10u
static u32 s_labels[CELL_GCM_MAX_LABEL_COUNT];

/* GCM_LABEL_WATCH=<byte offset>: emit only semaphore writes targeting this
 * label slot. This keeps a stuck label poll diagnosable without tracing the
 * whole RSX method stream. */
static u32 gcm_label_watch_offset(void)
{
    static int initialized = 0;
    static u32 offset = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    if (!initialized) {
        const char* e = getenv("GCM_LABEL_WATCH");
        if (e && *e) offset = (u32)strtoul(e, NULL, 0);
        initialized = 1;
    }
    return offset;
}

/* GCM control register (put/get/ref). This MUST live in guest memory: the title
 * takes the pointer from cellGcmGetControlRegister, writes `put` when it kicks
 * the FIFO, and spins reading `get`/`ref` to know the RSX has caught up. A host
 * pointer would be read through vm_base as a guest address and never update, so
 * every FIFO-space / cellGcmFinish wait would hang. Placed just past the 256
 * label slots (0x03000000..0x03001000). Fields are big-endian (vm_write32). */
#define GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR (VM_HLE_INJECT_BASE + 0x2000u)

/* Synthetic guest code EA for the FIFO command-buffer-full callback. The title's
 * inline gcmReserve calls context->callback(context, count) when `current` nears
 * `end`; we point the context's callback OPD at this EA and register it in the
 * PPU function table (ppu_sysprx.cpp: hle_gcm_callback) so the indirect call
 * routes back into cellGcm_fifo_recycle(). Lives in the injected control page,
 * never real guest code. MUST match GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA there. */
#define GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA (VM_HLE_INJECT_BASE + 0x2F00u)

/* EA the ticker's RSX drain has consumed up to. Exposed so the wrap callback can
 * wait for the RSX to catch up before recycling the ring (else the frame's
 * just-written commands are lost). Updated in cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo. */
volatile u32 g_gcm_fifo_drained_ea = 0;

/* The guest variable cellGcmInit's ctx_out pointed at -- the title's own
 * gCellGcmCurrentContext. A title that switches to a command buffer of its own
 * does it by repointing this, and until something reads it back the runtime has
 * no way to notice. GCM_CTXDBG=1 reports it. */
static u32 s_gcm_ctx_out_ea = 0;

/* Set by cellGcm_syscall_bringup: this run reaches RSX through the lv2 sys_rsx_*
 * syscalls (libs/video/sys_rsx.c) rather than through the HLE cellGcm* imports. */
static int s_gcm_syscall_mode = 0;

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Internal helpers
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* Populate the offset table entries for an IO mapping */
static void populate_offset_table(u32 ea, u32 io, u32 size)
{
    /*
     * The offset table uses 1MB pages (20-bit shift).
     * ioAddress[ea >> 20] = io >> 20   (EA -> IO offset)
     * eaAddress[io >> 20] = ea >> 20   (IO offset -> EA)
     */
    /* Round UP: a mapping is described by whole 1MB table entries, so a size
     * that is not a multiple of 1MB still needs its final partial page mapped.
     * Truncating dropped that page -- and dropped the mapping ENTIRELY for any
     * size below 1MB (pages == 0) -- after which cellGcmResolveOffset finds no
     * IO entry and falls back to VRAM, where the guest never wrote anything. */
    u32 pages = (size + 0xFFFFFu) >> 20;  /* number of 1MB pages, rounded up */
    u32 ea_page = ea >> 20;
    u32 io_page = io >> 20;

    for (u32 i = 0; i < pages && (ea_page + i) < 65536 && (io_page + i) < 65536; i++) {
        s_io_address_table[ea_page + i] = (u16)(io_page + i);
        s_ea_address_table[io_page + i] = (u16)(ea_page + i);
    }

    /* cellGcmGetOffsetTable returns guest pointers to these arrays. Keep the
     * guest-visible copy coherent with the host lookup tables after every map;
     * titles commonly cache the pointers and index them directly in libgcm. */
    const u32 ea_end = ea_page + pages;
    const u32 io_end = io_page + pages;
    for (u32 page = ea_page; page < ea_end && page < GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_PAGES; ++page)
        vm_write16(GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_IO_ADDR + page * 2,
                   s_io_address_table[page]);
    for (u32 page = io_page; page < io_end && page < GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_PAGES; ++page)
        vm_write16(GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_EA_ADDR + page * 2,
                   s_ea_address_table[page]);
}

/* Clear offset table entries for an IO mapping */
static void clear_offset_table(u32 ea, u32 io, u32 size)
{
    u32 pages = (size + 0xFFFFFu) >> 20;
    u32 ea_page = ea >> 20;
    u32 io_page = io >> 20;

    for (u32 i = 0; i < pages && (ea_page + i) < 65536 && (io_page + i) < 65536; i++) {
        s_io_address_table[ea_page + i] = 0xFFFF;
        s_ea_address_table[io_page + i] = 0xFFFF;
    }

    /* Unmaps are visible to guest code through the same cached table pointers. */
    const u32 ea_end = ea_page + pages;
    const u32 io_end = io_page + pages;
    for (u32 page = ea_page; page < ea_end && page < GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_PAGES; ++page)
        vm_write16(GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_IO_ADDR + page * 2,
                   s_io_address_table[page]);
    for (u32 page = io_page; page < io_end && page < GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_PAGES; ++page)
        vm_write16(GCM_OFFSET_TABLE_EA_ADDR + page * 2,
                   s_ea_address_table[page]);
}

/* Find an IO mapping by EA */
static IoMapping* find_mapping_by_ea(u32 ea)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS; i++) {
        if (s_io_mappings[i].active && s_io_mappings[i].ea == ea)
            return &s_io_mappings[i];
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* Find an IO mapping by IO offset */
/* RPCS3's cellGcmUnmapEaIoAddress/IoAddress ignore the byte offset within a
 * 1 MiB page, but identify an unmap by the first page of a mapped range. */
static IoMapping* find_mapping_starting_at_ea_page(u32 ea)
{
    const u32 page = ea >> 20;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS; i++)
        if (s_io_mappings[i].active && (s_io_mappings[i].ea >> 20) == page)
            return &s_io_mappings[i];
    return NULL;
}

static IoMapping* find_mapping_starting_at_io_page(u32 io)
{
    const u32 page = io >> 20;
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS; i++)
        if (s_io_mappings[i].active && (s_io_mappings[i].io >> 20) == page)
            return &s_io_mappings[i];
    return NULL;
}

/* Find a free IO mapping slot */
static IoMapping* find_free_mapping(void)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS; i++) {
        if (!s_io_mappings[i].active)
            return &s_io_mappings[i];
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* Valid tiled pitch sizes (power-of-two aligned, common RSX values) */
static const u32 s_valid_pitches[] = {
    0x0200, 0x0300, 0x0400, 0x0500, 0x0600, 0x0700, 0x0800,
    0x0A00, 0x0C00, 0x0D00, 0x0E00, 0x1000, 0x1400, 0x1800,
    0x1A00, 0x1C00, 0x2000, 0x2800, 0x3000, 0x3400, 0x3800,
    0x4000, 0x5000, 0x6000, 0x6800, 0x7000, 0x8000, 0xA000,
    0xC000, 0xD000, 0xE000, 0x10000
};
static const int s_valid_pitch_count = sizeof(s_valid_pitches) / sizeof(s_valid_pitches[0]);

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * API implementations -- Initialization
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* NID: 0xB2E761D4 */
s32 cellGcmInit(u32 cmdSize, u32 ioSize, u32 ioAddress)
{
    printf("[cellGcmSys] Init(cmdSize=0x%X, ioSize=0x%X, ioAddr=0x%08X)\n",
           cmdSize, ioSize, ioAddress);

    if (s_gcm_initialized) {
        printf("[cellGcmSys] WARNING: already initialized\n");
        return CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE;
    }

    memset(s_display_buffers, 0, sizeof(s_display_buffers));
    memset(s_display_buffer_set, 0, sizeof(s_display_buffer_set));
    memset(&s_config, 0, sizeof(s_config));
    memset(&s_control, 0, sizeof(s_control));
    memset(s_io_mappings, 0, sizeof(s_io_mappings));
    memset(s_tiles, 0, sizeof(s_tiles));
    memset(s_zcull, 0, sizeof(s_zcull));
    memset(s_report_data, 0, sizeof(s_report_data));
    memset(s_zcull_report_accum, 0, sizeof(s_zcull_report_accum));
    s_report_dma = CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_MEMORY_FRAME_BUFFER;
    memset(s_labels, 0, sizeof(s_labels));
    memset(s_io_address_table, 0xFF, sizeof(s_io_address_table));
    memset(s_ea_address_table, 0xFF, sizeof(s_ea_address_table));
    gcm_publish_offset_tables();

    /*
     * Populate a plausible configuration.
     * In a real implementation these would reflect actual allocated memory.
     */
    s_config.localAddress    = 0xC0000000;  /* typical RSX local mem base */
    s_config.localSize       = 256 * 1024 * 1024;  /* 256 MB */
    s_config.ioAddress       = ioAddress;
    s_config.ioSize          = ioSize;
    s_config.memoryFrequency = 650000000;   /* 650 MHz */
    s_config.coreFrequency   = 500000000;   /* 500 MHz */

    s_local_mem_allocated = 0;
    s_io_mapping_count = 0;
    /* Unmapped = 0xFFFF. The tables are static (zero-initialized), so without
     * this every unmapped EA page silently aliased io page 0 (and vice versa),
     * producing plausible-but-wrong offsets instead of a translation failure. */
    memset(s_io_address_table, 0xFF, sizeof(s_io_address_table));
    memset(s_ea_address_table, 0xFF, sizeof(s_ea_address_table));
    s_current_display_buffer_id = 0;
    s_flip_fifo_present_pending = 0;
    s_flip_api_present_pending = 0;
    s_flip_direct_pending = 0;
    s_fifo_flips_queued = 0;
    s_fifo_flips_reached = 0;
    s_fifo_flip_events = 0;
    s_fifo_flip_events_completed = 0;
    s_flip_request_count = 0;
    s_flip_handler = NULL;
    s_vblank_handler = NULL;
    s_user_handler = NULL;
    s_second_v_handler = NULL;
    s_last_flip_time = get_timestamp_ns();
    s_flip_status = CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_DONE;
    s_flip_mode = CELL_GCM_DISPLAY_VSYNC;
    s_debug_level = CELL_GCM_DEBUG_LEVEL0;
    s_vblank_count = 0;
    s_io_map_reserved = 0;
    s_io_alloc_next = 0;
    s_default_fifo_mode = 0;
    s_graphics_handler = NULL;
    s_queue_handler = NULL;
    s_second_v_frequency = 0;
    s_vblank_frequency = 0;
    GCM_USER_STORE(0);
    GCM_USER_PENDING_STORE(0);

    /* Set up the initial IO mapping for the command buffer region */
    if (ioAddress != 0 && ioSize > 0) {
        populate_offset_table(ioAddress, 0, ioSize);

        s_io_mappings[0].ea     = ioAddress;
        s_io_mappings[0].io     = 0;
        s_io_mappings[0].size   = ioSize;
        s_io_mappings[0].active = 1;
        s_io_mapping_count = 1;
    }

    /* Zero the guest-visible control register (put/get/ref). */
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, 0);
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 4, 0);
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 8, 0);

    /* Watch SPU DMA for pushbuffers. A title that builds its command stream on
     * an SPU never tells libgcm where that stream is, so the write is the only
     * evidence of it -- see gcm_note_spu_put. Costs one NULL check per SPU DMA
     * for titles that do not. */
    { extern void (*g_spu_put_hook)(u32 ea, u32 size);
      void gcm_note_spu_put(u32 ea, u32 size);       /* defined with the walker */
      void gcm_forget_spu_blocks(void);
      gcm_forget_spu_blocks();
      g_spu_put_hook = gcm_note_spu_put; }

    s_gcm_initialized = 1;
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* RPCS3_REFERENCE_REVIEW: cellGcmInitSystemMode stores the mode for the
 * subsequent GCM setup. Mode 1 selects the 512 MiB RSX I/O address space;
 * other values use the default 256 MiB space. */
s32 cellGcmInitSystemMode(u64 mode)
{
    s_io_address_space_size = mode == 1u
        ? GCM_IO_ADDRESS_SPACE_SIZE_512MB
        : GCM_IO_ADDRESS_SPACE_SIZE_DEFAULT;
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* Reusable _cellGcmInitBody core (NID 0x15BAE46B). See cellGcmSys.h for why the
 * guest vm is injected as callbacks. The CellGcmContextData layout here is the
 * one proven in the shipping Simpsons port (begin@0/end@4/current@8/callback@C);
 * getting it wrong makes the game read `current` as the callback OPD and stall
 * in cellGcmFlush. The command buffer is the start of the game's IO region. */
u32 cellGcmSetupContext(u32 ctx_out_addr, u32 cmdSize, u32 ioSize, u32 ioAddress,
                        CellGcmGuestAlloc galloc, CellGcmGuestWrite32 gwrite32)
{
    if (cmdSize < 0x10000)
        cmdSize = 0x10000;

    /* PSL1GHT's gcmInitBody passes ioAddress = 0, expecting gcm to allocate the
     * IO region itself (the official SDK has the app allocate and pass it).
     * Taking the 0 literally put the FIFO command buffer at guest address 0 --
     * the guest then wrote its command stream over low memory and every offset
     * resolution failed. Allocate a guest region of ioSize instead. */
    if (ioAddress == 0 && galloc)
        ioAddress = galloc(ioSize ? ioSize : 0x100000, 0x100000);

    cellGcmInit(cmdSize, ioSize, ioAddress);

    /* The first 4 KiB of the default IO allocation is reserved by libgcm.
     * RPCS3's _cellGcmInitBody starts commands at ioAddress + 4096 too.
     * Starting at zero lets a ring wrap execute reserved data as commands. */
    u32 cmdbuf = ioAddress + 0x1000u;
    u32 cdata  = galloc ? galloc(16, 16) : 0;
    if (cdata && gwrite32) {
        gwrite32(cdata + 0x0, cmdbuf);              /* begin   */
        gwrite32(cdata + 0x4, ioAddress + cmdSize - 4u); /* reserve tail JUMP */
        gwrite32(cdata + 0x8, cmdbuf);              /* current */
        /* Command-buffer-full callback: a guest OPD {func, toc} routed to
         * hle_gcm_callback -> cellGcm_fifo_recycle. Without a real callback the
         * ring never recycles and the FIFO wedges once `current` reaches `end`. */
        u32 opd = galloc ? galloc(8, 8) : 0;
        if (opd) {
            gwrite32(opd + 0x0, GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA);  /* func EA */
            gwrite32(opd + 0x4, 0);                              /* toc (unused) */
            gwrite32(cdata + 0xC, opd);                          /* callback OPD */
        } else {
            gwrite32(cdata + 0xC, 0);
        }
        if (ctx_out_addr)
            gwrite32(ctx_out_addr, cdata);          /* *context = &ctxdata */
        s_gcm_ctx_out_ea = ctx_out_addr;   /* the title's gCellGcmCurrentContext */
        s_gcm_context_ea = cdata;                   /* RSX drains commands from here */
        /* cellGcmInit mapped the IO allocation at offset zero. Both ends of
         * the FIFO must begin at the first command, not its reserved prefix. */
        cellGcm_syscall_set_fifo(0x1000u, 0x1000u);
    }
    return cdata;
}

s32 cellGcmGetConfiguration(CellGcmConfig* config)
{
    /* `config` is a GUEST address; write the 6 u32 fields big-endian via
     * vm_write32 (a raw *config = s_config faults / is host-endian). The game
     * reads localAddress/localSize from here to lay out VRAM framebuffers. */
    uint32_t cfg = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)config;
    if (!cfg)
        return CELL_GCM_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE;

    vm_write32(cfg +  0, s_config.localAddress);
    vm_write32(cfg +  4, s_config.ioAddress);
    vm_write32(cfg +  8, s_config.localSize);
    vm_write32(cfg + 12, s_config.ioSize);
    vm_write32(cfg + 16, s_config.memoryFrequency);
    vm_write32(cfg + 20, s_config.coreFrequency);
    return CELL_OK;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Command buffer control
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* NID: 0x8572A8E0 */
CellGcmControl* cellGcmGetControlRegister(void)
{
    /* Return the GUEST address of the control register (not &s_control, a host
     * pointer). The recompiled title reads/writes it through vm_base, so it must
     * be a guest EA for put/get/ref to actually flow. */
    return (CellGcmControl*)(uintptr_t)GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Display / flip
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* NID: 0xDB23E867 */
u32 cellGcmGetCurrentField(void)
{
    /* Returns 0 or 1 for interlaced; always 0 for progressive. */
    return 0;
}

/* NID: 0xA53D12AE */
void cellGcmSetFlipMode(u32 mode)
{
    printf("[cellGcmSys] SetFlipMode(mode=%u)\n", mode);
    s_flip_mode = mode;
}

/* NID: 0xC44D8F34 */
void cellGcmSetWaitFlip(void)
{
    /* Block until the pending flip completes (the present thread marks it done
     * via cellGcmTickFlip, ~once per display refresh). This throttles the title
     * to vsync; without it the guest loops unthrottled and many frames batch
