===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_depth24_rounding.c =====
/* Exercise production depth-to-guest storage through actual texture lookup,
 * dirty tracking and cache refresh; expected quantized bytes are literal.
 * No game programs, original assets or graphics API are used. */
#define main original_engine_test_main
#include "test_rsx_draw_engine.c"
#undef main
#include <math.h>

#define PACK_W 12u
#define PACK_H 2u
#define PACK_PITCH 80u
static float samples[PACK_W];
static const u32 expected24[PACK_W]={0xFFFFFF,0xFFFFFE,0xFFFFFD,0x800000,0,0,0,0xFFFFFF,0xFFFFFF,0,0xBFFFFF,0x400000};
static const u16 expected16[PACK_W]={0xFFFF,0xFFFF,0xFFFF,0x8000,0,0,0,0xFFFF,0xFFFF,0,0xBFFF,0x4000};
static u8 uploaded[PACK_W*PACK_H*4];
static rsx_be_format uploaded_format;
static int changed,read_w,read_h;
static u32 sample_at(u32 x,u32 y) { return (y+changed)&1u ? PACK_W-1u-x:x; }
static int varied_depth(void* user,u32 depth,u32 x,u32 y,u32 w,u32 h,float* out,u32 pitch)
{
    (void)user;(void)depth;stub.n_depth_readback++;read_w=w;read_h=h;
    if(x || y || w!=PACK_W || h!=PACK_H || pitch!=PACK_W*sizeof(float))return -1;
    for(u32 row=0;row<h;row++)for(u32 col=0;col<w;col++)
        *(float*)((u8*)out+row*pitch+col*sizeof(float))=samples[sample_at(col,row)];
    return 0;
}
static u32 capture_create(void* user,rsx_be_format fmt,u32 w,u32 h,u32 mips,u32 faces,u32 remap,u32 rsx_fmt)
{
    uploaded_format=fmt;return stub_texture_create(user,fmt,w,h,mips,faces,remap,rsx_fmt);
}
static void capture_upload(void* user,u32 texture,u32 face,u32 mip,u32 w,u32 h,const void* data,u32 pitch,u32 rows)
{
    stub_texture_upload(user,texture,face,mip,w,h,data,pitch,rows);
    u32 bpp=uploaded_format==RSX_BE_FMT_R16?2u:4u;
    if(mip || w!=PACK_W || h!=PACK_H || pitch!=PACK_W*bpp || rows!=PACK_H)return;
    for(u32 y=0;y<h;y++)memcpy(uploaded+y*PACK_W*bpp,(const u8*)data+y*pitch,PACK_W*bpp);
}
static void check_guest(u32 bpp)
{
    const u8* p=vm_base+GUEST_LOCAL_EA+ZETA_OFFSET;
    for(u32 y=0;y<PACK_H;y++)for(u32 x=0;x<PACK_W;x++){
        u32 want=bpp==4?expected24[sample_at(x,y)]:expected16[sample_at(x,y)];
        const u8* q=p+y*PACK_PITCH+x*bpp;
        int ok=bpp==4?(q[0]==(want>>16) && q[1]==((want>>8)&255) && q[2]==(want&255) && q[3]==0):(q[0]==(want>>8) && q[1]==(want&255));
        CHECK(ok,"depth%u pixel(%u,%u) has literal big-endian depth %06X and zero stencil (actual %02X %02X %02X %02X)",bpp==4?24:16,x,y,want,q[0],q[1],q[2],q[3]);
    }
    int intact=1;
    for(int i=-16;i<(int)(PACK_PITCH*3);i++){
        int used=i>=0 && i<(int)(PACK_PITCH*PACK_H) && i%(int)PACK_PITCH<(int)(PACK_W*bpp);
        if(!used)intact &= p[i]==0xA6;
    }
    CHECK(intact,"depth%u preserves prefix, row padding and rows outside used ROI",bpp==4?24:16);
}
static void check_upload(u32 bpp)
{
    int ok=1;
    for(u32 y=0;y<PACK_H;y++)for(u32 x=0;x<PACK_W;x++){
        u32 want=bpp==4?expected24[sample_at(x,y)]:expected16[sample_at(x,y)];
        const u8* q=uploaded+(y*PACK_W+x)*bpp;
        if(bpp==4)ok &= q[0]==((want>>8)&255) && q[1]==(want&255) && q[2]==0 && q[3]==(want>>16);
        else {u16 got;memcpy(&got,q,sizeof got);ok &= got==want;}
    }
    CHECK(ok,"depth%u texture upload decodes the newly stored guest bytes",bpp==4?24:16);
}
static void packing_case(u32 bpp)
{
    rsx_draw_backend be=g_stub_backend;be.depth_readback=varied_depth;be.texture_create=capture_create;be.texture_upload=capture_upload;
    memset(&stub,0,sizeof stub);rsx_draw_engine_set_backend(&be);
    CHECK(rsx_draw_engine_init(32,8)==0,"packing engine initializes");
    m(M_CONTEXT_DMA_COLOR_A,DMA_LOCAL);m(M_SURFACE_CLIP_H,PACK_W<<16);m(M_SURFACE_CLIP_V,PACK_H<<16);
    m(M_VTXFMT,2u|(4u<<4)|(16u<<8));m(M_VTXBUF_OFFSET,0x80000000u|VTX_OFFSET);
    m(M_CONTEXT_DMA_ZETA,DMA_LOCAL);m(M_SURFACE_FORMAT,8u|((bpp==4?2u:1u)<<5));
    m(M_ZETA_OFFSET,ZETA_OFFSET);m(M_ZETA_PITCH,PACK_PITCH);m(M_COLOR_A_OFFSET,0x90000u);
    u8* guest=vm_base+GUEST_LOCAL_EA+ZETA_OFFSET;memset(guest-16,0xA6,PACK_PITCH*3+16);
    bind_texture_unit(RSX_LOCATION_LOCAL,ZETA_OFFSET);m(M_TEX_UNIT+0x18,(PACK_W<<16)|PACK_H);m(0x1840,PACK_PITCH);
    if(bpp==2)m(M_TEX_UNIT+0x04,1u|(2u<<4)|(0xB2u<<8)|(1u<<16));
    changed=0;draw_triangle();const u32 cached=stub.bound_tex[0];
    CHECK(cached && stub.n_depth_readback==0,"alias texture is cached before any depth write");
    for(int pass=0;pass<2;pass++){
        changed=pass;m(M_TEX_UNIT+0x0C,0);m(M_COLOR_A_OFFSET,ZETA_OFFSET);m(M_COLOR_MASK,0);m(M_DEPTH_TEST,1);m(M_DEPTH_WRITE,1);draw_triangle();
        m(M_COLOR_A_OFFSET,0x90000u);m(M_COLOR_MASK,0x01010101);m(M_DEPTH_TEST,0);m(M_DEPTH_WRITE,0);m(M_TEX_UNIT+0x0C,0x80000000u);
        const u32 before=stub.bound_tex[0];const int uploads=stub.n_texture_upload;draw_triangle();
        CHECK(stub.n_depth_readback==pass+1 && read_w==PACK_W && read_h==PACK_H,"dirty depth readback uses only the used ROI");
        CHECK(stub.n_texture_upload==uploads+1 && stub.bound_tex[0]!=before,"same-frame guest-byte change refreshes cached alias");
        CHECK(uploaded_format==(bpp==4?RSX_BE_FMT_R8G8B8A8:RSX_BE_FMT_R16),"alias upload uses its descriptor format");
        check_guest(bpp);check_upload(bpp);
        const u32 stable=stub.bound_tex[0];const int stable_uploads=stub.n_texture_upload;draw_triangle();
        CHECK(stub.n_depth_readback==pass+1 && stub.n_texture_upload==stable_uploads && stub.bound_tex[0]==stable,"unchanged depth reuses alias without another readback");
    }
    m(M_ZSTENCIL_CLEAR,bpp==4?0xFFFFFF00u:0xFFFFu);m(M_CLEAR_BUFFERS,1u);
    CHECK(stub.last_clear_depth==1.0f,"far-plane clear decoding remains unchanged");
    engine_down();
}
int main(void)
{
    vm_base=calloc(1,GUEST_BYTES);if(!vm_base)return 1;ppu_vm_size=GUEST_BYTES;
    for(u32 i=0;i<12;i++){u8* p=vm_base+VTX_OFFSET+i*4;p[0]=0x3F;p[1]=0x80;}
    samples[0]=1;samples[1]=nextafterf(1,0);samples[2]=nextafterf(samples[1],0);samples[3]=.5f;samples[4]=0;samples[5]=NAN;samples[6]=-.25f;samples[7]=1.25f;samples[8]=INFINITY;samples[9]=-INFINITY;samples[10]=.75f;samples[11]=.25f;
    packing_case(4);packing_case(2);free(vm_base);
    printf("depth packing: %d failures\n",g_failures);return g_failures?1:0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_fp_decompiler.c =====
/*
 * Standalone unit test for the RSX fragment-program decompiler.
 *
 * Build (no D3D12 dependency), from this directory:
 *   cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -I../../../include \
 *       test_fp_decompiler.c ../rsx_fp_decompiler.c -o test_fp
 *
 * Exercises the decode path (word swap, source swizzle/type, opcode -> HLSL,
 * dest mask, inline constants) by hand-assembling tiny programs and checking
 * the generated HLSL contains the expected expressions, then the colour
 * export selection: which register file the fragment colour comes out of, and
 * how many SV_TARGETs a program that writes more than one export gets.
 */

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L   /* setenv */
#include "../rsx_fp_decompiler.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static int g_pass = 0, g_fail = 0;

/* Store host word H into guest bytes so that rsx_fp_read_word(p) == H.
 * rsx_fp_read_word does be32-load then 16-bit half-swap, so we invert: the
 * guest stores big-endian of swap16(H). */
static void put_word(u8* p, u32 h)
{
    u32 be = (h << 16) | (h >> 16);
    p[0] = (u8)(be >> 24); p[1] = (u8)(be >> 16);
    p[2] = (u8)(be >> 8);  p[3] = (u8)(be);
}

static void put_float(u8* p, float f)
{
    u32 h; memcpy(&h, &f, 4);
    put_word(p, h);
}

static void check(const char* test, const char* hlsl, const char* needle)
{
    if (strstr(hlsl, needle)) {
        printf("[PASS] %s -- found \"%s\"\n", test, needle);
        g_pass++;
    } else {
        printf("[FAIL] %s -- missing \"%s\"\nHLSL:\n%s\n", test, needle, hlsl);
        g_fail++;
    }
}

static void check_absent(const char* test, const char* hlsl, const char* needle)
{
    if (!strstr(hlsl, needle)) {
        printf("[PASS] %s -- no \"%s\"\n", test, needle);
        g_pass++;
    } else {
        printf("[FAIL] %s -- unexpected \"%s\"\nHLSL:\n%s\n", test, needle, hlsl);
        g_fail++;
    }
}

static void check_true(const char* test, int cond)
{
    if (cond) { printf("[PASS] %s\n", test); g_pass++; }
    else      { printf("[FAIL] %s\n", test); g_fail++; }
}

/* OPDEST/SRC bit helpers (mirror the decoder's macros). */
#define OPC(x)      ((u32)(x) << 24)
#define OUTMASK_ALL (0xFu << 9)
#define END         (1u << 0)
#define OUTREG(i)   ((u32)(i) << 1)
#define OUTHALF     (1u << 7)
#define INSRC(x)    ((u32)(x) << 13)
#define TEXU(x)     ((u32)(x) << 17)
#define SWZ_IDENT   ((0u<<9)|(1u<<11)|(2u<<13)|(3u<<15))
#define T_TEMP      0u
#define T_INPUT     1u
#define T_CONST     2u
#define REG(i)      ((u32)(i) << 2)
/* The execution condition, exec_if lt/eq/gt at [18:20] with its swizzle at
 * [21:28]. All three bits set is unconditional; an all-zero source word is
 * "never", which suppresses the write -- so every instruction below carries
 * this, as a real program's does. */
#define EXEC_ALWAYS ((7u << 18) | (0u << 21) | (1u << 23) | (2u << 25) | (3u << 27))

/* SHADER_CONTROL: 0x40 exports fp32 (colour from r0/r2/r3/r4), clear exports
 * fp16 (colour from h0/h4/h6/h8). */
#define CTRL_32BIT  0x40u
#define CTRL_16BIT  0x00u

int main(void)
{
    char hlsl[16384];

    /* RSX_FP_DEBUG=<hash>:<n>:<reg>: the named register, captured after the
     * program's n-th instruction, becomes colour target 0 with alpha 1 --
     * in that program only. The variable is read once, on the first
     * decompile, so this runs first. */
    {
        u8 prog[32];
        u32 mask_xy = (1u<<9)|(1u<<10);
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x02) | mask_xy | OUTREG(1));          /* MUL r1.xy, r0, r0 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        put_word(prog + 16, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | END); /* MOV r0, COL0 */
        put_word(prog + 20, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 24, 0);
        put_word(prog + 28, 0);
        char spec[64];
        snprintf(spec, sizeof spec, "%llx:1:r1.xyyy", (unsigned long long)
                 rsx_fp_structural_hash(prog, sizeof prog, 1469598103934665603ull));
        setenv("RSX_FP_DEBUG", spec, 1);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("fp_debug_capture", hlsl,
              "r[1].xy = _v.xy; }\n"
              "    _rsx_dbg = (float4)((r[1]).xyyy);\n"
              "    { float4 _v = (float4)((saturate(input.col0)).xyzw);");
        check("fp_debug_export", hlsl, "_d.w = 1.0; r[0] = _d; h[0] = _d; }\n"
                                       "    float4 _o = r[0];");
        u8 other[16];
        memcpy(other, prog + 16, sizeof other);
        rsx_fp_decompile(other, sizeof(other), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check_absent("fp_debug_other_program", hlsl, "_rsx_dbg");
        unsetenv("RSX_FP_DEBUG");
    }

    /* Test 1: MOV r0, COL0  (write all, END). */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | END); /* MOV, COL0 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);        /* src0 = INPUT */
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        int n = rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        printf("-- test1 MOV: %d instr\n", n);
        check("mov_dest",   hlsl, "r[0].xyzw =");
        check("mov_input",  hlsl, "input.col0");
        check("mov_entry",  hlsl, "float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_TARGET {");
        check("mov_return", hlsl, "    float4 _o = r[0];\n"
                                  "    return (_o == _o) ? _o : (float4)0;\n}\n");
    }

    /* Test 2: MUL r1.xy, r0, r0  (partial write mask). */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        u32 mask_xy = (1u<<9)|(1u<<10);
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x02) | mask_xy | OUTREG(1) | END); /* MUL, dest r1 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("mul_mask", hlsl, "r[1].xy =");
        check("mul_expr", hlsl, "(r[0]).xyzw) * ((r[0]).xyzw)");
    }

    /* Test 3: MAD r0, r0, CONST, r0 with inline constant + saturate. */
    {
        u8 prog[32];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x04) | OUTMASK_ALL | (1u<<31) | END); /* MAD + SAT */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_TEMP  | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, T_CONST | SWZ_IDENT);                      /* src1 CONST */
        put_word(prog + 12, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT);
        put_float(prog + 16, 0.5f);  /* inline constant float4 */
        put_float(prog + 20, 0.25f);
        put_float(prog + 24, 0.0f);
        put_float(prog + 28, 1.0f);
        int n = rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        printf("-- test3 MAD: %d instr\n", n);
        check("mad_sat",   hlsl, "saturate(");
        check("mad_const", hlsl, "float4(0.5,0.25,0,1)");

        /* ...and the buffered variant, which hoists that constant into b1. */
        u32 nk = 0;
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_ex(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, 0,
                                     hlsl, sizeof(hlsl), &nk);
        check_true("mad_buffered_count", nk == 1);
        check("mad_buffered", hlsl, "fp_constants[0]");
    }

    /* Test 4: TEX r0, TC0 from texture unit 3. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(3) | END); /* TEX */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("tex_sample", hlsl, "rsx_tex[3].Sample(rsx_samp[3]");
        check("tex_coord",  hlsl, "input.tc0");
    }

    /* Test 5: negate + abs on a source (MOV r0, -|r1|). */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | END);
        put_word(prog + 4, T_TEMP | REG(1) | SWZ_IDENT | (1u<<17) | (1u<<29)
                           | EXEC_ALWAYS); /* neg+abs */
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("neg_abs", hlsl, "-(abs((r[1]).xyzw))");
    }

    /* Test 6: the export register file follows SHADER_CONTROL, not whichever
     * temp was written. A program writing h0 exports h0 with 16-bit exports
     * and r0 with 32-bit ones. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | OUTHALF | END);
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_16BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("h0_16bit", hlsl, "float4 _o = h[0];");
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("h0_32bit", hlsl, "float4 _o = r[0];");
    }

    /* Test 7: MRT. The second colour export is r2 with 32-bit exports and h4
     * with 16-bit ones, so the same instruction is a second render target in
     * one mode and an ordinary temp write in the other. A deferred pass
     * writing both planes has to come out as a struct of SV_TARGETs; a
     * material shader accumulating into r2 while its colour goes to h0 must
     * not. */
    {
        u8 prog[32];
        put_word(prog +  0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | OUTREG(0));
        put_word(prog +  4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog +  8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        put_word(prog + 16, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(2) | OUTREG(2) | END);
        put_word(prog + 20, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 24, 0);
        put_word(prog + 28, 0);

        int n = rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        printf("-- test7 MRT: %d instr\n", n);
        check("mrt_struct",  hlsl, "struct PSOutput {\n"
                                   "    float4 t0 : SV_TARGET0;\n"
                                   "    float4 t1 : SV_TARGET1;\n"
                                   "};\n");
        check("mrt_entry",   hlsl, "PSOutput main(PSInput input) {");
        check("mrt_t0",      hlsl, "float4 _o0 = r[0];\n"
                                   "    _out.t0 = (_o0 == _o0) ? _o0 : (float4)0;");
        check("mrt_t1",      hlsl, "float4 _o1 = r[2];\n"
                                   "    _out.t1 = (_o1 == _o1) ? _o1 : (float4)0;");
        check("mrt_return",  hlsl, "    return _out;\n}\n");
        check_absent("mrt_no_target2", hlsl, "SV_TARGET2");

        /* ...and the alpha test still patches it, testing target 0's alpha. */
        check_true("mrt_alpha_patched",
                   rsx_fp_apply_alpha_test(hlsl, sizeof(hlsl), 0x204u, 0.5f) == 1);
        check("mrt_alpha_type", hlsl, "PSOutput _rsx_out = _out;");
        check("mrt_alpha_cmp",  hlsl, "if (!(_rsx_out.t0.a > _rsx_alpha_ref)) discard;");

        /* The same program under 16-bit exports: r2 is a plain temp there, so
         * the colour is h0 alone and nothing about the output changes. */
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_16BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check_absent("mrt_16bit_single", hlsl, "PSOutput");
        check("mrt_16bit_h0", hlsl, "float4 _o = h[0];");
    }

    /* Test 8: all four exports, and the highest written one decides how many
     * targets come out -- r3 alone still declares SV_TARGET0 through 2. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | OUTREG(3) | END);
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("r3_target0", hlsl, "float4 t0 : SV_TARGET0;");
        check("r3_target2", hlsl, "float4 t2 : SV_TARGET2;");
        check("r3_reads",   hlsl, "float4 _o2 = r[3];");
        check_absent("r3_no_target3", hlsl, "SV_TARGET3");
    }

    /* Test 9: the structural hash separates programs that differ only in
     * which export register they write -- so a pipeline cache keyed on it
     * cannot hand an MRT program the single-target program's shader. It is
     * the instruction bytes that are hashed, and the destination register is
     * one of them; nothing had to be added for the MRT case. */
    {
        u8 single[16], mrt[16];
        put_word(single + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | OUTREG(0) | END);
        put_word(single + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(single + 8, 0);
        put_word(single + 12, 0);
        memcpy(mrt, single, sizeof mrt);
        put_word(mrt + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | OUTREG(2) | END);

        const u64 seed = 1469598103934665603ull;
        const u64 hs = rsx_fp_structural_hash(single, sizeof single, seed);
        const u64 hm = rsx_fp_structural_hash(mrt, sizeof mrt, seed);
        check_true("hash_nonzero", hs != 0 && hm != 0);
        check_true("hash_distinguishes_mrt", hs != hm);
        check_true("hash_stable",
                   hs == rsx_fp_structural_hash(single, sizeof single, seed));
    }

    /* Test 10: IFE with an else branch. The IFE's SRC1/SRC2 hold the else and
     * end addresses in words; each side must land in its own HLSL block, not
     * run one after the other (Crazy Taxi's uber shader drew the city black
     * that way). @0 IFE(cc0.x > 0) else=@32 end=@48; @16 MOV r0,COL0;
     * @32 MOV r0,COL1; @48 LIF r1,r0 END. */
    {
        u8 prog[64];
        const u32 exec_gt_x = (1u << 20);   /* exec_if gr, cond swizzle x */
        put_word(prog +  0, OPC(0x02));
        put_word(prog +  4, exec_gt_x);
        put_word(prog +  8, (1u << 31) | (32u >> 2));   /* branch, else */
        put_word(prog + 12, 48u >> 2);                  /* end */
        put_word(prog + 16, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1));
        put_word(prog + 20, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 24, 0);
        put_word(prog + 28, 0);
        put_word(prog + 32, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(2));
        put_word(prog + 36, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 40, 0);
        put_word(prog + 44, 0);
        put_word(prog + 48, OPC(0x3C) | OUTMASK_ALL | OUTREG(1) | END);
        put_word(prog + 52, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 56, 0);
        put_word(prog + 60, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        const char* ife  = strstr(hlsl, "    if (cc0.x > 0.0) {\n");
        const char* then = strstr(hlsl, "input.col0");
        const char* els  = strstr(hlsl, "    } else {\n");
        const char* alt  = strstr(hlsl, "input.col1");
        const char* lif  = strstr(hlsl, "float4(1.0, ");
        check_true("ife_order", ife && then && els && alt && lif &&
                                ife < then && then < els && els < alt && alt < lif);
        check_absent("ife_not_skipped", hlsl, "flow-control op skipped");
        check_absent("lif_handled", hlsl, "unhandled FP opcode");
    }

    /* A unit bound to a 3D texture (SET_TEXTURE_FORMAT dimension 3) is
     * declared Texture3D and sampled with three coordinates; TXP divides
     * them by w. inFAMOUS 2's occlusion volumes look up an 8x8x8 cone LUT. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        u32 nk = 0;
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | END); /* TEX TC0 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_vol_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, 1u,
                                                             NULL, NULL, NULL, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("vol_decl",   hlsl, "Texture3D   rsx_tex0 : register(t0);");
        check("vol_sample", hlsl, "rsx_tex0.Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xyz)");
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x18) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | END); /* TXP TC0 */
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_vol_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, 1u,
                                                             NULL, NULL, NULL, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("vol_txp", hlsl, "rsx_tex0.Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xyz / ((input.tc0).xyzw).w)");
        /* No volume units: the array declaration and 2D sample as before. */
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | END);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_vol_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, 0,
                                                             NULL, NULL, NULL, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("vol_none", hlsl, "rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy)");
    }

    /* A 4096-byte program fits the D3D12 caller's input bound, but its
     * predicated, CC-writing instructions expand beyond 32 KiB of HLSL.
     * Assemble it here instead of depending on a captured game shader. */
    {
        enum { INSTRUCTION_COUNT = 256 };
        u8 prog[INSTRUCTION_COUNT * 16];
        static char backend_hlsl[RSX_FP_HLSL_BUFFER_SIZE];
        for (int i = 0; i < INSTRUCTION_COUNT; i++) {
            u8* ins = prog + i * 16;
            u32 end = i == INSTRUCTION_COUNT - 1 ? END : 0u;
            u32 opcode = i == 0 ? OPC(0x01) : OPC(0x04);
            u32 condition = i == 0 ? EXEC_ALWAYS : (1u << 20);
            put_word(ins + 0, opcode | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) |
                             (1u << 8) | end); /* MOV/MAD r0, set CC0 */
            put_word(ins + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | condition);
            put_word(ins + 8, T_TEMP | REG(0) | SWZ_IDENT);
            put_word(ins + 12, T_TEMP | REG(1) | SWZ_IDENT);
        }
        int n = rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), RSX_FP_CTRL_AUTO,
                                 backend_hlsl, sizeof(backend_hlsl));
        printf("-- source capacity: %d instr, %zu HLSL bytes\n",
               n, strlen(backend_hlsl));
        check_true("backend_source_capacity", n == INSTRUCTION_COUNT);
        check_true("source_exceeds_old_capacity", strlen(backend_hlsl) > 32768u);
        check("large_program_return", backend_hlsl, "return (_o == _o) ? _o");
    }

    /* A predicated write is a select, not a blend: MOV r0, COL0 executed
     * only where CC0 > 0 must keep r0 bit for bit in the other components.
     * lerp(r0, v, mask) is arithmetic, so an Inf/NaN in either operand
     * leaks into the components the condition leaves alone. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | END); /* MOV r0, COL0 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | (1u << 20) |          /* exec_if gt */
                           (0u << 21) | (1u << 23) | (2u << 25) | (3u << 27));
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("pred_select", hlsl,
              "r[0].xyzw = (_p.xyzw != 0.0) ? _v.xyzw : r[0].xyzw;");
        check_absent("pred_no_lerp", hlsl, "lerp(");
    }

    /* Depth export: SHADER_CONTROL bits 1-3 (0xE) make r1.z the fragment
     * depth. The program must declare SV_Depth and write r1.z, clamped,
     * even with a single colour target; without those bits it keeps the
     * single float4 return. */
    {
        u8 prog[32];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | OUTREG(1) | INSRC(4)); /* MOV r1, TC0 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        put_word(prog + 16, OPC(0x01) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(1) | END);     /* MOV r0, COL0 */
        put_word(prog + 20, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 24, 0);
        put_word(prog + 28, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT | 0xEu, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("depth_export_semantic", hlsl, "    float depth : SV_Depth;\n");
        check("depth_export_entry",    hlsl, "PSOutput main(PSInput input) {");
        check("depth_export_colour",   hlsl, "_out.t0 = (_o0 == _o0) ? _o0 : (float4)0;");
        check("depth_export_value",    hlsl, "    float _d = r[1].z;\n"
                                             "    _out.depth = (_d == _d) ? saturate(_d) : 0.0;\n");
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check_absent("no_depth_export_semantic", hlsl, "SV_Depth");
        check("no_depth_export_entry", hlsl, "float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_TARGET {");
    }

    /* Sign expansion: a TEX on a unit whose SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS asks for the
     * biased unsigned remap returns the masked lanes re-centred, and with
     * EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) as x*2-1 (RPCS3
     * _process_texel). inFAMOUS 2's deferred composite reads its normals
     * G-buffer that way; read unexpanded, normalize() ran on 0..1 encodings
     * and every normal leaned towards (1,1,1). */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        u8 expand[16] = {0};
        u32 nk = 0;
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | (1u << 21) | END); /* TEX TC0, EXP_TEX */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        expand[0] = 0x7;   /* R, G, B lanes signed */
        check_true("expand_units", rsx_fp_texture_expand_units(prog, sizeof prog, expand) == 1u);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, NULL,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_wrapped", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 15u, true)");
        check("expand_helper",  hlsl, "float4 _rsx_expand_input(float4 v, uint mask, bool bx2)");
        check("expand_math",    hlsl, "v * 2.0 - 1.0");

        expand[0] = 0;     /* the unit is not biased: _bx2 still expands every lane */
        check_true("expand_units_none", rsx_fp_texture_expand_units(prog, sizeof prog, expand) == 0u);
        check_true("bx2_units", rsx_fp_texture_bx2_units(prog, sizeof prog) == 1u);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, NULL,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_bx2_unbiased", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 15u, true)");
        /* ...and the older entry point, with no masks, is byte-identical. */
        char plain[16384];
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, NULL,
                                                  plain, sizeof plain, &nk);
        check_true("expand_old_entry_identical", strcmp(plain, hlsl) == 0);

        /* Biased but no EXP_TEX bit: the fetch still re-centres (RPCS3 applies
         * the remap to every read; only the formula and gamma differ). */
        expand[0] = 0x7;
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | END);
        check_true("expand_units_nobit", rsx_fp_texture_expand_units(prog, sizeof prog, expand) == 1u);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, NULL,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_nobit_wrapped", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 7u, false)");
        check("expand_nobit_math",    hlsl, "(floor(v * 255.0 + 0.5) - 128.0) / 127.0");

        /* Gamma lanes are decoded, not re-centred: gamma rgb + biased rgba
         * leaves the expansion with the alpha lane only, around the gamma. */
        u8 gamma[16] = {0}; gamma[0] = 0x7; expand[0] = 0xF;
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, gamma,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_after_gamma", hlsl,
              "_rsx_expand_input(_rsx_gamma_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 7u), 8u, false)");
        /* Gamma on every biased lane: nothing left to expand. */
        gamma[0] = 0xF;
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, gamma,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check_absent("expand_all_gamma", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex");
        /* With EXP_TEX, gamma steps aside and every biased lane is x*2-1. */
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | (1u << 21) | END);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, gamma,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_bx2_over_gamma", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 15u, true)");
        check_absent("expand_bx2_no_gamma", hlsl, "_rsx_gamma_input(");
        /* Bit 4 (16-bit channels) rides along in the mask argument. */
        expand[0] = 0x13;
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(4) | TEXU(0) | END);
        rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex(prog, sizeof prog, CTRL_32BIT, 0, NULL, NULL,
                                                         expand, hlsl, sizeof hlsl, &nk);
        check("expand_16bit", hlsl, "_rsx_expand_input(rsx_tex[0].Sample(rsx_samp[0], ((input.tc0).xyzw).xy), 19u, false)");
    }

    /* SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) on a texcoord read multiplies the input
     * by 1/w (RPCS3 FragmentProgramDecompiler: "Perspective correct flag
     * multiplies the result by 1/w"). inFAMOUS 2's water writes uv*w from the
     * vertex program and samples TC2 with the flag set; read raw, uv*w lands
     * far outside the screen copy and the river samples black. */
    {
        u8 prog[16];
        put_word(prog + 0, OPC(0x17) | OUTMASK_ALL | INSRC(6) | TEXU(0) | END); /* TEX TC2 */
        put_word(prog + 4, T_INPUT | SWZ_IDENT | EXEC_ALWAYS);
        put_word(prog + 8, 0);
        put_word(prog + 12, 1u << 31);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("persp_tc_scaled", hlsl, "(input.tc2 * _rsx_inv_w(input.position))");
        check("persp_helper",    hlsl, "#define _rsx_inv_w(p)");

        put_word(prog + 12, 0);
        rsx_fp_decompile(prog, sizeof(prog), CTRL_32BIT, hlsl, sizeof(hlsl));
        check("persp_off_raw",    hlsl, "((input.tc2).xyzw).xy");
        check_absent("persp_off_no_helper", hlsl, "_rsx_inv_w");
    }

    printf("\n===========================================\n");
    printf("Results: %d passed, %d failed\n", g_pass, g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}

===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c =====
/* GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (method 0xEB00) executed by the FIFO walker reaches a
 * handler registered with the HLE cellGcmSetUserHandler.
 *
 * A command ring with one user command is built in guest memory, drained with
 * cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and followed by ppu_gcm_pump, five times with a
 * different argument each time. The handler must run once per command, with
 * that command's argument. The lv2 route (rsx_raise_user_cmd, sys_rsx.c) is
 * stubbed here and must still be taken.
 *
 * gcc -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video
 *   libs/video/tests/test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c -ffunction-sections
 *   -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread -o /tmp/test_gcm_fifo_user_command
 *   (clang on macOS: -Wl,-dead_strip)
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller;
/* The walker's other consumers: no graphics backend, no lifted program. */
PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;
u32 g_rsx_last_reference;
void (*g_spu_put_hook)(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size);
void ppu_dump_bctrl_ring(uint32_t n, const char* why) { (void)n; (void)why; }
void ppu_dump_guest_stack(ppu_context* c, const char* why) { (void)c; (void)why; }
void rsx_state_init(rsx_state* state) { (void)state; }
int  rsx_process_method(rsx_state* state, u32 method, u32 data) { (void)state; (void)method; (void)data; return 0; }
int  rsx_draw_engine_enabled(void) { return 0; }
void rsx_draw_engine_method(u32 method, u32 arg) { (void)method; (void)arg; }
void rsx_draw_engine_note_flip(u32 buffer_id) { (void)buffer_id; }
void rsx_draw_engine_guest_read(u32 l, u32 o, u32 p, u32 w, u32 h) { (void)l; (void)o; (void)p; (void)w; (void)h; }
void rsx_draw_engine_guest_wrote(u32 l, u32 o, u32 p, u32 w, u32 h) { (void)l; (void)o; (void)p; (void)w; (void)h; }
int  rsx_live_draw_enabled(void) { return 0; }
void rsx_live_draw_method(u32 method, u32 arg) { (void)method; (void)arg; }
int  rsx_live_draw_blit(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 w, u32 h)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)w; (void)h; return 0; }
void rsx_live_draw_note_resolve(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d) { (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; }
int  rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 g, u32 h,
                                u32 i, u32 j, u32 k, u32 l)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)g; (void)h; (void)i; (void)j; (void)k; (void)l; return 0; }

static unsigned lv2_raised;
void rsx_raise_user_cmd(uint32_t arg) { (void)arg; lv2_raised++; }

#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00100000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00010000u
#define HANDLER   0x00000100u

static uint32_t g_heap = 0x00400000u;
static u32 host_alloc(u32 size, u32 align)
{
    if (!align) align = 4;
    g_heap = (g_heap + align - 1u) & ~(align - 1u);
    u32 r = g_heap;
    g_heap += size;
    return r;
}
static void gw32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    uint8_t* p = vm_base + ea;
    p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}
static void host_w32(u32 ea, u32 v) { gw32(ea, v); }

static unsigned calls;
static uint32_t last_arg, last_opd;
static void callback(uint32_t opd, uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t c,
                     uint64_t d, uint64_t e, uint64_t f, uint64_t h, uint64_t i)
{
    (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)h; (void)i;
    calls++; last_opd = opd; last_arg = (uint32_t)a;
}

int main(void)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    const uint32_t vm_size = ppu_hle_inject_base + 0x10000u;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, vm_size);
    if (!vm_base) { puts("FAIL: guest VM alloc"); return 1; }
    ppu_vm_size = vm_size;
    g_ps3_guest_caller = callback;

    u32 ctx_out = host_alloc(4, 4);
    u32 cdata = cellGcmSetupContext(ctx_out, CMD_SIZE, IO_SIZE, IO_ADDR, host_alloc, host_w32);
    uint32_t ctrl = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cellGcmGetControlRegister();
    cellGcmSetUserHandler((CellGcmUserHandler)(uintptr_t)HANDLER);

    int fails = 0;
    uint32_t head = 0;
    const uint32_t args[] = { 0x11, 0xC0FFEE, 0, 0x80000001u, 0x5 };
    for (unsigned n = 0; n < sizeof args / sizeof args[0]; n++) {
        /* One method, count 1, subchannel 7, method 0x0B00: GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND. */
        gw32(IO_ADDR + head, (1u << 18) | (7u << 13) | 0x0B00u); head += 4;
        gw32(IO_ADDR + head, args[n]); head += 4;
        gw32(cdata + 0x8, IO_ADDR + head);           /* context current */
        vm_write32(ctrl + 0, head);                  /* put */
        cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
        ppu_gcm_pump();
        int ok = vm_read32(ctrl + 4) == head && calls == n + 1 && last_opd == HANDLER &&
                 last_arg == args[n] && lv2_raised == n + 1;
        printf("[%s] user command %u (arg 0x%X): handler calls %u, last arg 0x%X, lv2 events %u\n",
               ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", n + 1, args[n], calls, last_arg, lv2_raised);
        fails += !ok;
    }
    printf("[gcm_fifo_user_command] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_flip_status.c =====
/* clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video
 *   libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_status.c -Wl,-dead_strip -pthread
 *   -o /tmp/test_gcm_flip_status && /tmp/test_gcm_flip_status
 *
 * The flip status against a flip completion that is delivered late: the
 * ticker marks a completion pending, but the flip handler only runs when a
 * guest thread next pumps, and the title may have requested another flip by
 * then. That newer request must stay WAITING until a tick of its own
 * completes it, and so must one that outlives cellGcmSetWaitFlip's bound.
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <assert.h>
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller;
static unsigned flips;
static void callback(uint32_t opd, uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t c,
                     uint64_t d, uint64_t e, uint64_t f, uint64_t h, uint64_t i)
{
    (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)h; (void)i;
    if (opd == 0x400) flips++;
}
int main(void)
{
    g_ps3_guest_caller = callback;
    s_flip_handler_opd = 0x400;

    /* The plain case: request, tick, deliver. */
    cellGcmResetFlipStatus();
    assert(cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_WAITING);
    cellGcmTickFlip();
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(flips == 1 && cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_DONE);
    /* No flip outstanding: a tick completes nothing and calls no handler. */
    cellGcmTickFlip();
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(flips == 1);

    /* A newer request between the tick and the delivery: the late completion
     * runs the handler for the old flip but leaves the new one WAITING. */
    cellGcmResetFlipStatus();
    cellGcmTickFlip();
    cellGcmResetFlipStatus();
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(flips == 2 && cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_WAITING);
    cellGcmTickFlip();
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(flips == 3 && cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_DONE);

    /* cellGcmSetWaitFlip gives up after its bound, but the flip it waited
     * for is still outstanding and its handler still has to run. */
    cellGcmResetFlipStatus();
    cellGcmSetWaitFlip();
    assert(cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_WAITING);
    cellGcmTickFlip();
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(flips == 4 && cellGcmGetFlipStatus() == CELL_GCM_FLIP_STATUS_DONE);

    puts("GCM flip status checks passed");
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_flip_stream.c =====
/* A flip queued in the command stream (cellGcmSys.c).
 *
 * _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel(ctx, buffer, label, value): libgcm puts
 * NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the label into the context,
 * then the flip. The import used to write the label itself from the PPU and flip
 * at call time.
 *
 * And the flip completes when the drain reaches it: the 60 Hz tick used to mark
 * it done on the next beat wherever the walker was, so a title pacing itself on
 * the flip status rebuilt command segments the walker had not executed yet.
 *
 *   1. The context holds OFFSET, ACQUIRE, then the flip marker, current has
 *      moved past them, and the label in memory is untouched.
 *   2. A tick before the drain is a vblank but no flip.
 *   3. The drain executes up to the marker; the next tick completes the flip.
 *   4. A flip written but not flushed does not complete; an executed one does,
 *      even with a newer flip written behind it and not yet flushed.
 *   5. A flip the walker abandons when it resyncs out of unmapped IO does not
 *      hold back the flip status.
 *   6. With every flip completed, a beat completes nothing: not after the
 *      status was reset, and not for a flip queued after that beat.
 *   7. A flip requested outside the stream completes on the next beat, once.
 *
 * gcc -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_stream.c
 *   -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread
 *   -o /tmp/test_gcm_flip_stream        (clang on macOS: -Wl,-dead_strip)
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;

int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}

/* The rest of the walker's world: no graphics backend, no lifted program. */
PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;
u32 g_rsx_last_reference;
void (*g_spu_put_hook)(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size);
void rsx_raise_user_cmd(uint32_t arg) { (void)arg; }
void ppu_dump_bctrl_ring(uint32_t n, const char* why) { (void)n; (void)why; }
void ppu_dump_guest_stack(ppu_context* c, const char* why) { (void)c; (void)why; }
void rsx_state_init(rsx_state* state) { (void)state; }

                                u32 i, u32 j, u32 k, u32 l)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)g; (void)h; (void)i; (void)j; (void)k; (void)l; return 0; }

#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00400000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00080000u
#define TITLE_CB  0x012D6A78u      /* a title function: its own buffer-full callback */


#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00400000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00080000u
#define TITLE_CB  0x012D6A78u      /* a title function: its own buffer-full callback */
#define LABEL     0x42u
#define VALUE     7u

static uint32_t g_heap = 0x00800000u;
static u32 host_alloc(u32 size, u32 align)
{
    if (!align) align = 4;
    g_heap = (g_heap + align - 1u) & ~(align - 1u);
    u32 r = g_heap;
    g_heap += size;
    return r;
}
static void host_w32(u32 ea, u32 v) { vm_write32(ea, v); }

static int fails;
static void check(int ok, const char* what)
{
    printf("[%s] %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", what);
    fails += !ok;
}

int main(void)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    const uint32_t vm_size = ppu_hle_inject_base + 0x10000u;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, vm_size);
    if (!vm_base) { puts("FAIL: guest VM alloc"); return 1; }
    ppu_vm_size = vm_size;

    u32 ctx_out = host_alloc(4, 4);
    (void)cellGcmSetupContext(ctx_out, CMD_SIZE, IO_SIZE, IO_ADDR, host_alloc, host_w32);
    s_display_buffer_set[1] = 1;

    /* A title context inside the IO window, with its own callback (so the
     * flip never wraps it), and the walker idle at its start. */
    const u32 ctx = host_alloc(0x18, 16), buf = IO_ADDR + 0x200000u;
    vm_write32(ctx + 0x0, buf);
    vm_write32(ctx + 0x4, buf + 0x30000u);
    vm_write32(ctx + 0x8, buf);
    vm_write32(ctx + 0xC, ctx + 0x10);
    vm_write32(ctx + 0x10, TITLE_CB);
    vm_write32(ctx + 0x14, 0);
    const u32 io = gcm_ea2io(buf);
    s_fifo_getoff = io;
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, io);    /* put == get: nothing queued */
    const u32 label_ea = GCM_LABEL_GUEST_BASE + LABEL * GCM_LABEL_STRIDE;
    vm_write32(label_ea, 0);
    (void)GCM_PENDING_TAKE();

    /* 1 */
    const s32 rc = _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel((void*)(uintptr_t)ctx, 1, LABEL, VALUE);
    check(rc == CELL_OK, "WithWaitLabel returns CELL_OK");
    check(vm_read32(buf + 0) == 0x00040064u && vm_read32(buf + 4) == LABEL * GCM_LABEL_STRIDE,
          "SEMAPHORE_OFFSET for the label is in the context");
    check(vm_read32(buf + 8) == 0x00040068u && vm_read32(buf + 12) == VALUE,
          "SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the value follows it");
    check(vm_read32(buf + 16) == (GCM_FLIP_MARKER | 1u), "then the flip");
    check(vm_read32(ctx + 8) == buf + 20, "current is past the flip");
    check(vm_read32(label_ea) == 0, "the label itself is not written by the PPU");

    /* 2 */
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    long p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && !(p & 2), "a tick before the drain is a vblank, not a flip");

    /* 3: the title flushes; the walker runs to put (the acquire does not block
     * unless GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE is set) and stops at the flip. */
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, io + 20);
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
    check(s_fifo_getoff == io + 20, "the drain consumed the wait and the flip");
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && (p & 2), "the next tick completes the flip");

    /* 4: a second flip is written but not flushed (put stays). The first one
     * has already completed, so the tick has nothing new to report... */
    const u32 cur2 = vm_read32(ctx + 8);
    (void)_cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel((void*)(uintptr_t)ctx, 1, LABEL, VALUE);
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && !(p & 2), "a written, unflushed flip does not complete");
    /* ...and once it is flushed and executed, it completes even though a third
     * one has been written behind it and not flushed: the RSX reports the flip
     * it did, not the ones still ahead of it. */
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, gcm_ea2io(cur2) + 20);
    (void)_cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel((void*)(uintptr_t)ctx, 1, LABEL, VALUE);
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && (p & 2), "an executed flip completes with a newer one still unflushed");

    /* 5: the walker is lost in unmapped IO and resyncs to put, abandoning the
     * flip it had not reached. That flip will never be executed, so the next
     * flip status must not wait for it. */
    const u32 cur3 = vm_read32(ctx + 8);
    (void)_cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel((void*)(uintptr_t)ctx, 1, LABEL, VALUE);
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check(!(p & 2), "a written, unflushed flip does not complete (again)");
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, gcm_ea2io(cur3) + 20);
    s_fifo_getoff = 0x0FD00000u;              /* no mapping there */
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
    check(s_fifo_getoff == gcm_ea2io(cur3) + 20, "the walker resynced to put");
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && (p & 2), "a flip abandoned by a resync does not hold back the status");

    /* 6: everything queued has completed. The title resets the status and
     * builds its next frame; beats go by before it queues the flip. */
    cellGcmResetFlipStatus();
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check((p & 1) && !(p & 2), "with no flip outstanding, a beat completes nothing");
    const u32 cur4 = vm_read32(ctx + 8);
    (void)_cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel((void*)(uintptr_t)ctx, 1, LABEL, VALUE);
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check(!(p & 2), "and the flip queued after it waits for the drain");
    vm_write32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 0, gcm_ea2io(cur4) + 20);
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check(p & 2, "which completes it");

    /* 7 */
    check(cellGcmSetFlipCommand(1) == CELL_OK, "a flip outside the stream is accepted");
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check(p & 2, "it completes on the next beat");
    cellGcm_request_tick();
    p = GCM_PENDING_TAKE();
    check(!(p & 2), "once");

    printf("[gcm_flip_stream] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_flip_wrap.c =====
/* The flip HLE's in-FIFO flip (gcm_flip_into_fifo, used by
 * _cellGcmSetFlipCommand) wraps a nearly used command buffer back to its
 * begin only when the runtime owns that buffer.
 *
 * Two contexts, both "nearly full" (less than GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES left) with
 * the walker far past their begin:
 *   - the runtime's own ring, made by cellGcmSetupContext (its buffer-full
 *     callback is the runtime's): the flip marker is written, then a JUMP to
 *     begin, and current goes back to begin;
 *   - a title's context with its own buffer-full callback: the flip marker is
 *     written and current advances past it; no JUMP, no rewind.
 *
 * gcc -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_wrap.c
 *   -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread
 *   -o /tmp/test_gcm_flip_wrap        (clang on macOS: -Wl,-dead_strip)
 */

#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00400000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00080000u
#define TITLE_CB  0x012D6A78u      /* a title function: its own buffer-full callback */

static uint32_t g_heap = 0x00800000u;
static u32 host_alloc(u32 size, u32 align)
{
    if (!align) align = 4;
    g_heap = (g_heap + align - 1u) & ~(align - 1u);
    u32 r = g_heap;
    g_heap += size;
    return r;
}
static void host_w32(u32 ea, u32 v) { vm_write32(ea, v); }

static int fails;
/* Put ctx's current 0x10000 bytes before its end, the walker 0x28000 bytes
 * past its begin, flip, and report what happened to the buffer. */
static void flip_on(const char* what, u32 ctx, int want_wrap)
{
    const u32 begin = vm_read32(ctx), end = vm_read32(ctx + 4), cur = end - 0x10000u;
    vm_write32(ctx + 8, cur);
    vm_write32(cur, 0); vm_write32(cur + 4, 0);
    s_fifo_getoff = gcm_ea2io(begin) + 0x28000u;
    int r = gcm_flip_into_fifo(ctx, 1);
    const u32 marker = vm_read32(cur), next = vm_read32(cur + 4), now = vm_read32(ctx + 8);
    const int wrapped = next == (0x20000000u | gcm_ea2io(begin)) && now == begin;
    const int advanced = next == 0 && now == cur + 4;
    const int ok = r == 1 && marker == (GCM_FLIP_MARKER | 1u) && (want_wrap ? wrapped : advanced);
    printf("[%s] %s: marker 0x%08X, next word 0x%08X, current %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", what,
           marker, next, wrapped ? "rewound to begin (JUMP written)" : advanced ? "advanced past the marker" : "?");
    fails += !ok;
}

int main(void)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    const uint32_t vm_size = ppu_hle_inject_base + 0x10000u;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, vm_size);
    if (!vm_base) { puts("FAIL: guest VM alloc"); return 1; }
    ppu_vm_size = vm_size;

    u32 ctx_out = host_alloc(4, 4);
    u32 rt = cellGcmSetupContext(ctx_out, CMD_SIZE, IO_SIZE, IO_ADDR, host_alloc, host_w32);
    s_display_buffer_set[1] = 1;

    /* The title's draw context: 0x30000 bytes inside the IO window, with its
     * own callback descriptor. */
    const u32 tctx = host_alloc(0x18, 16), tbuf = IO_ADDR + 0x200000u;
    vm_write32(tctx + 0x0, tbuf);
    vm_write32(tctx + 0x4, tbuf + 0x30000u);
    vm_write32(tctx + 0x8, tbuf);
    vm_write32(tctx + 0xC, tctx + 0x10);
    vm_write32(tctx + 0x10, TITLE_CB);
    vm_write32(tctx + 0x14, 0);

    flip_on("runtime ring (cellGcmSetupContext)", rt, 1);
    flip_on("title context (own callback)", tctx, 0);
    printf("[gcm_flip_wrap] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_get_on_jump.c =====
/* The control register's get follows the walker across a JUMP (cellGcmSys.c).
 *
 * On the RSX, get is the fetch pointer: a title polling it sees the GPU leave
 * a segment as soon as the JUMP out of it is taken. The walker used to publish
 * get only at the end of a drain pass, which on a slow host comes tens of
 * milliseconds after the JUMP, so a title waiting for the RSX to leave a
 * segment before it reuses that segment waited for the whole pass.
 *
 * Segment A (io 0x0000) runs a probe method, then JUMPs to segment B
 * (io 0x8000), which runs two more; put is after them. The probe stub reads
 * get each time: in A it is where the pass started, in B it must already be
 * B's start. A self-JUMP (park) publishes nothing, and get ends at put.
 *
 * gcc -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video
 *   libs/video/tests/test_gcm_get_on_jump.c -ffunction-sections
 *   -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread -o /tmp/test_gcm_get_on_jump
 *   (clang on macOS: -Wl,-dead_strip)
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;

void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}

/* The walker's other consumers: no graphics backend, no lifted program. */
PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;
u32 g_rsx_last_reference;
void (*g_spu_put_hook)(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size);

/* Records where the control register's get stood when each probe method ran. */

{
    (void)state;
    if (method == PROBE_METHOD && data < 8) { seen_get[data] = vm_read32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 4); seen_n++; }
    return 0;
}

{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)w; (void)h; return 0; }
void rsx_live_draw_note_resolve(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d) { (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; }
int  rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 g, u32 h,
                                u32 i, u32 j, u32 k, u32 l)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)g; (void)h; (void)i; (void)j; (void)k; (void)l; return 0; }

void rsx_raise_user_cmd(uint32_t arg) { (void)arg; }

#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00100000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00010000u
#define SEG_B     0x00008000u

static uint32_t g_heap = 0x00400000u;
static u32 host_alloc(u32 size, u32 align)
{
    if (!align) align = 4;
    g_heap = (g_heap + align - 1u) & ~(align - 1u);
    u32 r = g_heap;
    g_heap += size;
    return r;
}
static void gw32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    uint8_t* p = vm_base + ea;
    p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}
static void host_w32(u32 ea, u32 v) { gw32(ea, v); }

static int fails;
static void check(int ok, const char* what)
{
    printf("[%s] %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", what);
    fails += !ok;
}

/* One method, count 1, subchannel 0. */
static u32 put_probe(u32 io, u32 arg)
{
    gw32(IO_ADDR + io, (1u << 18) | PROBE_METHOD);
    gw32(IO_ADDR + io + 4, arg);
    return io + 8;
}

int main(void)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    const uint32_t vm_size = ppu_hle_inject_base + 0x10000u;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, vm_size);
    if (!vm_base) { puts("FAIL: guest VM alloc"); return 1; }
    ppu_vm_size = vm_size;

    u32 ctx_out = host_alloc(4, 4);
    (void)cellGcmSetupContext(ctx_out, CMD_SIZE, IO_SIZE, IO_ADDR, host_alloc, host_w32);
    const uint32_t ctrl = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cellGcmGetControlRegister();

    /* A: probe 0, JUMP to B.  B: probe 1, probe 2, then a park at put. */
    u32 a = put_probe(0, 0);
    gw32(IO_ADDR + a, 0x20000000u | SEG_B);
    u32 b = put_probe(SEG_B, 1);
    b = put_probe(b, 2);
    gw32(IO_ADDR + b, 0x20000000u | b);          /* park: JUMP to itself */

    s_fifo_getoff = 0;
    vm_write32(ctrl + 4, 0);
    vm_write32(ctrl + 0, b);                     /* put at the park */
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();

    check(seen_n == 3, "the three probe methods ran");
    check(seen_get[0] == 0, "in A, get is where the pass started");
    check(seen_get[1] == SEG_B, "in B, get is already B's start (the JUMP's target)");
    check(seen_get[2] == SEG_B, "get does not move with every method");
    check(vm_read32(ctrl + 4) == b, "after the pass, get is put");

    printf("[gcm_get_on_jump] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_get_on_release.c =====
/* The control register's get is past a semaphore RELEASE by the time its
 * label lands (cellGcmSys.c).
 *
 * On the RSX the semaphore write happens after the command has been fetched,
 * so a title that sees a label move may read get once and take it as the
 * RSX's position. The walker wrote the label at once but published get only
 * at a JUMP and at the end of the pass, so that read returned where the pass
 * started: Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction then spins until its own put
 * equals that get, which it never does.
 *
 * The probe is GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (subchannel 7, method 0x0B00), which
 * calls rsx_raise_user_cmd from inside the pass; the stub records the label
 * and get there. A probe before any RELEASE sees neither move, a single
 * RELEASE and a two-method ACQUIRE+RELEASE each leave get past the whole
 * command, and get does not move with the methods after it. With
 * GCM_GET_EQ_PUT=1 (argument "eq-put") the RELEASE publishes nothing and get
 * is put at the end of the pass, as before.
 *
 * gcc -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video
 *   libs/video/tests/test_gcm_get_on_release.c -ffunction-sections
 *   -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread -o /tmp/test_gcm_get_on_release
 *   (clang on macOS: -Wl,-dead_strip)
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller;
/* The walker's other consumers: no graphics backend, no lifted program. */
PPU_THREAD_LOCAL ppu_context* g_active_ctx;
u32 g_rsx_last_reference;
void (*g_spu_put_hook)(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size);
void ppu_dump_bctrl_ring(uint32_t n, const char* why) { (void)n; (void)why; }
void ppu_dump_guest_stack(ppu_context* c, const char* why) { (void)c; (void)why; }
void rsx_state_init(rsx_state* state) { (void)state; }
int  rsx_process_method(rsx_state* state, u32 method, u32 data) { (void)state; (void)method; (void)data; return 0; }
int  rsx_draw_engine_enabled(void) { return 0; }
void rsx_draw_engine_method(u32 method, u32 arg) { (void)method; (void)arg; }
void rsx_draw_engine_note_flip(u32 buffer_id) { (void)buffer_id; }
void rsx_draw_engine_guest_read(u32 l, u32 o, u32 p, u32 w, u32 h) { (void)l; (void)o; (void)p; (void)w; (void)h; }
void rsx_draw_engine_guest_wrote(u32 l, u32 o, u32 p, u32 w, u32 h) { (void)l; (void)o; (void)p; (void)w; (void)h; }
int  rsx_live_draw_enabled(void) { return 0; }
void rsx_live_draw_method(u32 method, u32 arg) { (void)method; (void)arg; }
int  rsx_live_draw_blit(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 w, u32 h)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)w; (void)h; return 0; }
void rsx_live_draw_note_resolve(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d) { (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; }
int  rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 g, u32 h,
                                u32 i, u32 j, u32 k, u32 l)
{ (void)a; (void)b; (void)c; (void)d; (void)e; (void)f; (void)g; (void)h; (void)i; (void)j; (void)k; (void)l; return 0; }

#define SEMA_OFF  0x10u
#define LABEL_EA  (GCM_LABEL_GUEST_BASE + SEMA_OFF)

/* Records the label and get each time a probe user command runs. */
static u32 seen_get[8], seen_label[8], seen_n;
void rsx_raise_user_cmd(uint32_t arg)
{
    if (arg < 8) {
        seen_get[arg] = vm_read32(GCM_CONTROL_GUEST_ADDR + 4);
        seen_label[arg] = vm_read32(LABEL_EA);
        seen_n++;
    }
}

#define IO_ADDR   0x00100000u
#define IO_SIZE   0x00100000u
#define CMD_SIZE  0x00010000u

static uint32_t g_heap = 0x00400000u;
static u32 host_alloc(u32 size, u32 align)
{
    if (!align) align = 4;
    g_heap = (g_heap + align - 1u) & ~(align - 1u);
    u32 r = g_heap;
    g_heap += size;
    return r;
}
static void gw32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    uint8_t* p = vm_base + ea;
    p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}
static void host_w32(u32 ea, u32 v) { gw32(ea, v); }

static int fails;
static void check(int ok, const char* what)
{
    printf("[%s] %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", what);
    fails += !ok;
}

/* An incrementing method header: count words, subchannel subch. */
static u32 put_cmd(u32 io, u32 subch, u32 method, u32 count, const u32* args)
{
    gw32(IO_ADDR + io, (count << 18) | (subch << 13) | method);
    for (u32 i = 0; i < count; i++) gw32(IO_ADDR + io + 4 + i * 4, args[i]);
    return io + 4 + count * 4;
}
static u32 put_probe(u32 io, u32 arg) { return put_cmd(io, 7, 0x0B00u, 1, &arg); }

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    const int eq_put = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "eq-put");
    if (eq_put != gcm_get_eq_put()) { puts("FAIL: GCM_GET_EQ_PUT does not match the argument"); return 1; }
    const uint32_t vm_size = ppu_hle_inject_base + 0x10000u;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, vm_size);
    if (!vm_base) { puts("FAIL: guest VM alloc"); return 1; }
    ppu_vm_size = vm_size;

    u32 ctx_out = host_alloc(4, 4);
    (void)cellGcmSetupContext(ctx_out, CMD_SIZE, IO_SIZE, IO_ADDR, host_alloc, host_w32);
    const uint32_t ctrl = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cellGcmGetControlRegister();

    /* probe 0, OFFSET, RELEASE 0x11, probe 1, ACQUIRE 0x11 + RELEASE 0x22 in
     * one two-method command, probe 2, probe 3; put after the last probe. */
    const u32 off = SEMA_OFF, rel1 = 0x11u, acq_rel[2] = { 0x11u, 0x22u };
    u32 io = put_probe(0, 0);
    io = put_cmd(io, 0, 0x64u, 1, &off);
    io = put_cmd(io, 0, 0x6Cu, 1, &rel1);
    const u32 end_rel1 = io;
    io = put_probe(io, 1);
    io = put_cmd(io, 0, 0x68u, 2, acq_rel);
    const u32 end_rel2 = io;
    io = put_probe(io, 2);
    io = put_probe(io, 3);
    const u32 put = io;

    s_fifo_getoff = 0;
    vm_write32(ctrl + 4, 0);
    vm_write32(ctrl + 0, put);
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();

    check(seen_n == 4, "the four probe commands ran");
    check(seen_get[0] == 0 && seen_label[0] == 0, "before any RELEASE, neither get nor the label has moved");
    check(seen_label[1] == 0x11u, "the RELEASE wrote its label");
    check(seen_label[2] == 0x22u, "the RELEASE inside ACQUIRE+RELEASE wrote its label");
    if (!eq_put) {
        check(seen_get[1] == end_rel1, "get is past the RELEASE when its label is seen");
        check(seen_get[2] == end_rel2, "get is past the whole ACQUIRE+RELEASE command");
        check(seen_get[3] == end_rel2, "get does not move with the methods after it");
    } else {
        check(seen_get[1] == 0 && seen_get[2] == 0 && seen_get[3] == 0,
              "GCM_GET_EQ_PUT: a RELEASE publishes nothing mid-pass");
    }
    check(vm_read32(ctrl + 4) == put, "after the pass, get is put");

    printf("[gcm_get_on_release%s] %s (%d failed)\n", eq_put ? " eq-put" : "", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_gcm_user_command.c =====
/* clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I libs/video
 *   libs/video/tests/test_gcm_user_command.c -Wl,-dead_strip -pthread
 *   -o /tmp/test_gcm_user_command && /tmp/test_gcm_user_command
 */
#include "../cellGcmSys.c"
#include <assert.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <sched.h>
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
int g_resv_store_active;
uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller;
static unsigned calls;
static uint32_t last;
static atomic_int paused, resume_pump;
static void* pump_thread(void* unused)
{
    (void)unused; ppu_gcm_pump(); return NULL;
}
static void callback(uint32_t opd, uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t c,
                        uint64_t d, uint64_t e, uint64_t f, uint64_t h, uint64_t i)
{
    if (opd == 0x300) {
        atomic_store(&paused, 1);
        while (!atomic_load(&resume_pump)) sched_yield();
        return;
    }
    if (opd == 0x200) { cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xDD); return; }
    assert(opd == 0x100 && !b && !c && !d && !e && !f && !h && !i);
    calls++; last = (uint32_t)a;
    if (a == 0xAA) { cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xBB); ppu_gcm_pump(); }
    return;
}
int main(void)
{
    g_ps3_guest_caller = callback;
    cellGcmSetUserHandler((CellGcmUserHandler)(uintptr_t)0x100);
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(1);
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xAA);
    assert(calls == 0);
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(calls == 1 && last == 0xAA);
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(calls == 2 && last == 0xBB);
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 2);
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0); ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(calls == 3 && last == 0);
    /* A vblank callback can publish another cause after this pump has
     * claimed the old interrupt. It must not replace that claimed cause. */
    s_vblank_handler_opd = 0x200;
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xCC);
    cellGcmTickVBlank();
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 4 && last == 0xCC);
    s_vblank_handler_opd = 0;
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 5 && last == 0xDD);
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 5);
    /* While one host thread has claimed an interrupt but is still in a
     * vblank callback, another pump must not deliver a newer cause first. */
    pthread_t worker;
    s_vblank_handler_opd = 0x300;
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xE1);
    cellGcmTickVBlank();
    assert(pthread_create(&worker, NULL, pump_thread, NULL) == 0);
    while (!atomic_load(&paused)) sched_yield();
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(0xE2);
    ppu_gcm_pump();
    assert(calls == 5);
    atomic_store(&resume_pump, 1);
    assert(pthread_join(worker, NULL) == 0);
    assert(calls == 6 && last == 0xE1);
    s_vblank_handler_opd = 0;
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 7 && last == 0xE2);
    ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 7);
    cellGcmSetUserHandler(NULL);
    cellGcmQueueUserCommand(7); ppu_gcm_pump(); assert(calls == 7);
    puts("Deferred GCM user-command checks passed");
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_live_draw_aa_surface.c =====
/*
 * D3D12 live-draw test: antialiased surfaces at sample resolution.
 *
 * An RSX surface with antialiasing (SURFACE_FORMAT bits 12-15) holds its
 * sample grid in memory: 3 = 2x1 samples per pixel, 4 and 5 = 2x2. For each
 * mode an 8x8-pixel A8R8G8B8 target is cleared to black and a white quad is
 * drawn over the whole 8x8 viewport with the scissor on the left 4 pixel
 * columns. The surface must read back at its sample size with the left half
 * of the samples white and the right half black.
 * Build and run: see live_draw_test_harness.h.
 */
#include "live_draw_test_harness.h"

#define T "test_live_draw_aa_surface"

#define VTX     0x00000000u    /* main memory */
#define FP_COL  0x00001000u

int main(void)
{
    if (ldh_init(T) != 0) return 2;
    rsx_test_fp_mov_r0_col0(ldh_main + FP_COL, RSX_TEST_FP_SWZ_IDENT);
    ldh_setup_quad(VTX, 1, 1, 0, 0);
    static const struct { u32 aa, sx, sy; } cases[] = {
        { 0, 1, 1 }, { 3, 2, 1 }, { 4, 2, 2 }, { 5, 2, 2 },
    };
    for (u32 i = 0; i < sizeof cases / sizeof cases[0]; i++) {
        const u32 surf = 0x10000u * i;
        ldh_surface(0x8u | (0x1u << 8) | (cases[i].aa << 12), surf, 64, 0x200000u, 64, 8, 8);
        ldh_m(NV4097_SET_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE, 0xFF000000u);
        ldh_m(NV4097_CLEAR_SURFACE, 0xF0u);
        ldh_m(NV4097_SET_SCISSOR_HORIZONTAL, 4u << 16);   /* left 4 pixels */
        ldh_draw(FP_COL, 0x40u, 0, 0, 0x207u);
        static uint8_t rgb[32 * 32 * 3];
        u32 w = 0, h = 0;
        char path[64], name[96];
        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "aa_surface_%u.ppm", cases[i].aa);
        const u32 ww = 8u * cases[i].sx, wh = 8u * cases[i].sy;
        const int read = ldh_read_rgb(surf, path, rgb, 32, 32, &w, &h) == 0;
        snprintf(name, sizeof name, "antialias %u: surface is %ux%u samples (got %ux%u)",
                 cases[i].aa, ww, wh, w, h);
        ldh_check(name, read && w == ww && h == wh);
        if (!read) continue;
        int good = 0;
        for (u32 y = 0; y < h; y++)
            for (u32 x = 0; x < w; x++) {
                const int lit = rgb[(y * w + x) * 3] > 200;
                good += lit == (x < w / 2u);
            }
        snprintf(name, sizeof name, "antialias %u: left half drawn, right half scissored "
                 "(%d of %u samples right)", cases[i].aa, good, w * h);
        ldh_check(name, good == (int)(w * h));
    }
    return ldh_done(T);
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_live_draw_alias_subrect.c =====
/*
 * D3D12 live-draw test: a texture smaller than the colour surface it aliases
 * reads the surface's top-left samples, texel for sample.
 *
 *   A. an 8x8-pixel A8R8G8B8 target with antialias 4 (2x2 samples) is held at
 *      16x16 samples, guest pitch 64. It is cleared to black and a white quad
 *      is drawn with the scissor on the left 4 pixels, so the left 8 sample
 *      columns are white and the right 8 are black.
 *   B. an 8x8 pass into a second surface samples the same address as an 8x8
 *      linear A8R8G8B8 texture with pitch 64. Texel (x, y) of that texture is
 *      sample (x, y) of A, so every texel is white. Bound to the whole 16x16
 *      surface and scaled into the 8x8 texture, the right half would be black.
 * Build and run: see live_draw_test_harness.h.
 */
#include "live_draw_test_harness.h"

#define T "test_live_draw_alias_subrect"

#define SURF_A  0x00000000u   /* 8x8 pixels, 16x16 samples, pitch 64 */
#define SURF_E  0x00010000u   /* 8x8, the result */
#define VTX     0x00000000u
#define FP_COL  0x00001000u
#define FP_TX   0x00001100u

int main(void)
{
    if (ldh_init(T) != 0) return 2;
    rsx_test_fp_mov_r0_col0(ldh_main + FP_COL, RSX_TEST_FP_SWZ_IDENT);
    rsx_test_fp_tex_r0_tc0(ldh_main + FP_TX, 0);
    ldh_setup_quad(VTX, 1, 1, 0, 0);

    ldh_surface(0x8u | (0x1u << 8) | (4u << 12), SURF_A, 64, 0x200000u, 64, 8, 8);
    ldh_m(NV4097_SET_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE, 0xFF000000u);
    ldh_m(NV4097_CLEAR_SURFACE, 0xF0u);
    ldh_m(NV4097_SET_SCISSOR_HORIZONTAL, 4u << 16);          /* left 4 pixels = 8 samples */
    ldh_draw(FP_COL, 0x40u, 0, 0, 0x207u);                   /* A */

    ldh_surface(0x8u | (0x1u << 8), SURF_E, 32, 0x200000u, 64, 8, 8);
    ldh_m(NV4097_SET_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE, 0xFF000000u);
    ldh_m(NV4097_CLEAR_SURFACE, 0xF0u);
    ldh_texture0(SURF_A, 0x85u | 0x20u, 8, 8, 64);           /* A8R8G8B8, linear, pitch 64 */
    ldh_draw(FP_TX, 0x40u, 0, 0, 0x207u);                    /* B */

    static uint8_t rgb[8 * 8 * 3];
    u32 w = 0, h = 0;
    const int ok = ldh_read_rgb(SURF_E, "alias_subrect_e.ppm", rgb, 8, 8, &w, &h) == 0 && w == 8 && h == 8;
    ldh_check("result surface read back (8x8)", ok);
    if (ok) {
        int good = 0;
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 64; i++) good += rgb[i * 3] > 200;
        char name[96];
        snprintf(name, sizeof name, "8x8 texture over a 16x16-sample surface reads its top-left "
                 "samples (%d of 64 white)", good);
        ldh_check(name, good == 64);
    }
    return ldh_done(T);
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_live_draw_depth_export.c =====
/*
 * D3D12 live-draw test: fragment depth export, and the texel size of a
 * depth texture that reads a zeta snapshot larger than itself.
 *
 *   1. a 16x16 pass writes depth 0.5 into Z24S8 zeta Z;
 *   2. a 4x4 pass into Z with SHADER_CONTROL depth export (0xE) writes
 *      depth = r1.z = tc0.z, 0.1 at the left edge to 0.9 at the right,
 *      so columns 0..3 hold 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8;
 *   3. Z read as a 16x16 DEPTH24_D8 texture with normalised coordinates:
 *      the top-left 4x4 holds the exported depths, the rest 0.5;
 *   4. Z read as a 4x4 DEPTH24_D8 texture with texel (unnormalised)
 *      coordinates 0..4: it reads Z's top-left 4x4, as it does in VRAM.
 *
 * Without depth export the 4x4 pass keeps the quad's depth (0.5); dividing
 * the texel coordinates of step 4 by the texture size (4) instead of the
 * snapshot's (16) stretches the whole 16x16 zeta over the 4x4 target.
 * Build and run: see live_draw_test_harness.h.
 */
#include "live_draw_test_harness.h"
#include <math.h>

#define T "test_live_draw_depth_export"

/* Local memory. */
#define SURF_BIG 0x00000000u   /* 16x16 A8R8G8B8, pitch 64 */
#define SURF_S   0x00002000u   /* 4x4, the depth-export pass's colour */
#define SURF_E   0x00004000u   /* 16x16, step 3 result */
#define SURF_F   0x00006000u   /* 4x4, step 4 result */
#define ZETA     0x00100000u   /* Z24S8, 16x16, pitch 64 */
#define ZETA2    0x00102000u   /* zeta of the read passes (depth test off) */
/* Main memory. */
#define VTX_A    0x00000000u
#define VTX_B    0x00000400u
#define FP_DE    0x00001000u   /* MOV r1, TC0 ; MOV r0, COL0 */
#define FP_TX    0x00001100u   /* TEX r0, TC0, unit 0 */
#define FP_COL   0x00001200u   /* MOV r0, COL0 */

#define FMT_ARGB_Z24 (0x8u | (0x2u << 5) | (0x1u << 8))   /* A8R8G8B8, Z24S8, linear */
#define TEXF_DEPTH24_D8 0x90u
#define TEXF_LN 0x20u
#define TEXF_UN 0x40u

static int near_u8(uint8_t got, float want) { return fabsf(got / 255.0f - want) <= 3.0f / 255.0f; }

int main(void)
{
    if (ldh_init(T) != 0) return 2;
    uint8_t* fpm = ldh_main;
    rsx_test_fp_instr(fpm + FP_DE,
                      RSX_TEST_FP_OPC(RSX_TEST_FP_OP_MOV) | RSX_TEST_FP_MASK_XYZW |
                      RSX_TEST_FP_INSRC_TC0 | RSX_TEST_FP_OUTREG(1),
                      RSX_TEST_FP_SRC_INPUT | RSX_TEST_FP_SWZ_IDENT);
    rsx_test_fp_mov_r0_col0(fpm + FP_DE + 16, RSX_TEST_FP_SWZ_IDENT);
    rsx_test_fp_tex_r0_tc0(fpm + FP_TX, 0);
    rsx_test_fp_mov_r0_col0(fpm + FP_COL, RSX_TEST_FP_SWZ_IDENT);
    const u32 X32 = 0x40u, ALWAYS = 0x207u;

    ldh_setup_quad(VTX_A, 1, 1, 0.1f, 0.9f);
    ldh_surface(FMT_ARGB_Z24, SURF_BIG, 64, ZETA, 64, 16, 16);
    ldh_draw(FP_COL, X32, 1, 1, ALWAYS);                        /* 1: depth 0.5 */
    ldh_surface(FMT_ARGB_Z24, SURF_S, 64, ZETA, 64, 4, 4);
    ldh_draw(FP_DE, X32 | 0xEu, 1, 1, ALWAYS);                  /* 2: depth = tc0.z */

    ldh_surface(FMT_ARGB_Z24, SURF_E, 64, ZETA2, 64, 16, 16);
    ldh_texture0(ZETA, TEXF_DEPTH24_D8 | TEXF_LN, 16, 16, 64);
    ldh_draw(FP_TX, X32, 0, 0, ALWAYS);                         /* 3: normalised read */

    ldh_setup_quad(VTX_B, 4, 4, 0, 0);
    ldh_surface(FMT_ARGB_Z24, SURF_F, 64, ZETA2, 64, 4, 4);
    ldh_texture0(ZETA, TEXF_DEPTH24_D8 | TEXF_LN | TEXF_UN, 4, 4, 64);
    ldh_draw(FP_TX, X32, 0, 0, ALWAYS);                         /* 4: texel read */

    static uint8_t rgb[16 * 16 * 3];
    u32 w = 0, h = 0;
    int ok = ldh_read_rgb(SURF_E, "depth_export_e.ppm", rgb, 16, 16, &w, &h) == 0 && w == 16 && h == 16;
    ldh_check("step 3 surface read back (16x16)", ok);
    if (ok) {
        int good = 0;
        for (u32 y = 0; y < 4; y++) {
            printf("[" T "] exported row %u:", y);
            for (u32 x = 0; x < 4; x++) {
                const uint8_t r = rgb[(y * 16 + x) * 3];
                printf(" %.3f", r / 255.0f);
                good += near_u8(r, 0.2f + 0.2f * x);
            }
            printf("\n");
        }
        ldh_check("depth export: 16 exported depths 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8 by column", good == 16);
        ldh_check("depth export: depth outside the 4x4 pass stays 0.5",
                  near_u8(rgb[(10 * 16 + 10) * 3], 0.5f) && near_u8(rgb[(2 * 16 + 12) * 3], 0.5f));
    }
    ok = ldh_read_rgb(SURF_F, "depth_export_f.ppm", rgb, 16, 16, &w, &h) == 0 && w == 4 && h == 4;
    ldh_check("step 4 surface read back (4x4)", ok);
    if (ok) {
        int good = 0;
        for (u32 y = 0; y < 4; y++) {
            printf("[" T "] texel-read row %u:", y);
            for (u32 x = 0; x < 4; x++) {
                const uint8_t r = rgb[(y * 4 + x) * 3];
                printf(" %.3f", r / 255.0f);
                good += near_u8(r, 0.2f + 0.2f * x);
            }
            printf("\n");
        }
        ldh_check("texel coordinates address the snapshot: 4x4 corner read 1:1", good == 16);
    }
    return ldh_done(T);
}


===== FILE: \libs\video\tests\test_live_draw_depth_textures.c =====
/*
 * D3D12 live-draw test: a depth buffer read as a texture returns its depth.
 *
 *   A. a 4x4 pass writes depth into Z24S8 zeta ZA (the zeta and its R32F
 *      snapshot are created with a 4x4 clip);
 *   B. a 16x16 pass whose colour target is ZA itself (colour writes masked)
 *      writes depth 0.1 at the left edge to 0.9 at the right into ZA;
 *   C. a 16x16 pass into colour surface E with ZA still bound as its zeta,
 *      depth test on and depth write off, reads ZA as a 16x16 DEPTH24_D8
 *      texture: E at column x must be 0.1 + 0.8 * (x + 0.5) / 16.
 * C needs all three: the snapshot grown to 16x16 (it was created 4x4), the
 * depth read preferring the zeta over the colour surface at the same
