     * channel the result comes back on. */
    _exit(ok ? 0 : 1);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The guest thread body. sys_ppu_thread_create was given the OPD at
 * SMOKE_OPD_THREAD; the runtime resolved it and dispatched here on a fresh
 * host thread, with the creator's argument in r3.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
void func_00010100(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    g_body_host_tid = (unsigned long)GetCurrentThreadId();
    g_body_arg      = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
    /* Let the creator mark first (see g_create_marked); a sleep through the
     * timer syscall rather than a spin, so the wait is itself guest-shaped. */
    while (!atomic_load(&g_create_marked)) smoke_usleep(ctx, 100);
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_THREAD_BODY);

    smoke_check(ctx->gpr[13] != 0, "the guest thread has no thread pointer in r13");

    ctx->gpr[11] = SC_PPU_THREAD_EXIT;
    ctx->gpr[3]  = SMOKE_THREAD_STATUS;
    lv2_syscall(ctx);   /* does not return: the runtime unwinds the thread */
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * _start. ppu_run resolved the entry OPD out of the loaded image and called
 * this with the PS3 process-entry register state: r1 stack, r2 TOC, r3/r4
 * argc/argv, r13 the thread pointer.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
void func_00010000(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    uint32_t argc = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
    uint32_t argv = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4];
    uint32_t envp = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5];
    uint64_t envc = ctx->gpr[6];
    uint32_t toc  = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[2];
    uint32_t tp   = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[13];
    uint32_t gcm_ctx, ctrl;
    uint64_t tid;

    g_main_host_tid = (unsigned long)GetCurrentThreadId();
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_ENTRY);

    /* The entry state ppu_run built. argv[0] is a big-endian 8-byte slot whose
     * pointer sits in the low word, which is where the PS3 CRT reads it. */
    smoke_check(toc == SMOKE_DATA_BASE + 0x0D00u, "r2 is not this image's TOC");
    smoke_check(argc == 1, "argc is not 1");
    smoke_check(argv != 0 && vm_read8(vm_read32(argv + 4)) != 0,
                "argv[0] does not point at a string");
    /* Even an empty environment has an addressable NULL pointer slot. The
     * guest CRT reads envp[0] before checking the environment count. */
    smoke_check(envp != 0, "r5 does not point at an environment list");
    smoke_check(envc == 0, "r6 is not the empty environment count");
    smoke_check(vm_read64(envp) == 0, "envp[0] is not NULL");

    /* The image itself: initialised data, the BSS tail past filesz, and the
     * PT_TLS template ppu_run copied into the main thread's TLS block. */
    smoke_check(vm_read32(SMOKE_CANARY_EA) == SMOKE_CANARY,
                "the image canary is not in guest RAM (PT_LOAD did not land)");
    vm_write32(SMOKE_SC_BSSPROBE, SMOKE_CANARY);
    smoke_check(vm_read32(SMOKE_SC_BSSPROBE) == SMOKE_CANARY,
                "the BSS tail past filesz is not backed guest RAM");
    smoke_check(tp != 0 && vm_read32(tp - SMOKE_TLS_TP_BIAS) == SMOKE_TLS_CANARY,
                "r13 does not point at the loaded PT_TLS template");
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_IMAGE);

    /* A firmware import, through the NID bridge. _cellGcmInitBody is the call
     * the SDK's cellGcmInit() macro makes, and it is what brings up the GCM
     * context the frame loop below writes into.
     *   r3 = &context (out), r4 = cmdSize, r5 = ioSize, r6 = ioAddress */
    ctx->gpr[3] = SMOKE_SC_GCMCTX;
    ctx->gpr[4] = SMOKE_CMD_SIZE;
    ctx->gpr[5] = SMOKE_IO_SIZE;
    ctx->gpr[6] = SMOKE_IO_ADDR;
    func_00010200(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
    smoke_check((int32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == 0, "_cellGcmInitBody returned an error");
    gcm_ctx = vm_read32(SMOKE_SC_GCMCTX);
    smoke_check(gcm_ctx != 0, "_cellGcmInitBody left the context pointer null");
    smoke_check(vm_read32(gcm_ctx + 0) == SMOKE_IO_ADDR,
                "the GCM context does not begin at the IO address");
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_HLE);

    /* A guest thread. The entry is an OPD address, which the runtime's thread
     * trampoline resolves the same way ppu_run resolved ours. */
    ctx->gpr[11] = SC_PPU_THREAD_CREATE;
    ctx->gpr[3]  = SMOKE_SC_TID;          /* u64* thread id (out) */
    ctx->gpr[4]  = SMOKE_OPD_THREAD;      /* entry OPD           */
    ctx->gpr[5]  = SMOKE_THREAD_ARG;      /* the new thread's r3 */
    ctx->gpr[6]  = 1000;                  /* priority            */
    ctx->gpr[7]  = 0x10000;               /* stack size          */
    ctx->gpr[8]  = 1;                     /* flags: JOINABLE (joined below) */
    ctx->gpr[9]  = SMOKE_THREAD_NAME;
    lv2_syscall(ctx);
    smoke_check((int32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == 0, "sys_ppu_thread_create failed");
    tid = vm_read64(SMOKE_SC_TID);
    smoke_check(tid != 0, "sys_ppu_thread_create returned thread id 0");
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_THREAD_CREATE);
    atomic_store(&g_create_marked, 1u);

    ctx->gpr[11] = SC_PPU_THREAD_JOIN;
    ctx->gpr[3]  = tid;
    ctx->gpr[4]  = SMOKE_SC_EXITSTAT;     /* s64* exit status (out) */
    lv2_syscall(ctx);
    smoke_check((int32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == 0, "sys_ppu_thread_join failed");
    smoke_check((int64_t)vm_read64(SMOKE_SC_EXITSTAT) == SMOKE_THREAD_STATUS,
                "sys_ppu_thread_join handed back the wrong exit status");
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_THREAD_JOIN);

    /* Give the flip a display buffer to land on, then take the control
     * register's guest address: put and get live there, and writing put is how
     * a title tells the RSX there is work.
     *   cellGcmSetDisplayBuffer(id, offset, pitch, width, height) */
    ctx->gpr[3] = 0;
    ctx->gpr[4] = 0;
    ctx->gpr[5] = 1280 * 4;
    ctx->gpr[6] = 1280;
    ctx->gpr[7] = 720;
    func_00010300(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
    smoke_check((int32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == 0, "cellGcmSetDisplayBuffer returned an error");

    func_00010400(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
    ctrl = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
    smoke_check(ctrl != 0, "cellGcmGetControlRegister returned null");

    /* Register the vblank handler before the first frame: the frame loop's
     * status polls are the HLE boundaries the runtime delivers it at. The
     * argument is the handler's OPD, as a title passes it. */
    ctx->gpr[3] = SMOKE_OPD_VBLANK;
    func_00010900(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);

    /* Three frames. Each one appends its commands to the ring, publishes put,
     * asks for a flip and waits for the flip to complete -- the shape of a
     * title's frame loop, and the reason the harness's frame clock has to be
     * running for any of it to finish. */
    for (int frame = 0; frame < SMOKE_FRAMES; frame++) {
        int waited;

        smoke_emit(NV4097_SET_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE, SMOKE_CLEAR_ARGB);
        smoke_emit(NV4097_CLEAR_SURFACE,         0xF0u);
        vm_write32(ctrl + 0, g_fifo_len);        /* put: the RSX chases this */

        ctx->gpr[3] = 0;                         /* buffer id */
        func_00010500(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
        smoke_check((int32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == 0, "cellGcmSetFlipCommand returned an error");

        /* The flip completes on the harness's vblank beat, delivered on this
         * thread at the next HLE boundary -- which is the status poll itself.
         * Bounded so a stalled clock fails the run instead of hanging it. */
        for (waited = 0; waited < 2000; waited++) {
            func_00010600(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
            if ((uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3] == SMOKE_FLIP_DONE) break;
            smoke_usleep(ctx, 1000);
        }
        if (waited >= 2000) smoke_fail("a flip never completed");
        smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_FRAME_1 + frame);
    }

    /* The RSX walker consumed everything the guest wrote: get caught up with
     * put. Without this the frames above prove only that the flips were
     * counted, not that the command stream was read. */
    {
        int waited;
        for (waited = 0; waited < 2000; waited++) {
            if (vm_read32(ctrl + 4) == g_fifo_len) break;
            smoke_usleep(ctx, 1000);
        }
        smoke_check(vm_read32(ctrl + 4) == g_fifo_len,
                    "the RSX never drained the guest's command stream (get != put)");
    }

    /* The vblank handler ran. Three frames of polling is normally beats
     * enough, and the poll is itself the boundary that delivers a pending
     * one, so keep polling, bounded, until it has. The verdict checks what
     * the handler recorded: that it ran on this thread with a count in r3. */
    {
        int waited;
        for (waited = 0; waited < 2000; waited++) {
            if (atomic_load(&g_vblank_calls) != 0) break;
            func_00010600(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
            smoke_usleep(ctx, 1000);
        }
        if (waited >= 2000) smoke_fail("the guest's vblank handler never ran");
    }
    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_VBLANK);

    /* A flip reads as done the moment the clock ticks it; the backend presents
     * it a step later on the clock's own thread. A guest that exits in that
     * gap takes the process down with the last frame still unpresented, and
     * the verdict below then counts one present too few -- which is what a
     * loaded runner showed. Give the clock the beat it needs, bounded like the
     * waits above, so the verdict measures the backend and not the race. */
    {
        int waited;
        for (waited = 0; waited < 2000; waited++) {
            if (ppu_boot_frames_presented() >= (unsigned)SMOKE_FRAMES) break;
            smoke_usleep(ctx, 1000);
        }
    }

    smoke_mark(ctx, SMOKE_STEP_EXIT);

    /* Installed last so it runs first: exit() calls handlers in reverse order
     * of registration, and this one must get its verdict out while the rest of
     * the process is still standing. */
    atexit(smoke_verify);

    ctx->gpr[3] = SMOKE_EXIT_STATUS;
    func_00010700(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);

    /* sys_process_exit does not return. Reaching here means it did. */
    smoke_fail("sys_process_exit returned");
    smoke_verify();
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The lifted function table. ppu_recomp_register() (runtime/ppu/ppu_loader.cpp)
 * walks this into the address -> function map that ps3_indirect_call, the
 * thread trampoline and ppu_run all resolve through.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
const func_entry function_table[] = {
    { 0x00010000ULL, func_00010000, "func_00010000" },
    { 0x00010100ULL, func_00010100, "func_00010100" },
    { 0x00010200ULL, func_00010200, "func_00010200" },
    { 0x00010300ULL, func_00010300, "func_00010300" },
    { 0x00010400ULL, func_00010400, "func_00010400" },
    { 0x00010500ULL, func_00010500, "func_00010500" },
    { 0x00010600ULL, func_00010600, "func_00010600" },
    { 0x00010700ULL, func_00010700, "func_00010700" },
    { 0x00010800ULL, func_00010800, "func_00010800" },
    { 0x00010900ULL, func_00010900, "func_00010900" },
    { 0, NULL, NULL }
};
const uint64_t function_table_count = 10;


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_fs_aio.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellFsAioRead on a shared fd (ppu_fs.cpp).
 *
 * An AIO read names its own offset. It must not move the fd's position for
 * the plain cellFsRead that follows, and several guest threads (FIOS media
 * threads, audio streamers) issue them on one fd at once. The fixture writes
 * a file whose every 4-byte word holds its own offset, then checks both:
 * a cellFsRead after an AIO read continues from the fd's position, and
 * reads racing from four threads each get the words they asked for.
 *
 *   tools/test_ppu_fs_aio.py
 *   test_fs_aio [DIR]     (DIR: where the file goes; default the temp dir)
 */
#include "ppu_fs.cpp"
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

/* ---- link stubs: nothing on the paths this test drives calls them ---- */
extern "C" {
uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;
void vm_write32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v) { uint32_t be = __builtin_bswap32(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 4); }
void vm_write64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) { uint64_t be = __builtin_bswap64(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 8); }
void ppu_guest_caller(char* out, size_t n) { if (n) out[0] = 0; }
void ps3_vfs_ps3game_fallback(char* path, size_t cap) { (void)path; (void)cap; }
void ydkj_host_bt(const char* tag) { (void)tag; }
void ps3_hle_register_ctx(uint32_t, const char*, void (*)(ppu_context*)) {}
}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller = nullptr;
const char* edat_resolve(const char* host_path, char* buf, size_t cap) { (void)buf; (void)cap; return host_path; }

static uint32_t rd32(uint32_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 4); return __builtin_bswap32(v); }
static uint64_t rd64(uint32_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 8); return __builtin_bswap64(v); }
static void wr32(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { vm_write32(a, v); }
static void wr64(uint32_t a, uint64_t v) { vm_write64(a, v); }

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { printf((c) ? "[PASS] " : "[FAIL] "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); \
                           if (!(c)) fails++; } while (0)

static const uint32_t WORDS = 1u << 16;   /* 256 KiB file */

/* One AIO read of `len` bytes at `off` into guest `buf`, through a CellFsAio
 * at guest `aio`: {fd u32, pad, offset u64, buf u32, pad, size u64}. */
static void aio_read(uint32_t aio, uint32_t fd, uint64_t off, uint32_t buf, uint64_t len)
{
    wr32(aio + 0x00, fd); wr64(aio + 0x08, off); wr32(aio + 0x10, buf); wr64(aio + 0x18, len);
    ppu_context ctx; memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx);
    ctx.gpr[3] = aio; ctx.gpr[4] = 0; ctx.gpr[5] = 0;
    cellFsAioRead(&ctx);
}

/* Every word at file offset o holds o (big-endian), so a buffer read from
 * offset `off` is right iff word i holds off + 4*i. */
static bool holds(uint32_t buf, uint64_t off, uint32_t len)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < len; i += 4) if (rd32(buf + i) != (uint32_t)(off + i)) return false;
    return true;
}

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    static uint8_t mem[1 << 20];
    vm_base = mem; ppu_vm_size = sizeof mem;

    const char* dir = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : getenv("TMPDIR");
    if (!dir) dir = "/tmp";
    char host[1100];
    snprintf(host, sizeof host, "%s/ps3recomp_fs_aio.bin", dir);
    {
        FILE* f = fopen(host, "wb");
        if (!f) { printf("FAIL: could not create %s\n", host); return 1; }
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < WORDS; i++) { uint32_t be = __builtin_bswap32(i * 4); fwrite(&be, 4, 1, f); }
        fclose(f);
    }

    ppu_vfs_root = dir;
    strcpy((char*)mem + 0x100, "/dev_hdd1/ps3recomp_fs_aio.bin");
    ppu_context ctx;
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = 0x100; ctx.gpr[4] = 0 /* O_RDONLY */; ctx.gpr[5] = 0x200;
    cellFsOpen(&ctx);
    const uint32_t fd = rd32(0x200);
    CHECK((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "cellFsOpen returns CELL_OK (fd %u)", fd);
    if ((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] != 0) { remove(host); return 1; }

    /* 1. The fd's position survives an AIO read. */
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x40; ctx.gpr[5] = 0 /* SET */; ctx.gpr[6] = 0x208;
    cellFsLseek(&ctx);
    aio_read(0x300, fd, 0x8000, 0x1000, 0x100);
    CHECK(holds(0x1000, 0x8000, 0x100), "the AIO read returns the words at its own offset");
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x2000; ctx.gpr[5] = 16; ctx.gpr[6] = 0x210;
    cellFsRead(&ctx);
    CHECK(rd64(0x210) == 16 && holds(0x2000, 0x40, 16),
          "cellFsRead after it continues from the fd's position 0x40 (got word 0x%08X)", rd32(0x2000));

    /* 2. AIO reads racing on the same fd each get their own bytes. */
    const int THREADS = 4, ROUNDS = 2000;
    const uint32_t LEN = 0x400;
    std::vector<int> bad(THREADS, 0);
    std::vector<std::thread> ts;
    for (int t = 0; t < THREADS; t++)
        ts.emplace_back([&, t] {
            const uint32_t aio = 0x400 + 0x40 * t, buf = 0x10000 + 0x10000 * t;
            uint32_t seed = 0x9E3779B9u * (t + 1);
            for (int r = 0; r < ROUNDS; r++) {
                seed = seed * 1664525u + 1013904223u;
                const uint64_t off = (uint64_t)(seed % (WORDS * 4 - LEN)) & ~3ull;
                aio_read(aio, fd, off, buf, LEN);
                if (!holds(buf, off, LEN)) bad[t]++;
            }
        });
    for (auto& th : ts) th.join();
    int total = 0; for (int b : bad) total += b;
    CHECK(total == 0, "%d racing AIO reads over %d threads, %d returned the wrong bytes",
          THREADS * ROUNDS, THREADS, total);

    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd;
    cellFsClose(&ctx);
    remove(host);
    printf("%s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_fs_imports.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellFs imports registered by ppu_fs_register().
 *
 * A firmware import with no registered handler takes the unresolved-NID path:
 * CELL_OK with every out-parameter left unwritten. This fixture compiles
 * ppu_fs.cpp in, records each ps3_hle_register_ctx() call, and checks four
 * imports a title can call during boot:
 *   - each is registered under the NID a title imports it by;
 *   - cellFsGetFreeSize writes a block size and a non-zero free block count
 *     (both big-endian) and returns CELL_OK;
 *   - cellFsChmod and cellFsUtime return CELL_OK;
 *   - cellFsSdataOpenByFd returns CELL_ENOSYS instead of a silent CELL_OK.
 *
 * Driven by tools/test_ppu_fs_imports.py (writes the stub ppu_recomp.h).
 */
#include "ppu_fs.cpp"
#include <vector>

/* ---- link stubs: nothing on the paths this test drives calls them ---- */
extern "C" {
uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;
void vm_write32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v) { uint32_t be = __builtin_bswap32(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 4); }
void vm_write64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) { uint64_t be = __builtin_bswap64(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 8); }
void ppu_guest_caller(char* out, size_t n) { if (n) out[0] = 0; }
void ps3_vfs_ps3game_fallback(char* path, size_t cap) { (void)path; (void)cap; }
void ydkj_host_bt(const char* tag) { (void)tag; }
}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller = nullptr;
const char* edat_resolve(const char* host_path, char* buf, size_t cap) { (void)buf; (void)cap; return host_path; }

struct Reg { uint32_t nid; const char* name; void (*fn)(ppu_context*); };
static std::vector<Reg> g_regs;
extern "C" void ps3_hle_register_ctx(uint32_t nid, const char* name, void (*fn)(ppu_context*))
{
    g_regs.push_back({nid, name, fn});
}

static void (*find(uint32_t nid))(ppu_context*)
{
    for (auto& r : g_regs) if (r.nid == nid) return r.fn;
    return nullptr;
}
static uint32_t rd32(uint32_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 4); return __builtin_bswap32(v); }
static uint64_t rd64(uint32_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 8); return __builtin_bswap64(v); }

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { printf((c) ? "[PASS] " : "[FAIL] "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); \
                           if (!(c)) fails++; } while (0)

int main()
{
    static uint8_t mem[1 << 16];
    vm_base = mem; ppu_vm_size = sizeof mem;
    ppu_fs_register();

    /* NIDs as they appear in a title's cellFs import table. */
    const uint32_t NID_GETFREESIZE = 0xAA3B4BCDu, NID_CHMOD = 0x99406D0Bu,
                   NID_UTIME = 0xBEF554A4u, NID_SDATAOPENBYFD = 0x6D3BB15Bu;
    struct { uint32_t nid; const char* name; } want[] = {
        {NID_GETFREESIZE, "cellFsGetFreeSize"}, {NID_CHMOD, "cellFsChmod"},
        {NID_UTIME, "cellFsUtime"},             {NID_SDATAOPENBYFD, "cellFsSdataOpenByFd"},
    };
    for (auto& w : want) {
        CHECK(ps3_compute_nid(w.name) == w.nid, "%s: NID 0x%08X is the hash of its name", w.name, w.nid);
        CHECK(find(w.nid) != nullptr, "%s: handler registered", w.name);
    }

    ppu_context ctx;
    if (auto f = find(NID_GETFREESIZE)) {   /* (path, u32* block_size, u64* free_block_count) */
        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx);
        strcpy((char*)mem + 0x100, "/dev_hdd0");
        memset(mem + 0x200, 0xEE, 16);
        ctx.gpr[3] = 0x100; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x200; ctx.gpr[5] = 0x208;
        f(&ctx);
        uint32_t bs = rd32(0x200); uint64_t fb = rd64(0x208);
        CHECK(ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "cellFsGetFreeSize returns CELL_OK");
        CHECK(bs == 4096, "cellFsGetFreeSize block_size = %u", bs);
        CHECK(fb != 0 && fb != 0xEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEull, "cellFsGetFreeSize free_block_count = %llu",
              (unsigned long long)fb);
    }
    struct { uint32_t nid; const char* name; uint32_t ret; } rets[] = {
        {NID_CHMOD, "cellFsChmod", 0}, {NID_UTIME, "cellFsUtime", 0},
        {NID_SDATAOPENBYFD, "cellFsSdataOpenByFd", 0x80010003u /* CELL_ENOSYS */}};
    for (auto& r : rets) if (auto f = find(r.nid)) {
        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = 0x100;
        f(&ctx);
        CHECK((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == r.ret, "%s returns 0x%08X (want 0x%08X)", r.name, (uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3], r.ret);
    }
    printf("%s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_fs_large_file.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - cellFs on a file larger than 4 GiB (ppu_fs.cpp).
 *
 * Windows is LLP64: `long` is 32 bits, so a file past 2 GiB needs 64-bit
 * seek/tell/stat calls. This fixture creates a sparse 5 GiB file with a
 * marker near its end, then drives cellFsStat, cellFsOpen, cellFsLseek,
 * cellFsRead and cellFsFstat through ppu_fs.cpp and checks every size and
 * offset comes back whole. On an LP64 host it passes either way; build it
 * for Windows (MSVC, MinGW-w64 or llvm-mingw) to exercise the LLP64 path.
 *
 *   tools/test_ppu_fs_large_file.py [--exe-out PATH]
 *   test_fs_large_file [DIR]     (DIR: where the sparse file goes; default
 *                                 the system temp directory)
 */
#include "ppu_fs.cpp"
#ifdef _WIN32
#  include <windows.h>
#  include <winioctl.h>
#endif

/* ---- link stubs: nothing on the paths this test drives calls them ---- */
extern "C" {
uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;
void vm_write32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v) { uint32_t be = __builtin_bswap32(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 4); }
void vm_write64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) { uint64_t be = __builtin_bswap64(v); memcpy(vm_base + a, &be, 8); }
void ppu_guest_caller(char* out, size_t n) { if (n) out[0] = 0; }
void ps3_vfs_ps3game_fallback(char* path, size_t cap) { (void)path; (void)cap; }
void ydkj_host_bt(const char* tag) { (void)tag; }
void ps3_hle_register_ctx(uint32_t, const char*, void (*)(ppu_context*)) {}
}
ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller = nullptr;
const char* edat_resolve(const char* host_path, char* buf, size_t cap) { (void)buf; (void)cap; return host_path; }

static uint32_t rd32(uint32_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 4); return __builtin_bswap32(v); }
static uint64_t rd64(uint32_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + a, 8); return __builtin_bswap64(v); }

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { printf((c) ? "[PASS] " : "[FAIL] "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); \
                           if (!(c)) fails++; } while (0)

static const uint64_t FILE_SIZE = (5ULL << 30) + 16;   /* past 2 GiB and past 4 GiB */
static const uint64_t MARK_OFF  = (5ULL << 30) + 8;

/* The fixture's own file setup uses 64-bit calls directly, independent of the
 * code under test. Returns 0 when the sparse file is ready. */
static int make_sparse(const char* path)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    HANDLE h = CreateFileA(path, GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE, 0, NULL, CREATE_ALWAYS,
                           FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, NULL);
    if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return -1;
    DWORD got = 0;
    /* Without the sparse flag NTFS would write gigabytes of zeros. */
    if (!DeviceIoControl(h, FSCTL_SET_SPARSE, NULL, 0, NULL, 0, &got, NULL)) { CloseHandle(h); return -2; }
    LARGE_INTEGER at; at.QuadPart = (LONGLONG)MARK_OFF;
    DWORD wr = 0;
    int ok = SetFilePointerEx(h, at, NULL, FILE_BEGIN) && WriteFile(h, "MARKtail", 8, &wr, NULL) && wr == 8;
    CloseHandle(h);
    return ok ? 0 : -1;
#else
    FILE* f = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!f) return -1;
    int ok = fseeko(f, (off_t)MARK_OFF, SEEK_SET) == 0 && fwrite("MARKtail", 1, 8, f) == 8;
    return (fclose(f) == 0 && ok) ? 0 : -1;
#endif
}

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
    static uint8_t mem[1 << 16];
    vm_base = mem; ppu_vm_size = sizeof mem;

    const char* dir = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : NULL;
#ifdef _WIN32
    char tmp[MAX_PATH];
    if (!dir) { DWORD n = GetTempPathA(sizeof tmp, tmp); if (n && n < sizeof tmp) { tmp[n - 1] = 0; dir = tmp; } }
#endif
    if (!dir) dir = getenv("TMPDIR");
    if (!dir) dir = "/tmp";
    char host[1100];
    snprintf(host, sizeof host, "%s/ps3recomp_fs_large_file.bin", dir);
    int mk = make_sparse(host);
    if (mk == -2) { remove(host); printf("SKIP: the filesystem under %s cannot hold a sparse file\n", dir); return 0; }
    if (mk != 0) { remove(host); printf("FAIL: could not create %s\n", host); return 1; }

    ppu_vfs_root = dir;
    const char* gpath = "/dev_hdd1/ps3recomp_fs_large_file.bin";
    strcpy((char*)mem + 0x100, gpath);
    ppu_context ctx;

    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = 0x100; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x400;
    cellFsStat(&ctx);
    CHECK((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "cellFsStat returns CELL_OK (0x%08X)", (uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3]);
    CHECK(rd64(0x400 + 0x24) == FILE_SIZE, "cellFsStat size 0x%llX (want 0x%llX)",
          (unsigned long long)rd64(0x400 + 0x24), (unsigned long long)FILE_SIZE);

    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = 0x100; ctx.gpr[4] = 0 /* O_RDONLY */; ctx.gpr[5] = 0x500;
    cellFsOpen(&ctx);
    uint32_t fd = rd32(0x500);
    CHECK((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "cellFsOpen returns CELL_OK (fd %u)", fd);
    if ((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == 0) {
        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = MARK_OFF; ctx.gpr[5] = 0 /* SET */; ctx.gpr[6] = 0x508;
        cellFsLseek(&ctx);
        CHECK(rd64(0x508) == MARK_OFF, "cellFsLseek(SET) position 0x%llX (want 0x%llX)",
              (unsigned long long)rd64(0x508), (unsigned long long)MARK_OFF);

        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x600; ctx.gpr[5] = 4; ctx.gpr[6] = 0x510;
        cellFsRead(&ctx);
        CHECK(rd64(0x510) == 4 && memcmp(mem + 0x600, "MARK", 4) == 0, "cellFsRead after the seek reads the marker");

        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = 0; ctx.gpr[5] = 2 /* END */; ctx.gpr[6] = 0x518;
        cellFsLseek(&ctx);
        CHECK(rd64(0x518) == FILE_SIZE, "cellFsLseek(END) position 0x%llX (want 0x%llX)",
              (unsigned long long)rd64(0x518), (unsigned long long)FILE_SIZE);

        memset(mem + 0x700, 0, 0x34);
        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd; ctx.gpr[4] = 0x700;
        cellFsFstat(&ctx);
        CHECK((uint32_t)ctx.gpr[3] == 0 && rd64(0x700 + 0x24) == FILE_SIZE, "cellFsFstat size 0x%llX (want 0x%llX)",
              (unsigned long long)rd64(0x700 + 0x24), (unsigned long long)FILE_SIZE);

        memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof ctx); ctx.gpr[3] = fd;
        cellFsClose(&ctx);
    }
    remove(host);
    printf("%s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_hle_integration.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - NID -> HLE end-to-end integration test (real library).
 *
 * Proves the full bridge with a *real* HLE function (not a mock): the generated
 * NID table (gen_hle_nids.py, computed NIDs) registers cellGcmSys's functions;
 * we compute a function's NID with the same firmware algorithm (nid.h) and
 * dispatch through ps3_hle_call, confirming the real cellGcmSys handler runs
 * and returns via the PPC ABI (r3).
 *
 * Build: see the command in test_loader; links ppu_hle.cpp + the generated
 * ppu_hle_nids.cpp + cellGcmSys.c + rsx_commands.c.
 */
#include "ppu_recomp.h"
#include "ps3emu/nid.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

extern "C" {
void     ps3_hle_call(uint32_t nid, ppu_context* ctx);
uint32_t ps3_hle_count(void);
void     ppu_hle_init(void);
}

/* Host-provided symbols the HLE libs need. */
extern "C" uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
typedef void (*ps3_guest_caller_fn)(uint32_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t,
                                    uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t);
extern "C" ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller = nullptr;

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, m) do { if (c) printf("[PASS] %s\n", m); else { printf("[FAIL] %s\n", m); fails++; } } while (0)

int main()
{
    ppu_hle_init();                       /* registers cellGcmSys (computed NIDs) */
    uint32_t n = ps3_hle_count();
    printf("registered HLE NIDs: %u\n", n);
    CHECK(n >= 26, "cellGcmSys HLE registered");

    /* cellGcmGetMaxIoMapSize() takes no args and, with no IO mappings yet,
     * returns 256 MiB (0x10000000) -- a deterministic, non-zero value that
     * proves the *real* handler ran (an unresolved NID would return 0). */
    uint32_t nid = ps3_compute_nid("cellGcmGetMaxIoMapSize");
    printf("NID(cellGcmGetMaxIoMapSize) = 0x%08X\n", nid);

    ppu_context ctx;
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof(ctx));
    ps3_hle_call(nid, &ctx);
    printf("ps3_hle_call -> r3 = 0x%016llX\n", (unsigned long long)ctx.gpr[3]);
    CHECK(ctx.gpr[3] == 0x10000000ull,
          "real cellGcmGetMaxIoMapSize ran via NID dispatch (r3 = 256 MiB)");

    /* A second, distinct function to confirm dispatch isn't a fluke. */
    uint32_t nid2 = ps3_compute_nid("cellGcmGetCurrentField");
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof(ctx));
    ctx.gpr[3] = 0xDEAD;
    ps3_hle_call(nid2, &ctx);
    CHECK(ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "cellGcmGetCurrentField dispatched (returns 0)");

    printf("\nResults: %s (%d failure(s))\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "OK", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_hle.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - HLE NID dispatch + PPC-ABI adapter test (self-contained).
 *
 * Proves the NID -> handler resolution and the generic PPC integer/pointer ABI
 * marshalling (args r3..r10 -> C args, return -> r3) without linking any HLE
 * library. Generation of the real NID table from annotations is validated
 * separately by compiling gen_hle_nids.py's output.
 *
 * Build: g++ -std=c++17 -I <lift_out> -x c++ test_hle.cpp ../ppu_hle.cpp -o test_hle.exe
 */
#include "ppu_recomp.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

extern "C" {
void     ps3_hle_register(uint32_t nid, const char* name, void* handler);
void     ps3_hle_call(uint32_t nid, ppu_context* ctx);
uint32_t ps3_hle_count(void);
}

/* A mock "HLE" function: 3 integer args, returns a computed value. */
static uint64_t mock_combine(uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t c)
{
    return a * 1000 + b * 10 + c;
}

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, m) do { if (c) printf("[PASS] %s\n", m); else { printf("[FAIL] %s\n", m); fails++; } } while (0)

int main()
{
    ps3_hle_register(0x12345678u, "mock_combine", (void*)mock_combine);
    ps3_hle_register(0xAABBCCDDu, "mock_other",   (void*)mock_combine);
    CHECK(ps3_hle_count() == 2, "two HLE NIDs registered");

    /* Dispatch through the NID with PPC ABI args in r3/r4/r5. */
    ppu_context ctx;
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof(ctx));
    ctx.gpr[3] = 7; ctx.gpr[4] = 8; ctx.gpr[5] = 9;
    ps3_hle_call(0x12345678u, &ctx);
    printf("ps3_hle_call(mock_combine, r3=7,r4=8,r5=9) -> r3 = %llu\n",
           (unsigned long long)ctx.gpr[3]);
    CHECK(ctx.gpr[3] == 7089, "ABI adapter marshalled r3..r5 and returned via r3");

    /* Unresolved NID must not crash; returns 0. */
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof(ctx));
    ctx.gpr[3] = 999;
    ps3_hle_call(0xDEADBEEFu, &ctx);
    CHECK(ctx.gpr[3] == 0, "unresolved NID returns 0 (no crash)");

    printf("\nResults: %s (%d failure(s))\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "OK", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_loader.cpp =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - PPU loader smoke test
 *
 * Loads the real Uncharted EBOOT image into vm_base, registers the lifted
 * function table, and exercises the loader's core mechanics:
 *   - ELF image load (segments + BSS) into vm_base,
 *   - OPD resolution of the entry (code + TOC),
 *   - the address->function registry,
 *   - big-endian guest memory + a lifted leaf function executing via the
 *     indirect-call dispatch.
 *
 * Build (link the lifted output as C++):
 *   g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -I <lift_out> test_loader.cpp ../ppu_loader.cpp \
 *       <lift_out>/ppu_recomp.c -x c++ -o test_loader.exe
 * Run:
 *   ./test_loader.exe "<path to EBOOT.elf>"
 */
#include "ppu_recomp.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

extern "C" uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;

extern "C" {
uint32_t ppu_load_elf(const char* path);
uint32_t ppu_function_count(void);
int      ppu_opd_resolve(uint32_t opd, uint32_t* code, uint32_t* toc);
void     ps3_indirect_call(ppu_context* ctx);
uint32_t vm_read32(uint64_t a);
}

#define VM_SIZE 0x11000000u   /* ~285 MB: covers the highest segment vaddr+memsz */

static int fails = 0;
#define CHECK(c, msg) do { if (c) printf("[PASS] %s\n", msg); \
    else { printf("[FAIL] %s\n", msg); fails++; } } while (0)

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) { printf("usage: %s <EBOOT.elf>\n", argv[0]); return 2; }

    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, VM_SIZE);
    if (!vm_base) { printf("vm alloc failed\n"); return 1; }

    uint32_t entry_opd = ppu_load_elf(argv[1]);
    CHECK(entry_opd != 0, "ELF image loaded, entry OPD non-zero");

    ppu_recomp_register();
    uint32_t n = ppu_function_count();
    printf("registered functions: %u\n", n);
    CHECK(n >= 500, "function table registered (>=500 in this subset)");

    uint32_t code = 0, toc = 0;
    ppu_opd_resolve(entry_opd, &code, &toc);
    printf("entry OPD 0x%08X -> code 0x%08X, toc 0x%08X\n", entry_opd, code, toc);
    CHECK(code == 0x10230, "entry code resolved to 0x10230 (BE OPD read)");
    CHECK(toc == 0x7d3190, "entry TOC resolved to 0x7d3190");

    /* Sanity: a known code word at 0x10230 should be readable big-endian. */
    uint32_t w = vm_read32(0x10230);
    printf("first entry instruction word @0x10230 = 0x%08X\n", w);
    CHECK(w != 0 && w != 0xFFFFFFFF, "code segment present in vm_base");

    /* Execute a lifted leaf function through the indirect-call dispatch.
     * func_00010258: r9 = [toc-0x7FF8]; r3 = [r9]; sign-extend; return.
     * Validates registry lookup + TOC + BE memory + lifted execution. */
    ppu_context ctx;
    memset(&ctx, 0, sizeof(ctx));
    ctx.gpr[1] = VM_SIZE - 0x10000;  /* a stack top inside vm */
    ctx.gpr[2] = toc;
    ctx.ctr    = 0x10258;            /* target code address */
    ps3_indirect_call(&ctx);
    printf("after dispatch to 0x10258: r3 = 0x%016llX\n",
           (unsigned long long)ctx.gpr[3]);
    CHECK(true, "indirect dispatch to a lifted leaf executed without crashing");

    printf("\n===========================================\n");
    printf("Results: %s (%d failure(s))\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "OK", fails);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_ppu_directory.cpp =====
// Real directory stream and guest-memory ABI, without game data or a GPU.
#include "../ppu_fs.cpp"
#include <cassert>
#include <set>
#include <string>
extern "C" { uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr; uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 65536; }
extern "C" void vm_write32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v) {
    assert(a + 4 <= ppu_vm_size);
    for (int i=0;i<4;i++) vm_base[a+i]=uint8_t(v >> (24-i*8));
}
extern "C" void vm_write64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {
    vm_write32(a, uint32_t(v>>32)); vm_write32(a+4, uint32_t(v));
}
static uint32_t read32(uint32_t a) {
    return uint32_t(vm_base[a])<<24 | uint32_t(vm_base[a+1])<<16 |
           uint32_t(vm_base[a+2])<<8 | vm_base[a+3];
}
static ppu_context call(int fd, uint32_t size, uint32_t entries=0x100, uint32_t count=0x80) {
    ppu_context c={}; c.gpr[3]=fd; c.gpr[4]=entries; c.gpr[5]=size; c.gpr[6]=count;
    cellFsGetDirectoryEntries(&c); return c;
}
int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    assert(argc==2); uint8_t memory[65536]={}; vm_base=memory;
    DIR* d=opendir(argv[1]); assert(d);
    int fd=fd_alloc_dir(d); assert(fd>=3);
    snprintf(g_dir_path[fd],sizeof g_dir_path[fd],"%s",argv[1]);
    assert(uint32_t(call(fd,312,0).gpr[3])==0x8001000Du);
    assert(uint32_t(call(fd,312,0x100,0).gpr[3])==0x8001000Du);
    assert(uint32_t(call(999,312).gpr[3])==0x8001002Au);
    assert(call(fd,311).gpr[3]==0 && read32(0x80)==0);
    std::set<std::string> names;
    for (;;) {
        memset(memory+0x100,0xA5,625);
        auto c=call(fd,625); assert(c.gpr[3]==0);
        uint32_t n=read32(0x80); assert(n<=2);
        assert(memory[0x100+624]==0xA5); // incomplete trailing entry untouched
        if(!n) break;
        for(uint32_t i=0;i<n;i++) {
            uint32_t ea=0x100+i*312;
            std::string name(reinterpret_cast<char*>(memory+ea+54));
            assert(names.insert(name).second);
            assert(memory[ea+53]==name.size());
            if(name=="payload") {
                assert(memory[ea+52]==2);
                assert((read32(ea)&0xF000)==0x8000);
                assert(read32(ea+36)==0 && read32(ea+40)==7);
            } else if(name=="folder") {
                assert(memory[ea+52]==1);
                assert((read32(ea)&0xF000)==0x4000);
            }
        }
    }
    assert(names.count("payload") && names.count("folder") && names.count(".hidden"));
    assert(call(fd,312).gpr[3]==0 && read32(0x80)==0); // stable EOF
    closedir(d); g_dirs[fd]=nullptr;
    assert(uint32_t(call(fd,312).gpr[3])==0x8001002Au);
    puts("PASS: PPU directory-entry ABI, batching, bounds, errors, and EOF");
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ppu\tests\test_ppu_dispatch_depth.cpp =====
// ps3_indirect_call's recursion guard with host coroutines that end inside a call.
//
// 5000 coroutines (ucontext) each run a guest call chain five ps3_indirect_call
// levels deep and, at the bottom, switch back to the home context without
// returning -- the way a coroutine that runs guest jobs ends a finished job.
// Around each switch the home side does what a coroutine layer does with
// ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot(): save the count before entering the coroutine
// and restore it when control comes back. Afterwards an indirect call to a
// leaf function on the home thread must still run.
//
// Built by tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py against the real ppu_loader.cpp.
// macOS keeps the ucontext routines behind _XOPEN_SOURCE (deprecated, still
// present); _DARWIN_C_SOURCE keeps the rest of the system headers visible.
// Both must come before the first system header.
#if defined(__APPLE__)
#  define _XOPEN_SOURCE 600
#  define _DARWIN_C_SOURCE
#endif
#include "ppu_recomp.h"
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <cstdint>
#include <ucontext.h>
#include "win32_compat.h"

extern "C" {
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_hle_inject_base = 0x20000000;
int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t) { return 0; }
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t) { std::abort(); }
void spu_lockline_lock(void) { std::abort(); }
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) { std::abort(); }
int spu_raw_reg_load(uint32_t, uint32_t*) { std::abort(); }
void spu_raw_reg_store(uint32_t, uint32_t, unsigned) { std::abort(); }
void cellGcm_ref_on_poll(void) { std::abort(); }
HANDLE CreateThread(void*, SIZE_T, PS3_THREAD_FN, LPVOID, DWORD, DWORD*) { std::abort(); }
BOOL CloseHandle(HANDLE) { std::abort(); }
DWORD GetFileAttributesA(const char*) { return INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES; }
uint64_t ppu_thread_register_main(void) { return 1; }
void (*g_ppu_thread_entry_trampoline)(uint32_t, uint64_t, uint32_t, uint64_t);
const func_entry function_table[1] = {{0, nullptr, nullptr}};   // no lifted program: registered by hand below
const uint64_t function_table_count = 0;
uint32_t ps3_hle_count(void) { return 0; }
void ppu_register_function(uint64_t addr, void (*fn)(ppu_context*));
void ps3_indirect_call(ppu_context* ctx);
// The coroutine hook this test exercises. Weak, so the same test also builds
// against a loader without it and shows what happens there.
__attribute__((weak)) int* ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot(void);
__attribute__((weak)) int* ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(void);
}

enum { LEVELS = 5, COROUTINES = 5000, STACK = 256 * 1024 };
static const uint32_t CHAIN = 0x10000, LEAF = 0x20000;

static ucontext_t s_home, s_co;
static unsigned s_bottoms, s_leaf_calls;

static void chain(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    if (ctx->gpr[3] + 1 < LEVELS) {
        ctx->gpr[3]++;
        ctx->ctr = CHAIN;
        ps3_indirect_call(ctx);
        return;
    }
    ++s_bottoms;
    swapcontext(&s_co, &s_home);   // the coroutine ends here; it is never resumed
}

static void leaf(ppu_context*) { ++s_leaf_calls; }

static ppu_context s_ctx;
static void coroutine_main(void)
{
    s_ctx.gpr[3] = 0;
    s_ctx.ctr = CHAIN;
    ps3_indirect_call(&s_ctx);
}

int main()
{
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)std::calloc(1, 0x100000);
    ppu_register_function(CHAIN, chain);
    ppu_register_function(LEAF, leaf);
    const bool hook = ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot && ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot;
    std::printf("coroutine hook ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot: %s\n", hook ? "present" : "absent");

    static char stack[STACK];
    int depth0 = hook ? *ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() : 0;
    int vsp0 = hook ? *ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot() : 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < COROUTINES; i++) {
        int saved_depth = 0, saved_vsp = 0;
        if (hook) { saved_depth = *ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot(); saved_vsp = *ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(); }
        getcontext(&s_co);
        s_co.uc_stack.ss_sp = stack;
        s_co.uc_stack.ss_size = sizeof stack;
        s_co.uc_link = &s_home;
        makecontext(&s_co, coroutine_main, 0);
        swapcontext(&s_home, &s_co);
        if (hook) { *ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() = saved_depth; *ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot() = saved_vsp; }
    }

    unsigned fails = 0;
    std::printf("[%s] %u of %d coroutines reached the bottom of their %d-level chain\n",
                s_bottoms == COROUTINES ? "PASS" : "FAIL", s_bottoms, COROUTINES, LEVELS);
    fails += s_bottoms != COROUTINES;
    if (hook) {
        int d = *ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot(), v = *ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot();
        std::printf("[%s] home thread depth %d -> %d, vcall sp %d -> %d\n",
                    d == depth0 && v == vsp0 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", depth0, d, vsp0, v);
        fails += d != depth0 || v != vsp0;
    }
    s_ctx.ctr = LEAF;
    ps3_indirect_call(&s_ctx);
    std::printf("[%s] indirect call to a leaf on the home thread afterwards: %s\n",
                s_leaf_calls == 1 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", s_leaf_calls == 1 ? "ran" : "skipped");
    fails += s_leaf_calls != 1;
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

static void entry(ppu_context* ctx) {
    ++called;
    check(vm_read32(0x00B00000)==0x51525354,"entry arguments overwrote PT_LOAD sentinel at old scratch address");
    uint32_t argc=ctx->gpr[3],argv=ctx->gpr[4],envp=ctx->gpr[5];

          "arguments not protected above the entry frame");

    for(unsigned off=8;off<=0x100;off+=8) vm_write64(ctx->gpr[1]-off,~uint64_t(0));
    check(vm_read32(0x40000000)==0x61626364,"heap reservation overwritten");
    check(vm_read32(0xD0100000)==0x71727374,"storage exceeds reserved stack top");
    const char* expected[]={"/dev_bdvd/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/bin/test.self","alpha","beta"};
    unsigned want=std::getenv("PS3_ARGV")?3:1;

    for(unsigned i=0;i<argc && i<3;i++) {

        uint32_t ptr=vm_read32(argv+i*8+4);
        check(ptr && !std::strcmp((char*)vm_base+ptr,expected[i]),"argv string mismatch");
    }
    check(vm_read64(argv+argc*8)==0,"argv not terminated");
    check(envp && vm_read64(envp)==0 && ctx->gpr[6]==0,"empty environment list/count invalid");
    check((ctx->gpr[1]&15)==0,"entry stack not aligned");

int main(int argc,char** argv) {
    if(argc!=3)return 2;
    vm_base=(uint8_t*)mmap(nullptr,0xE0000000ull,PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE,MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANON,-1,0);
    if(vm_base==MAP_FAILED)return 2;
    ppu_vm_size=0xE0000000u;
    uint32_t opd=ppu_load_elf(argv[1]);
    if(!opd)return 2;
    ppu_recomp_register();
    vm_write32(0x40000000,0x61626364);
    vm_write32(0xD0100000,0x71727374);
    bool reject=std::strcmp(argv[2],"run")!=0;
    uint32_t top=0xD0100000u;
    if(!std::strcmp(argv[2],"low"))top=0x10020;
    if(!std::strcmp(argv[2],"outside"))top=0xF0000000u;
    int rc=ppu_run(opd,top);
    if(reject)check(rc!=0 && called==0,"overlapping entry storage must fail before guest dispatch");
    else check(rc==0 && called==1,"guest entry was not dispatched");
    munmap(vm_base,0xE0000000ull);
    return failures?1:0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\prx\prx_loader.c =====
/*
 * prx_loader.c — see prx_loader.h for the design.
 *
 * Two steps per module: place the relocated image into guest RAM at its load
 * base, then register every lifted function in the host dispatch table.
 */
#include "prx_loader.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/* The runtime's guest memory: host_ptr = vm_base + guest_addr. Declared by
 * runtime/memory/vm.h; we only need the symbol, so extern it directly to keep
 * the loader independent of the memory backend's init path. */
extern uint8_t* vm_base;

/* ---- export registry ---------------------------------------------------- *
 * Flat NID -> guest-address table, filled as modules load. A handful of system
 * PRXs export a few hundred symbols total, so a linear array with linear lookup
 * is plenty (lookups happen once per import resolution, not per call). */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t nid;
    uint32_t guest_addr;
    uint32_t library_index;
} prx_export_reg_entry;
#define PRX_EXPORT_REG_CAP 2048
static prx_export_reg_entry s_export_reg[PRX_EXPORT_REG_CAP];
static uint32_t             s_export_reg_n = 0;

typedef struct {
    uint8_t descriptor[0x1C];
    const char* name;
    uint32_t module_base;
    int externally_registered;
} prx_loaded_library;
#define PRX_LIBRARY_REG_CAP 256
static prx_loaded_library s_loaded_libraries[PRX_LIBRARY_REG_CAP];
static uint32_t s_loaded_libraries_n = 0;

static void prx_export_register(uint32_t nid, uint32_t guest_addr,
                                uint32_t library_index)
{
    /* Last writer wins if two modules export the same NID (matches the PS3
     * loader's link order). Overwrite an existing entry rather than duplicate. */
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < s_export_reg_n; i++) {
        if (s_export_reg[i].nid == nid) {
            s_export_reg[i].guest_addr = guest_addr;
            s_export_reg[i].library_index = library_index;
            return;
        }
    }
    if (s_export_reg_n < PRX_EXPORT_REG_CAP)
        s_export_reg[s_export_reg_n++] =
            (prx_export_reg_entry){ nid, guest_addr, library_index };
    else
        fprintf(stderr, "[prx] export registry full, dropping NID 0x%08X\n", nid);
}

static uint32_t prx_library_register_loaded(const prx_module* m,
                                            const prx_library_descriptor* lib)
{
    if (!m || !lib || !vm_base ||
        (uint64_t)lib->vaddr + sizeof(s_loaded_libraries[0].descriptor) > m->image_size ||
        s_loaded_libraries_n >= PRX_LIBRARY_REG_CAP)
        return UINT32_MAX;

    prx_loaded_library* loaded = &s_loaded_libraries[s_loaded_libraries_n];
    memcpy(loaded->descriptor, vm_base + m->base + lib->vaddr,
           sizeof(loaded->descriptor));
    loaded->name = lib->name;
    loaded->module_base = m->base;
    loaded->externally_registered = 0;
    return s_loaded_libraries_n++;
}

uint32_t prx_resolve_export(uint32_t nid)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < s_export_reg_n; i++)
        if (s_export_reg[i].nid == nid)
            return s_export_reg[i].guest_addr;
    return 0;
}

uint32_t prx_export_registry_count(void) { return s_export_reg_n; }

int prx_register_library_descriptor(const uint8_t descriptor[0x1C],
                                    const char** out_library_name)
{
    if (out_library_name)
        *out_library_name = NULL;
    if (!descriptor)
        return 0;

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < s_loaded_libraries_n; ++i) {
        prx_loaded_library* lib = &s_loaded_libraries[i];
        if (memcmp(descriptor, lib->descriptor, sizeof(lib->descriptor)) != 0)
            continue;
        lib->externally_registered = 1;
        if (out_library_name)
            *out_library_name = lib->name;
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

int prx_export_library_is_registered(uint32_t nid)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < s_export_reg_n; ++i) {
        if (s_export_reg[i].nid != nid ||
            s_export_reg[i].library_index == UINT32_MAX ||
            s_export_reg[i].library_index >= s_loaded_libraries_n)
            continue;
        return s_loaded_libraries[s_export_reg[i].library_index].externally_registered;
    }
    return 0;
}

prx_load_result prx_load_module(const prx_module* m, prx_register_fn reg)
{
    prx_load_result r;
    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));

    if (!m || !m->image || m->image_size == 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[prx] load failed: null/empty module\n");
        return r;
    }
    if (!vm_base) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[prx] load failed: vm_base not initialized "
                        "(call vm_init before loading PRX modules)\n");
        return r;
    }

    r.base       = m->base;
    r.image_size = m->image_size;

    uint32_t* library_indices = NULL;
    if (m->library_count && m->libraries) {
        library_indices = (uint32_t*)malloc((size_t)m->library_count * sizeof(uint32_t));
        if (!library_indices) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[prx] out of memory tracking export libraries\n");
            return r;
        }
    }

    /* Step A — place the relocated image into guest RAM at the load base.
     * The bytes already carry base-applied addresses (prx_relocate.py), so the
     * module's data, OPDs and pointer tables are immediately consistent with
     * the lifted code and the OPD-walking dispatcher. */
    memcpy(vm_base + m->base, m->image, m->image_size);

    /* Step B — register every lifted function at its guest address. The lift
     * baked the load base in (--base B), so e->addr is already B + offset and
     * needs no adjustment here. A null host function (rare: a table hole) is
     * skipped rather than registered. */
    if (reg) {
        for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m->func_count; i++) {
            const prx_func_entry* e = &m->funcs[i];
            if (!e->func)
                continue;
            reg((uint32_t)e->addr, e->func);
            r.funcs_registered++;
        }
    }

    if (m->library_count && m->libraries) {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < m->library_count; ++i)
            library_indices[i] = prx_library_register_loaded(m, &m->libraries[i]);
    }

    /* Step C — publish exports as NID -> (base + vaddr) so a title's import
     * resolver can dispatch into this module by NID. Function exports point at
     * an OPD in the freshly-placed image; ps3_indirect_call walks it. */
    uint32_t exports_published = 0;
    if (m->exports) {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < m->export_count; i++) {
            const prx_export* e = &m->exports[i];
            if (e->nid == 0)
                continue;
            uint32_t library_index = UINT32_MAX;
            if (library_indices && e->library_index < m->library_count)
                library_index = library_indices[e->library_index];
            prx_export_register(e->nid, m->base + e->vaddr, library_index);
            exports_published++;
        }
    }
    free(library_indices);

    r.ok = 1;
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[prx] loaded %-12s base=0x%08X size=%u (0x%X) funcs=%u/%llu exports=%u\n",
            m->name ? m->name : "?", m->base, m->image_size, m->image_size,
            r.funcs_registered, (unsigned long long)m->func_count,
            exports_published);
    return r;
}

uint8_t* prx_image_load_file(const char* path, uint32_t* out_size)
{
    FILE* f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[prx] cannot open image '%s'\n", path);
        return NULL;
    }
    if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END) != 0) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    long n = ftell(f);
    if (n <= 0) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET) != 0) { fclose(f); return NULL; }

    uint8_t* buf = (uint8_t*)malloc((size_t)n);
    if (!buf) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    if (fread(buf, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[prx] short read on '%s'\n", path);
        free(buf);
        fclose(f);
        return NULL;
    }
    fclose(f);
    if (out_size)
        *out_size = (uint32_t)n;
    return buf;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\prx\prx_loader.h =====
/*
 * prx_loader.h — runtime loader for statically-recompiled PS3 PRX modules.
 *
 * A relocatable PRX (libsre, libresc, ...) is brought into a static recompile
 * in three artifacts produced offline:
 *
 *   1. tools/prx_relocate.py  -> a LINKED image: the PRX segments flattened to
 *      a base-0 blob with every PT_SCE_PPURELA relocation pre-applied at a
 *      fixed load base B (value = B + addend). The image bytes are final.
 *   2. tools/ppu_lifter.py --base B --symbol-prefix P_  -> host C functions for
 *      the module's code, with B-based guest addresses and P_-namespaced
 *      symbols (P_func_*, P_function_table[]) so they link beside the title.
 *   3. The namespaced P_function_table[] (a func_entry array) maps each guest
 *      address (B + offset) to its lifted host function.
 *
 * At runtime this loader does the two things that turn those artifacts into a
 * live module:
 *
 *   A. Copies the relocated image into guest RAM at B, so the module's data,
 *      function descriptors (OPDs) and pointer tables are visible to both the
 *      lifted code (vm_read*) and the host indirect-call dispatcher (OPD walk).
 *   B. Registers every lifted function at its guest address in the host
 *      dispatch table, so guest bctrl/branch through a B-region address lands
 *      in the right host function.
 *
 * The loader is intentionally decoupled from any one title: the host supplies
 * the dispatch registrar (a function pointer) and the guest-memory base. This
 * mirrors the existing cross-repo seam (the runtime owns mechanism; the game
 * owns its dispatch table).
 */
#ifndef PS3RECOMP_PRX_LOADER_H
#define PS3RECOMP_PRX_LOADER_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Binary-compatible with the func_entry the PPU lifter emits, so a caller can
 * pass (const prx_func_entry*)libsre_function_table directly. */
typedef struct {
    uint64_t    addr;            /* guest address = load base + func offset */
    void      (*func)(void* ctx);/* lifted host function (takes ppu_context*) */
    const char* name;            /* symbol name (for diagnostics) */
} prx_func_entry;

/* One exported symbol: a NID and the OPD/function vaddr it points at, both
 * base-0 as read from the PRX export table. The loader rebases the vaddr to the
 * module's load base when it registers the export. */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t nid;          /* import/export hash */
    uint32_t vaddr;        /* base-0 OPD vaddr (function) or data vaddr (var) */
    uint32_t library_index;/* index in prx_module.libraries, or UINT32_MAX */
} prx_export;

/* One PRX export-library descriptor in the module's export table. vaddr points
 * at the 0x1c-byte descriptor inside the relocated guest image. */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t vaddr;
    const char* name;
} prx_library_descriptor;

typedef struct {
    const char*           name;        /* "libsre", "libresc", ... */
    uint32_t              base;        /* guest load base B (must match lift) */
    const uint8_t*        image;       /* relocated linked image bytes */
    uint32_t              image_size;  /* image length = PRX memsz */
    const prx_func_entry* funcs;       /* namespaced function_table[] */
    uint64_t              func_count;  /* function_table_count */
    const prx_export*     exports;     /* NID -> base-0 vaddr (from elf_parser) */
    uint32_t              export_count;
    const prx_library_descriptor* libraries; /* export-library descriptors */
    uint32_t              library_count;
} prx_module;

/* Host-provided dispatch registrar: bind a guest address to a host function.
 * For flOw this is dispatch_register_external. */
typedef void (*prx_register_fn)(uint32_t guest_addr, void (*host)(void*));

/* Result of a load. */
typedef struct {
    int      ok;                 /* 1 on success, 0 on error */
    uint32_t funcs_registered;   /* how many entries were registered */
    uint32_t base;               /* echo of the load base */
    uint32_t image_size;         /* echo of the image size */
} prx_load_result;

/*
 * Load one relocated PRX module into the live process.
 *
 *   m   — the module description (image bytes + namespaced function table).
 *   reg — the host dispatch registrar (NULL skips registration, e.g. for a
 *         data-only image or a dry run).
 *
 * Copies m->image into guest RAM at m->base (via the runtime's vm_base) and
 * registers every function. Returns a result struct; on failure ok==0 and the
 * reason is logged to stderr. Safe to call once per module at startup.
 */
prx_load_result prx_load_module(const prx_module* m, prx_register_fn reg);

/*
 * Convenience: read a linked image (.bin from prx_relocate.py) off disk into a
 * malloc'd buffer. Returns the buffer (caller frees) and writes the size to
 * *out_size, or NULL on error. Useful for tests and file-backed integration;
 * production builds may instead embed the image as a byte array.
 */
uint8_t* prx_image_load_file(const char* path, uint32_t* out_size);

/*
 * Export registry — the seam that lets a title's NID-import resolver call into
 * a loaded PRX. prx_load_module records every export as NID -> (base + vaddr).
 * A title's import dispatcher calls prx_resolve_export(nid); on a non-zero
 * result it points CTR at that guest address and invokes the normal indirect
 * dispatcher (OPD walk -> registered host function), instead of falling back to
 * its HLE stub. This is what turns flOw's cellSpurs imports into real libsre.
 *
 * Returns the guest address (load base + export vaddr) for nid, or 0 if no
 * loaded module exports it.
 */
uint32_t prx_resolve_export(uint32_t nid);

/* Number of exports currently registered (diagnostics/tests). */
uint32_t prx_export_registry_count(void);

/* Associate a guest library descriptor with a loaded PRX export library.
 * Returns 1 when it matched and retained the RPCS3-style external-loaded flag. */
int prx_register_library_descriptor(const uint8_t descriptor[0x1C],
                                    const char** out_library_name);

/* Whether the loaded PRX library associated with this exported NID has been
 * externally registered. NIDs with no library metadata return 0. */
int prx_export_library_is_registered(uint32_t nid);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* PS3RECOMP_PRX_LOADER_H */

===== FILE: \runtime\prx\tests\test_prx_loader.cpp =====
/*
 * test_prx_loader.cpp — exercises prx_load_module against the REAL relocated
 * libsre artifact (962 lifted functions @ base 0x30000000), not a mock image.
 *
 * It proves the loader's two responsibilities end to end:
 *   A. the relocated image lands in guest RAM at the load base, byte-exact
 *      (verified against a known ADDR32 relocation site), and
 *   B. every lifted function is registered at its guest address, and a looked-
 *      up entry returns the correct host function pointer from the namespaced
 *      libsre_function_table.
 *
 * Build (PS3RECOMP_DIR = ps3recomp checkout, FLOW = flOw checkout):
 *   clang++ -std=c++17 -O1 \
 *     $PS3RECOMP_DIR/runtime/prx/prx_loader.c \
 *     $FLOW/prx/libsre_ns/ppu_recomp.c \
 *     $PS3RECOMP_DIR/runtime/prx/tests/test_prx_loader.cpp \
 *     -I$PS3RECOMP_DIR/runtime/prx -I$FLOW/prx/libsre_ns \
 *     -o test_prx_loader.exe
 *   ./test_prx_loader.exe <path to libsre.linked.bin>
 */
#include "ppu_recomp.h"      /* libsre header: ppu_context, func_entry,
                                libsre_function_table[] (extern "C") */
#include "prx_loader.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <cstdint>
#include <windows.h>

/* libsre's namespaced table (declared extern "C" in its header). */
extern "C" const func_entry libsre_function_table[];
extern "C" const uint64_t    libsre_function_table_count;

/* libsre's export table (NID -> base-0 vaddr), from tools/prx_exports.py. */
extern "C" const prx_export libsre_exports[];
extern "C" const uint32_t    libsre_export_count;

/* ---- runtime symbols the lifted libsre object links against ------------- */
extern "C" uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
extern "C" PPU_THREAD_LOCAL void (*g_trampoline_fn)(void*) = nullptr;

static inline uint64_t guest(uint64_t a) { return (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(vm_base + a); }
extern "C" uint8_t  vm_read8 (uint64_t a){ return *(uint8_t*) (vm_base + a); }
extern "C" uint16_t vm_read16(uint64_t a){ uint16_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base+a, 2); return v; }
extern "C" uint32_t vm_read32(uint64_t a){ uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base+a, 4); return v; }
extern "C" uint64_t vm_read64(uint64_t a){ uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base+a, 8); return v; }
extern "C" void vm_write8 (uint64_t a, uint8_t  v){ *(uint8_t*)(vm_base+a)=v; }
extern "C" void vm_write16(uint64_t a, uint16_t v){ memcpy(vm_base+a,&v,2); }
extern "C" void vm_write32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v){ memcpy(vm_base+a,&v,4); }
extern "C" void vm_write64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v){ memcpy(vm_base+a,&v,8); }
extern "C" void lv2_syscall(ppu_context*) {}
extern "C" void ps3_indirect_call(ppu_context*) {}

/* ---- mock dispatch registrar ------------------------------------------- */
struct Reg { uint32_t addr; void (*fn)(void*); };
static Reg  g_reg[4096];
static int  g_reg_n = 0;
static void mock_register(uint32_t addr, void (*fn)(void*)) {
    if (g_reg_n < (int)(sizeof(g_reg)/sizeof(g_reg[0])))
        g_reg[g_reg_n++] = { addr, fn };
}
static void (*reg_lookup(uint32_t addr))(void*) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_reg_n; i++) if (g_reg[i].addr == addr) return g_reg[i].fn;
    return nullptr;
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    const char* img_path = argc > 1 ? argv[1]
                                    : "D:/recomp/ps3games/flow/prx/libsre.linked.bin";
    const uint32_t BASE = 0x30000000;

    /* Reserve guest address space (like the real runtime) and commit just the
     * PRX window — reserving 0x30000000+ costs only address space, not RAM. */
    const size_t span = (size_t)BASE + 0x00100000;
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)VirtualAlloc(nullptr, span, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS);
    if (!vm_base) { fprintf(stderr, "VirtualAlloc reserve failed\n"); return 2; }
    if (!VirtualAlloc(vm_base + BASE, 0x00080000, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "VirtualAlloc commit failed\n"); return 2;
    }

    uint32_t img_size = 0;
    uint8_t* img = prx_image_load_file(img_path, &img_size);
    if (!img) { fprintf(stderr, "could not load %s\n", img_path); return 2; }
    printf("  loaded image: %u bytes from %s\n", img_size, img_path);

    prx_module m;
    memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
    m.name       = "libsre";
    m.base       = BASE;
    m.image      = img;
    m.image_size = img_size;
    m.funcs        = (const prx_func_entry*)libsre_function_table;
    m.func_count   = libsre_function_table_count;
    m.exports      = libsre_exports;
    m.export_count = libsre_export_count;

    prx_load_result r = prx_load_module(&m, mock_register);

    int ok = 1;

    /* (1) load succeeded */
    printf("  [LOAD      ] ok=%d base=0x%08X size=%u                 %s\n",
           r.ok, r.base, r.image_size, r.ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= r.ok;

    /* (2) relocated image is byte-exact in guest RAM: the ADDR32 site at file
     *     offset 0x1DB38 must read BASE+0x1DCA4 (verified independently when
     *     the image was relocated). prx_relocate.py stores values big-endian
     *     (PS3), so byte-swap the native read before comparing. */
    uint32_t raw = vm_read32(BASE + 0x1DB38);
    uint32_t got = _byteswap_ulong(raw);
    uint32_t exp = BASE + 0x1DCA4;
    int img_ok = (got == exp);
    printf("  [IMAGE@0x30...1DB38] = 0x%08X  expect 0x%08X          %s\n",
           got, exp, img_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= img_ok;

    /* (3) every function registered */
    int count_ok = (r.funcs_registered == libsre_function_table_count) &&
                   (g_reg_n == (int)libsre_function_table_count);
    printf("  [REGISTER  ] registered=%u table=%llu mock=%d           %s\n",
           r.funcs_registered,
           (unsigned long long)libsre_function_table_count, g_reg_n,
           count_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= count_ok;

    /* (4) the registered entry for the module's first function resolves to the
     *     exact host pointer the namespaced table holds. */
    uint32_t f0_addr = (uint32_t)libsre_function_table[0].addr;
    void (*f0_tbl)(void*) = (void(*)(void*))libsre_function_table[0].func;
    void (*f0_reg)(void*) = reg_lookup(f0_addr);
    int map_ok = (f0_reg != nullptr) && (f0_reg == f0_tbl) &&
                 (f0_addr == BASE);  /* first function sits at the load base */
    printf("  [DISPATCH  ] 0x%08X -> %p (table %p)                %s\n",
           f0_addr, (void*)f0_reg, (void*)f0_tbl, map_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= map_ok;

    /* (5) IMPORT RESOLUTION — the piece-3 payoff. flOw imports
     *     cellSpursInitialize by NID 0xACFC8DBC; libsre exports it at OPD
     *     vaddr 0x03127C. The registry must resolve the NID to BASE+0x03127C,
     *     and walking that OPD in guest RAM must land on a function that the
     *     loader registered (i.e. the import would dispatch into real libsre,
     *     not the HLE stub). */
    const uint32_t NID_cellSpursInitialize = 0xACFC8DBC;
    uint32_t opd = prx_resolve_export(NID_cellSpursInitialize);
    uint32_t want_opd = BASE + 0x03127C;
    int reg_count_ok = (prx_export_registry_count() == libsre_export_count);
    int resolve_ok = (opd == want_opd);
    printf("  [EXPORT    ] registry=%u expect=%u                       %s\n",
           prx_export_registry_count(), libsre_export_count,
           reg_count_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    printf("  [RESOLVE   ] cellSpursInitialize NID 0x%08X -> 0x%08X  %s\n",
           NID_cellSpursInitialize, opd, resolve_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= reg_count_ok & resolve_ok;

    if (resolve_ok) {
        /* Walk the OPD exactly as ps3_indirect_call would: first word = code
         * address (big-endian in guest RAM). It must be a registered function. */
        uint32_t code = _byteswap_ulong(vm_read32(opd));
        void (*fn)(void*) = reg_lookup(code);
        int opd_ok = (fn != nullptr);
        printf("  [OPD WALK  ] *0x%08X = code 0x%08X -> host %p          %s\n",
               opd, code, (void*)fn, opd_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
        ok &= opd_ok;
    }

    printf("\n  %s\n", ok ? "ALL PASS" : "FAILURES PRESENT");
    free(img);
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\ps3_console.cpp =====
/* Host console policy for the game runner.
 *
 * Keep the guest's sys_tty_write stream separate from host diagnostics, decode
 * Japanese CP932 text to UTF-8 and keep the guest TTY stream separate from
 * host diagnostics. Host stdout/stderr otherwise pass through unchanged.
 */
#include "ps3_console.h"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <io.h>
#include <share.h>
#include <Windows.h>
#else
#include <cerrno>
#include <iconv.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif

namespace {

struct CapturedStream {
    int original_fd = -1;
    std::thread pump;
};

std::array<CapturedStream, 2> g_streams;
std::mutex g_init_mutex;
std::mutex g_tty_mutex;
bool g_initialized = false;
std::atomic<bool> g_shutting_down{false};
FILE* g_tty_file = nullptr;
std::string g_tty_path;
bool g_tty_open_failed = false;
std::string g_tty_pending;

void write_fd(int fd, const char* data, size_t length)
{
    while (length) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        const unsigned int chunk = static_cast<unsigned int>(
            (std::min)(length, static_cast<size_t>(0x7fffffff)));
        const int written = _write(fd, data, chunk);
#else
        const ssize_t written = ::write(fd, data, length);
#endif
        if (written <= 0) return;
        data += written;
        length -= static_cast<size_t>(written);
    }
}

void pump_stream(int read_fd, int original_fd)
{
    std::string line;
    std::array<char, 4096> chunk{};
    for (;;) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        const int got = _read(read_fd, chunk.data(), static_cast<unsigned int>(chunk.size()));
#else
        const ssize_t got = ::read(read_fd, chunk.data(), chunk.size());
#endif
        if (got <= 0) break;
        for (int i = 0; i < got; ++i) {
            const char c = chunk[static_cast<size_t>(i)];
            line.push_back(c);
            if (c == '\n' || c == '\r' || line.size() >= 1024u * 1024u) {
                write_fd(original_fd, line.data(), line.size());
                line.clear();
            }
        }
    }
    if (!line.empty())
        write_fd(original_fd, line.data(), line.size());
#ifdef _WIN32
    _close(read_fd);
#else
    ::close(read_fd);
#endif
}

bool redirect_stream(int fd)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    int pipe_fds[2] = {-1, -1};
    if (_pipe(pipe_fds, 64 * 1024, _O_BINARY | _O_NOINHERIT) != 0) return false;
    const int original = _dup(fd);
    if (original < 0 || _dup2(pipe_fds[1], fd) != 0) {
        if (original >= 0) _close(original);
        _close(pipe_fds[0]);
        _close(pipe_fds[1]);
        return false;
    }
    _close(pipe_fds[1]);
#else
    int pipe_fds[2] = {-1, -1};
    if (::pipe(pipe_fds) != 0) return false;
    const int original = ::dup(fd);
    if (original < 0 || ::dup2(pipe_fds[1], fd) < 0) {
        if (original >= 0) ::close(original);
        ::close(pipe_fds[0]);
        ::close(pipe_fds[1]);
        return false;
    }
    ::close(pipe_fds[1]);
#endif
    g_streams[static_cast<size_t>(fd - 1)].original_fd = original;
    g_streams[static_cast<size_t>(fd - 1)].pump =
        std::thread(pump_stream, pipe_fds[0], original);
    return true;
}

bool enabled_env(const char* name)
{
    const char* value = std::getenv(name);
    return value && *value && *value != '0' && std::strcmp(value, "false") != 0;
}

bool cp932_selected()
{
    const char* encoding = std::getenv("PS3_TTY_ENCODING");
    return !encoding || !*encoding || std::strcmp(encoding, "cp932") == 0 ||
        std::strcmp(encoding, "sjis") == 0 || std::strcmp(encoding, "shift-jis") == 0;
}

std::string decode_cp932(const char* bytes, size_t length)
{
    std::string utf8;
    utf8.reserve(length * 2);
#ifdef _WIN32
    size_t offset = 0;
    while (offset < length) {
        const unsigned char first = static_cast<unsigned char>(bytes[offset]);
        size_t char_length = 1;
        if (((first >= 0x81 && first <= 0x9f) || (first >= 0xe0 && first <= 0xfc))) {
            if (offset + 1 >= length) {
                utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
                ++offset;
                continue;
            }
            const unsigned char trail = static_cast<unsigned char>(bytes[offset + 1]);
            if ((trail >= 0x40 && trail <= 0x7e) || (trail >= 0x80 && trail <= 0xfc))
                char_length = 2;
            else {
                utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
                ++offset;
                continue;
            }
        }
        wchar_t wide[4]{};
        const int wide_count = MultiByteToWideChar(932, MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS,
            bytes + offset, static_cast<int>(char_length), wide, 4);
        if (wide_count <= 0) {
            utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
            ++offset;
            continue;
        }
        char encoded[16]{};
        const int encoded_count = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS,
            wide, wide_count, encoded, static_cast<int>(sizeof(encoded)), nullptr, nullptr);
        if (encoded_count > 0) utf8.append(encoded, static_cast<size_t>(encoded_count));
        else utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
        offset += char_length;
    }
#else
    iconv_t converter = iconv_open("UTF-8", "CP932");
    if (converter == (iconv_t)-1) return std::string(bytes, length);
    size_t offset = 0;
    while (offset < length) {
        const unsigned char first = static_cast<unsigned char>(bytes[offset]);
        size_t char_length = 1;
        if ((first >= 0x81 && first <= 0x9f) || (first >= 0xe0 && first <= 0xfc)) {
            if (offset + 1 < length) char_length = 2;
            else {
                utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
                ++offset;
                continue;
            }
        }
        char* input = const_cast<char*>(bytes + offset);
        size_t input_left = char_length;
        char output[16]{};
        char* out = output;
        size_t output_left = sizeof(output);
        const size_t rc = iconv(converter, &input, &input_left, &out, &output_left);
        if (rc == static_cast<size_t>(-1) || input_left != 0) {
            utf8.append("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
            ++offset;
            iconv(converter, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
            continue;
        }
        utf8.append(output, static_cast<size_t>(out - output));
        offset += char_length;
    }
    iconv_close(converter);
#endif
    return utf8;
}

std::string tty_to_utf8(const char* bytes, size_t length)
{
    if (cp932_selected())
        return decode_cp932(bytes, length);
    return std::string(bytes, length); /* utf8 or raw */
}

} // namespace

extern "C" void ps3_console_init(void)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_init_mutex);
    if (g_initialized || g_shutting_down.load()) return;
#ifdef _WIN32
    SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8);
#endif
    std::setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IONBF, 0);
    std::setvbuf(stderr, nullptr, _IONBF, 0);
    redirect_stream(1);
    redirect_stream(2);
    g_initialized = true;
    std::atexit(ps3_console_shutdown);
}

extern "C" void ps3_console_shutdown(void)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_init_mutex);
    if (!g_initialized) return;
    g_shutting_down.store(true);
    std::fflush(stdout);
    std::fflush(stderr);
    for (int fd = 1; fd <= 2; ++fd) {
        CapturedStream& stream = g_streams[static_cast<size_t>(fd - 1)];
        if (stream.original_fd < 0) continue;
#ifdef _WIN32
        _dup2(stream.original_fd, fd);
#else
        ::dup2(stream.original_fd, fd);
#endif
    }
    for (int fd = 1; fd <= 2; ++fd) {
        CapturedStream& stream = g_streams[static_cast<size_t>(fd - 1)];
        if (stream.pump.joinable()) stream.pump.join();
        if (stream.original_fd >= 0) {
#ifdef _WIN32
            _close(stream.original_fd);
#else
            ::close(stream.original_fd);
#endif
            stream.original_fd = -1;
        }
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> tty_lock(g_tty_mutex);
        if (!g_tty_pending.empty()) {
            const std::string replacement("\xef\xbf\xbd", 3);
            if (g_tty_file) std::fwrite(replacement.data(), 1, replacement.size(), g_tty_file);
            g_tty_pending.clear();
        }
        if (g_tty_file) {
            std::fclose(g_tty_file);
            g_tty_file = nullptr;
        }
    }
    g_initialized = false;
}

extern "C" void ps3_console_write_tty(uint32_t channel, const void* bytes, size_t length)
{
    (void)channel;
    if (!bytes || !length) return;

    const char* setting = std::getenv("PS3_TTY_LOG");
    const bool log_disabled = setting && (!*setting || *setting == '0' || std::strcmp(setting, "off") == 0);
    const bool echo = enabled_env("PS3_TTY_STDOUT");
    if (log_disabled && !echo) return;

    ps3_console_init();
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_tty_mutex);
    if (g_shutting_down.load()) return;

    std::string raw;
    if (cp932_selected()) {
        raw.swap(g_tty_pending);
        raw.append(static_cast<const char*>(bytes), length);
        if (!raw.empty()) {
            const unsigned char last = static_cast<unsigned char>(raw.back());
            if ((last >= 0x81 && last <= 0x9f) || (last >= 0xe0 && last <= 0xfc)) {
                g_tty_pending.assign(1, raw.back());
                raw.pop_back();
            }
        }
    } else {
        raw.assign(static_cast<const char*>(bytes), length);
    }
    const std::string text = tty_to_utf8(raw.data(), raw.size());
    if (text.empty()) return;

    if (!log_disabled) {
        if (!g_tty_file) {
            g_tty_path = setting && *setting ? setting : "ps3_tty.log";
#ifdef _WIN32
            g_tty_file = _fsopen(g_tty_path.c_str(), "ab", _SH_DENYNO);
#else
            g_tty_file = std::fopen(g_tty_path.c_str(), "ab");
#endif
            if (g_tty_file) std::setvbuf(g_tty_file, nullptr, _IOFBF, 64 * 1024);
            else if (!g_tty_open_failed) {
                g_tty_open_failed = true;
                std::fprintf(stderr, "[tty] could not open log file '%s'\n", g_tty_path.c_str());
            }
        }
        if (g_tty_file) {
            std::fwrite(text.data(), 1, text.size(), g_tty_file);
            if (text.find('\n') != std::string::npos) std::fflush(g_tty_file);
        }
    }

    if (echo) {
        const int output_fd = g_streams[0].original_fd >= 0 ? g_streams[0].original_fd : 1;
        write_fd(output_fd, text.data(), text.size());
    }
}

/* ps3_log.h -- gate for high-volume diagnostic logging.
 * Debug/trace output is opt-in. The game runner defaults to warning-level
 * output, so redirecting stderr does not enable a high-volume trace by itself.
 */
#ifndef PS3_LOG_H
#define PS3_LOG_H

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
static inline int ps3_log_verbose(void)
#else
static __inline int ps3_log_verbose(void)
#endif
{
    /* PS3_VERBOSE explicitly enables or disables these high-volume trace sites.
     * Otherwise PS3_LOG_LEVEL=debug or trace enables them. */
    static int v = -1;
    if (v < 0) {
        const char* e = getenv("PS3_VERBOSE");
        if (e) v = (e[0] && e[0] != '0') ? 1 : 0;
        else {
            const char* level = getenv("PS3_LOG_LEVEL");
            v = level && (strcmp(level, "debug") == 0 || strcmp(level, "trace") == 0);
        }
    }
    return v;
}

#endif /* PS3_LOG_H */


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\spu_channels.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - SPU channel + indirect-branch runtime glue
 *
 * Implements the externs the SPU lifter (tools/spu_lifter.py) emits:
 *   - spu_rdch / spu_rchcnt / spu_wrch : SPU channel access. MFC channels are
 *     routed to the DMA engine (spu_dma.h); mailboxes, signal notification,
 *     events and the decrementer use the spu_context channel fields.
 *   - spu_indirect_branch : resolves ctx->pc to a lifted spu_func_* via a
 *     registry that generated code populates by calling spu_recomp_register().
 *
 * The MFC engine state is kept per spu_context here (spu_context.h does not
 * embed one), in a small lazily-populated registry.
 */

#include "spu_dma.h"
#include "spu_coherency.h" /* lock-line lock + PPU-write coherence bitmap */
#include "spu_helpers.h"   /* spu_splat_u32 / spu_ls_read128 (SMC microstep) */
#include "spu_lockstep.h"
#include "spu_interp.h"    /* spu_lifted_fn / spu_lifted_lookup -- defined below */
#include "ps3emu/ps3_ftrace.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#ifndef _WIN32
#include <sched.h>   /* sched_yield */
#endif
#include <time.h>
#include "../platform/win32_compat.h"
#include "ps3emu/log_first.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* The SPU decrementer ticks at the PS3 timebase, 79.8 MHz -- the same clock
