===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spu_shufb.c =====
/* spu_shufb (pshufb / NEON tbl path) must match the byte-loop reference for
 * every selector class: a/b sources, 0x00 / 0xFF / 0x80 specials. Build with
 * -msse4.1 on x86 so the SIMD version is the one under test (NEON is always
 * on for arm64). */
#include "../spu_helpers.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void)
{
#if !defined(__SSE4_1__) && !defined(__ARM_NEON)
    puts("test_spu_shufb: built without SSE4.1 or NEON, nothing to compare");
    return 0;
#else
    srand(12345);
    /* Every selector in every destination position, with unique source bytes.
     * This catches endian mapping and adjacent-byte contamination in SIMD masks. */
    for (int sel = 0; sel < 256; ++sel) {
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 16; ++lane) {
            u128 a, b, c;
            for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
                a._u8[i] = (uint8_t)(i + 1);
                b._u8[i] = (uint8_t)(i + 33);
                c._u8[i] = (uint8_t)(i * 17);
            }
            c._u8[lane] = (uint8_t)sel;
            u128 x = spu_shufb(a, b, c), y = spu_shufb_ref(a, b, c);
            if (memcmp(&x, &y, 16)) {
                printf("test_spu_shufb: selector %02X lane %d mismatch\n", sel, lane);
                return 1;
            }
        }
    }
    for (int it = 0; it < 200000; it++) {
        u128 a, b, c;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
            a._u8[i] = (uint8_t)rand(); b._u8[i] = (uint8_t)rand();
            c._u8[i] = (uint8_t)rand();          /* covers all 256 selector values */
        }
        u128 x = spu_shufb(a, b, c), y = spu_shufb_ref(a, b, c);
        if (memcmp(&x, &y, 16)) {
            printf("test_spu_shufb: MISMATCH at iteration %d\n", it);
            return 1;
        }
    }
    puts("test_spu_shufb: ok (200000 random cases)");
    return 0;
#endif
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spu_taskset_elf_flags.c =====
/* Synthetic taskset requeue boundary. The driver inserts the unchanged production
 * ELF parser and scheduler functions; only host dispatch is intercepted so no
 * SPU thread or original title image is required. */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
typedef int32_t LONG;
static LONG InterlockedExchange(volatile LONG* value, LONG replacement)
{ LONG old = *value; *value = replacement; return old; }
static void Sleep(unsigned ms) { (void)ms; }
uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t g_ydkj_real_taskset_ea, g_ydkj_real_taskid;
static unsigned dispatches;
static const uint8_t* dispatched_image;
static uint32_t dispatched_size, dispatched_context;
/* The scheduler updates the taskset's bitset line under the lock-line lock;
 * single-threaded here, so the lock and the coherency note are no-ops. */
void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t ea) { (void)ea; }
static int spu_workload_dispatch_async(const uint8_t* image, uint32_t size, uint32_t context)
{
    dispatches++; dispatched_image = image; dispatched_size = size;
    dispatched_context = context; return 1;
}
/* Taskset2 exit-code slot: these tasksets are not registered as Taskset2,
 * where production returns without touching memory. */
static void spu_taskset2_set_exit(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t task, int exited, uint32_t code)
{ (void)taskset_ea; (void)task; (void)exited; (void)code; }
/* PRODUCTION_FUNCTIONS */
static unsigned passed, failed;
#define CHECK(test, message) do { if (test) passed++; else { failed++; fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s\n", message); } } while (0)
enum { TASKSET = 0x10000, ELF = 0x30000, CONTEXT = 0x50000 };
static void be16(uint8_t* p, uint16_t v) { p[0] = v >> 8; p[1] = v; }
static void be32(uint8_t* p, uint32_t v)
{ p[0] = v >> 24; p[1] = v >> 16; p[2] = v >> 8; p[3] = v; }
static void setup(uint32_t flags, int pending)
{
    memset(vm_base, 0, 0x400000); memset(s_ts_run, 0, sizeof(s_ts_run));
    s_ts_lock = 0; dispatches = 0; dispatched_image = NULL;
    dispatched_size = dispatched_context = 0;
    g_ydkj_real_taskset_ea = g_ydkj_real_taskid = 0;
    uint8_t* image = vm_base + ELF;
    memcpy(image, "\177ELF", 4); image[4] = 1; image[5] = 2; image[6] = 1;
    be16(image + 0x10, 2); be16(image + 0x12, 23); be32(image + 0x14, 1);
    be32(image + 0x18, 0x3000); be32(image + 0x1C, 52);
    be16(image + 0x28, 52); be16(image + 0x2A, 32); be16(image + 0x2C, 1);
    be32(image + 52, 1); be32(image + 56, 84); be32(image + 60, 0x3000);
    be32(image + 68, 16); be32(image + 72, 16); be32(image + 76, 5);
    be32(image + 80, 16); memset(image + 84, 0x5A, 16);
    uint8_t* ts = vm_base + TASKSET;
    ts[pending ? 0x20 : 0x10] = 0x80; ts[0x30] = 0x80;
    be32(ts + 0x80 + 0x14, ELF | flags);
    be32(ts + 0x80 + 0x1C, CONTEXT);
    /* Unrelated TaskInfo metadata must survive address normalization. */
    be32(ts + 0x80, 0x11223344); be32(ts + 0x90, 0xAABBCCDD);
}
int main(void)
{
    vm_base = calloc(1, 0x400000); if (!vm_base) return 2;
    for (uint32_t flags = 0; flags < 8; flags++) for (int pending = 0; pending < 2; pending++) {
        setup(flags, pending); uint8_t before[48];
        memcpy(before, vm_base + TASKSET + 0x80, sizeof(before));
        spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
        CHECK(dispatches == 1, "ready/pending task dispatches with ELF metadata tags");
        CHECK(dispatched_image == vm_base + ELF, "dispatch uses ELF base, not tagged address");
        CHECK(dispatched_size == 100, "real parser receives synthetic ELF header");
        CHECK(dispatched_context == CONTEXT, "context argument is preserved");
        CHECK(g_ydkj_real_taskset_ea == TASKSET && g_ydkj_real_taskid == 0,
              "requeued task keeps its taskset and slot identity");
        CHECK(memcmp(before, vm_base + TASKSET + 0x80, sizeof(before)) == 0,
              "TaskInfo flags and all other metadata remain unchanged");
        CHECK((s_ts_run[0].running[0] & 0x80) != 0, "submitted task is marked in host run table");
        CHECK(vm_base[TASKSET + 0x20] == 0, "pending-ready bit consumed on submission");
    }
    setup(1, 0); vm_base[TASKSET + 0x30] = 0;
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "disabled task is not dispatched");
    setup(1, 0); ts_running(TASKSET)[0] = 0x80;
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "already running task is not duplicated");
    setup(1, 0); vm_base[TASKSET + 0x10] = 0;
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "enabled task without work is not dispatched");
    setup(1, 0); vm_base[ELF] = 0;
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "invalid untagged ELF is not dispatched");
    CHECK(s_ts_run[0].running[0] == 0, "invalid ELF leaves host run table clear");
    CHECK(vm_base[TASKSET + 0x10] == 0x80, "invalid ELF preserves ready state");
    setup(7, 1); be32(vm_base + TASKSET + 0x94, 7);
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 127);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "metadata-only null ELF is not dispatched");
    CHECK(vm_base[TASKSET + 0x20] == 0x80, "null ELF preserves pending state");
    setup(1, 0); vm_base[TASKSET + 0x20] = 0x80; ts_running(TASKSET)[0] = 0x80;
    spu_taskset_task_exited(TASKSET, 0);
    CHECK(dispatches == 0, "exiting task is not restarted");
    CHECK(vm_base[TASKSET + 0x10] == 0 && vm_base[TASKSET + 0x20] == 0 &&
          vm_base[TASKSET + 0x30] == 0 && s_ts_run[0].running[0] == 0,
          "real exiting task ready/pending/enabled/run state is cleared");
    free(vm_base);
    printf("taskset ELF address flags: %u passed, %u failed\n", passed, failed);
    return failed ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spu_taskset_wake.c =====
/*
 * A task parked in WAIT_SIGNAL wakes when another SPU signals it
 * (runtime/spu/spu_workload.c, runtime/spu/spu_channels.c).
 *
 * libspurs signals a task from the SPU side: a GETLLAR/PUTLLC loop that sets
 * the target's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset. The parked task checks
 * that guest bit, but it sleeps on a host condition variable that only the
 * PPU-side cellSpursSendSignal used to broadcast. An SPU-side signal was
 * therefore seen only when the waiter's 1 s timed wait ran out. Twisted
 * Metal's post-FX pipeline chains six tasks that way, several times a frame,
 * and took 4 s or more per frame.
 *
 * So the assertions are on the waiter's latency: after an SPU commits the
 * waiter's bit with PUTLLC, or with PUTLLUC, the waiter is back well inside
 * the 1 s timeout. The cases that must stay parked are here too: a commit to
 * the same line that sets another task's bit, and a commit to the bitset of
 * another taskset. A spurious wake is allowed, a spurious return is not.
 *
 * spu_channels.c is compiled in rather than linked, because spu_mfc_atomic()
 * is file-static: the same reason test_spu_lockline_peer.c does it.
 *
 * Build:
 *   clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime/spu -I runtime/platform \
 *         -o /tmp/test_spu_taskset_wake \
 *         runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_taskset_wake.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_drain.c runtime/spu/spu_lockstep.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_coherency.c runtime/spu/spu_workload.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spurs_policy.c runtime/spu/spurs_job.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_tsp_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_vm_pagemap.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spurs_policy_blob_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_interp.c \
 *         runtime/platform/win32_compat.c -lpthread -lm
 *
 * Exit code: 0 if all passed, 1 if any failed. Final line prints a summary.
 */

#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

/* Guest memory. The atomic path indexes straight off this, so it has to cover
 * every EA the test uses. */
static uint8_t g_guest_mem[1u << 20];
uint8_t* vm_base = g_guest_mem;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;

/* The unit under test. */
#include "../spu_channels.c"

int  spu_taskset_wait_signal(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);
void spu_taskset_parked_add(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId, uint32_t wait_obj);
void spu_taskset_parked_del(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);
void spu_taskset_signal_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Harness
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
static int g_pass, g_fail;
static const char* g_current = "(none)";

#define TEST(name) g_current = (name)

#define CHECK(cond) do {                                          \
    if (cond) { g_pass++; }                                       \
    else {                                                        \
        g_fail++;                                                 \
        fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s\n  at %s:%d: %s\n",             \
                g_current, __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond);            \
    }                                                             \
} while (0)

/* Two tasksets, 128-byte aligned as the SDK requires. The signalled bitset is
 * at +0x40 (CSTS_SIGNALLED in libs/spurs/spurs_taskset.h, which is not included
 * here: it declares spurs_pm_build_context with the signature the stub below
 * cannot have), so it shares its line with the other task bitsets. Bit 0 is
 * the most significant bit of the first big-endian word. */
#define SIGNALLED  0x40u
#define TASKSET_A  0x00030000u
#define TASKSET_B  0x00032000u
#define LSA        0x00001000u

/* The task that parks, and a second one whose bit shares the word. */
#define WAITER     3u
#define OTHER      5u

/* Well under the waiter's 1 s timed wait: a wake that only came from the
 * timeout lands after this. */
#define WAKE_MS    400u
/* How long a waiter that must stay parked is watched. */
#define STAY_MS    300u

static spu_context g_spu;   /* 256 KB of local store: not on the stack */

static uint64_t now_ms(void)
{
    struct timespec ts;
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000u + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec / 1000000u;
}

static void sleep_ms(unsigned ms)
{
    struct timespec ts = { (time_t)(ms / 1000u), (long)(ms % 1000u) * 1000000L };
    nanosleep(&ts, NULL);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Driving the real channel path, as test_spu_lockline_peer.c does
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
static void wrch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel, uint32_t v)
{
    spu_wrch(ctx, channel, spu_make_preferred_u32(v));
}

static void spu_atomic(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa, uint32_t ea, uint32_t cmd)
{
    wrch(ctx, MFC_LSA, lsa);
    wrch(ctx, MFC_EAH, 0);
    wrch(ctx, MFC_EAL, ea);
    wrch(ctx, MFC_Cmd, cmd);
}

/* What libspurs does on the SPU: reserve the taskset's line, set the task's
 * bit in the signalled bitset in local store, commit. `cmd` is the commit:
 * PUTLLC after the reservation, or PUTLLUC. */
static void spu_signal(uint32_t taskset, uint32_t task, uint32_t cmd)
{
    spu_atomic(&g_spu, LSA, taskset, MFC_GETLLAR_CMD);
    uint8_t* b = &g_spu.ls[LSA + SIGNALLED + (task / 32u) * 4u];
    const uint32_t mask = (1u << 31) >> (task % 32u);
    b[0] |= (uint8_t)(mask >> 24); b[1] |= (uint8_t)(mask >> 16);
    b[2] |= (uint8_t)(mask >> 8);  b[3] |= (uint8_t)mask;
    spu_atomic(&g_spu, LSA, taskset, cmd);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The parked task: its own host thread, as a lifted task is
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
typedef struct {
    uint32_t taskset, task;
    volatile int returned;
    uint64_t returned_ms;
} waiter;

static void* waiter_main(void* p)
{
    waiter* w = (waiter*)p;
    spu_taskset_parked_add(w->taskset, w->task, 0);
    spu_taskset_wait_signal(w->taskset, w->task);
    spu_taskset_parked_del(w->taskset, w->task);
    w->returned_ms = now_ms();
    __atomic_store_n(&w->returned, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    return NULL;
}

static void park(waiter* w, pthread_t* th, uint32_t taskset, uint32_t task)
{
    memset((void*)w, 0, sizeof(*w));
    w->taskset = taskset;
    w->task = task;
    pthread_create(th, NULL, waiter_main, w);
    sleep_ms(100);   /* let it reach the timed wait: a wake before is not lost
                      * anyway, the bit is checked before it sleeps */
}

/* Wait up to `ms` for the waiter to return; how long it took, or ~0u. */
static uint64_t wait_return(waiter* w, uint64_t since, unsigned ms)
{
    const uint64_t end = now_ms() + ms;
    while (now_ms() < end) {
        if (__atomic_load_n(&w->returned, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return w->returned_ms - since;
        sleep_ms(1);
    }
    return ~(uint64_t)0;
}

static int signalled(uint32_t taskset, uint32_t task)
{
    return (g_guest_mem[taskset + SIGNALLED + task / 8u] >> (7u - task % 8u)) & 1u;
}

static void clear_guest(void)
{
    memset(&g_guest_mem[TASKSET_A], 0, 0x80);
    memset(&g_guest_mem[TASKSET_B], 0, 0x80);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Tests
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
static void test_putllc_signal_wakes(void)
{
    TEST("an SPU PUTLLC setting the waiter's bit wakes it");
    clear_guest();
    waiter w; pthread_t th;
    park(&w, &th, TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    CHECK(!w.returned);
    const uint64_t t = now_ms();
    spu_signal(TASKSET_A, WAITER, MFC_PUTLLC_CMD);
    CHECK(g_spu.atomic_stat == 0);   /* the commit went through */
    const uint64_t took = wait_return(&w, t, WAKE_MS);
    CHECK(took != ~(uint64_t)0);
    if (took == ~(uint64_t)0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "  waiter still parked %u ms after the commit\n", WAKE_MS);
        wait_return(&w, t, 2000);
    }
    pthread_join(th, NULL);
    /* The wait consumed the signal, as on the console. */
    CHECK(!signalled(TASKSET_A, WAITER));
}

static void test_putlluc_signal_wakes(void)
{
    TEST("an SPU PUTLLUC setting the waiter's bit wakes it");
    clear_guest();
    waiter w; pthread_t th;
    park(&w, &th, TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    const uint64_t t = now_ms();
    spu_signal(TASKSET_A, WAITER, MFC_PUTLLUC_CMD);
    const uint64_t took = wait_return(&w, t, WAKE_MS);
    CHECK(took != ~(uint64_t)0);
    if (took == ~(uint64_t)0) wait_return(&w, t, 2000);
    pthread_join(th, NULL);
}

static void test_other_task_stays_parked(void)
{
    TEST("a commit setting another task's bit leaves the waiter parked");
    clear_guest();
    waiter w; pthread_t th;
    park(&w, &th, TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    const uint64_t t = now_ms();
    spu_signal(TASKSET_A, OTHER, MFC_PUTLLC_CMD);
    CHECK(wait_return(&w, t, STAY_MS) == ~(uint64_t)0);
    /* Release it the PPU way, so the thread can be joined. */
    spu_taskset_signal_task(TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    CHECK(wait_return(&w, t, 2000) != ~(uint64_t)0);
    pthread_join(th, NULL);
}

static void test_other_taskset_stays_parked(void)
{
    TEST("a signal to another taskset leaves the waiter parked");
    clear_guest();
    waiter w; pthread_t th;
    park(&w, &th, TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    const uint64_t t = now_ms();
    spu_signal(TASKSET_B, WAITER, MFC_PUTLLC_CMD);
    CHECK(wait_return(&w, t, STAY_MS) == ~(uint64_t)0);
    spu_taskset_signal_task(TASKSET_A, WAITER);
    CHECK(wait_return(&w, t, 2000) != ~(uint64_t)0);
    pthread_join(th, NULL);
}

int main(void)
{
    printf("SPURS task wake on an SPU-side signal\n");
    spu_context_init(&g_spu, 0);   /* points ls at its own store */
    test_putllc_signal_wakes();
    test_putlluc_signal_wakes();
    test_other_task_stays_parked();
    test_other_taskset_stays_parked();
    printf("SPURS task wake on an SPU-side signal: %d passed, %d failed\n", g_pass, g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}

===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spu_thread_image_id.c =====
/* An SPU thread starts in the lifted image its sys_spu_image holds, not in the image that happens to own its entry
 * point. SPU programs all start near the same LS addresses, so two images can have code at one entry, and the
 * entry alone resolves to whichever registered first: the thread ran the other program's code (SoulCalibur II HD's
 * audio engine ran the wrong one). The image's own bytes say which it is.
 *
 * The registry is replaced by a table of two images (A registered first, B second, both with code at 0xD0), and
 * the checks follow what sys_spu_thread_group_start does: spu_thread_image_id, then spu_lifted_thread_setup.
 *
 * clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime -I runtime/syscalls -I runtime/spu -I libs/video
 *   runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_thread_image_id.c runtime/spu/spu_lifted_thread.c -Wl,-dead_strip -pthread
 *   -o /tmp/test_spu_thread_image_id && /tmp/test_spu_thread_image_id
 */
/* Syscall 14's classifier (#341) lives in lv2_lock_line.c, which pulls in the
 * VM map table; nothing here issues syscall 14. */
int64_t lv2_spu_lock_line_classify(uint32_t a, uint64_t f) { (void)a; (void)f; return 0; }
#include "../../syscalls/lv2_register.c"
#include <assert.h>
#include <stdio.h>

uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
void SetLastError(DWORD e) { (void)e; }
uint32_t spurs_port_queue(uint32_t port) { (void)port; return 0; }
int64_t sys_event_flag_set(ppu_context* c) { (void)c; return 0; }

/* --- the registry, reduced to what the lookup needs: two images, both with code at 0xD0 --- */
#define IMG_A 1
#define IMG_B 2
#define IMG_SIZE 64
static uint64_t fp_of_image(int id) { return id == IMG_A ? 0xAAAA0000AAAAull : 0xBBBB0000BBBBull; }
uint64_t spu_workload_fingerprint(const void* data, size_t n)
{
    (void)n;
    const uint8_t c = ((const uint8_t*)data)[0];
    return c == 'A' ? fp_of_image(IMG_A) : c == 'B' ? fp_of_image(IMG_B) : 0x1234ull;   /* anything else: not registered */
}
spu_lifted_entry_fn spu_workload_find_img(uint64_t fp, int* id)
{
    if (fp == fp_of_image(IMG_A)) { *id = IMG_A; return (spu_lifted_entry_fn)(uintptr_t)1; }
    if (fp == fp_of_image(IMG_B)) { *id = IMG_B; return (spu_lifted_entry_fn)(uintptr_t)1; }
    return NULL;
}
size_t spu_elf_image_size(const uint8_t* image, size_t max_avail) { (void)image; return max_avail >= IMG_SIZE ? IMG_SIZE : 0; }
uint32_t ps3_spu_image_source_ea(uint32_t img_ea) { return img_ea; }
/* the entry-point lookup: both images have code at 0xD0 and A registered first */
int spu_image_of_function(uint32_t addr) { return addr == 0xD0 ? IMG_A : -1; }

static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL: "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); fails++; } } while (0)

int main(void)
{
    vm_base = calloc(1, 1u << 20); assert(vm_base);
    ppu_vm_size = 1u << 20;
    vm_base[0x1000] = 'A';                       /* image A's bytes */
    vm_base[0x2000] = 'B';                       /* image B's bytes */
    vm_base[0x3000] = 'X';                       /* bytes of an image nothing registered */

    spu_thread_t* t = spu_alloc_thread(); assert(t);
    static spu_context ctx;
    spu_lifted_thread_desc d;

    t->img_ea = 0x2000;
    CHECK(spu_thread_image_id(t) == IMG_B, "image B's bytes give id %d", spu_thread_image_id(t));
    memset(&d, 0, sizeof d); d.tid = 7; d.entry = 0xD0; d.image_id = spu_thread_image_id(t);
    spu_lifted_thread_setup(&ctx, &d);
    CHECK(ctx.image_id == IMG_B, "the thread starts in image %d, not image B", ctx.image_id);

    t->img_ea = 0x1000;
    CHECK(spu_thread_image_id(t) == IMG_A, "image A's bytes give id %d", spu_thread_image_id(t));

    memset(&d, 0, sizeof d); d.tid = 8; d.entry = 0xD0; d.image_id = 0;     /* what the lookup by entry gives */
    spu_lifted_thread_setup(&ctx, &d);
    CHECK(ctx.image_id == IMG_A, "without an image id the entry point still picks the first image (got %d)", ctx.image_id);

    t->img_ea = 0x3000;
    CHECK(spu_thread_image_id(t) == 0, "an unregistered image gives id %d", spu_thread_image_id(t));
    t->img_ea = 0;
    CHECK(spu_thread_image_id(t) == 0, "a thread with no image gives id %d", spu_thread_image_id(t));

    printf("[spu_thread_image_id] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spu_user_event_port.c =====
/* An SPU's user event (send_event through the interrupt mailbox) goes to the queue its port is bound to.
 *
 * The port is bound by the PPU with sys_spu_thread_connect_event (this SPU thread) or
 * sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads (the group). The SPU thread starts running at
 * sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to those calls, so an event for a port that is not
 * bound yet has to wait for the binding for a while instead of being answered with ENOTCONN at once, which makes
 * the SPU program fail its first request. A binding made with sys_spu_thread_connect_event has to be found as well.
 *
 * clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime -I runtime/syscalls -I runtime/spu -I libs/video
 *   runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_user_event_port.c -Wl,-dead_strip -pthread -o /tmp/test_spu_user_event_port
 *   && /tmp/test_spu_user_event_port
 */
/* Syscall 14's classifier (#341) lives in lv2_lock_line.c, which pulls in the
 * VM map table; nothing here issues syscall 14. */
int64_t lv2_spu_lock_line_classify(uint32_t a, uint64_t f) { (void)a; (void)f; return 0; }
#include "../../syscalls/lv2_register.c"
#include <assert.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <pthread.h>

uint8_t* vm_base;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
void SetLastError(DWORD e) { (void)e; }                       /* the POSIX shim's condition variable reports a timeout */
uint32_t spurs_port_queue(uint32_t port) { (void)port; return 0; }
int64_t sys_event_flag_set(ppu_context* c) { (void)c; return 0; }

/* What the delivery pushes at the queue, recorded instead of sent. */
static uint32_t pushed_queue, pushed_data;
static int pushes;
int sys_event_queue_push_by_id(uint32_t queue_id, uint64_t source, uint64_t d1, uint64_t d2, uint64_t d3)
{
    (void)source; (void)d1; (void)d2;
    pushed_queue = queue_id; pushed_data = (uint32_t)d3; pushes++;
    return 0;
}

static double now_ms(void)
{
    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (double)ts.tv_sec * 1000.0 + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e6;
}

static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL: "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); fails++; } } while (0)

static spu_group_t*  grp;
static spu_thread_t* thr;
static spu_context   spu;

/* sys_spu_thread_connect_event(tid, queue, et = 1, port) */
static void bind_thread(uint32_t queue, uint32_t port)
{
    ppu_context c = {0};
    c.gpr[3] = thr->tid; c.gpr[4] = queue; c.gpr[5] = 1; c.gpr[6] = port;
    assert(sys_spu_thread_connect_event_handler(&c) == 0);
}

/* sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads(group, queue, ports_mask, &port) */
static void bind_group(uint32_t queue, uint32_t port)
{
    ppu_context c = {0};
    c.gpr[3] = grp->id; c.gpr[4] = queue; c.gpr[5] = 1ull << port; c.gpr[6] = 0x100;
    assert(sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads_handler(&c) == (int64_t)CELL_OK);
}

static void reset(void)
{
    memset(&grp->user_event_ports, 0, sizeof grp->user_event_ports);
    thr->evt_bind_n = 0;
    pushes = 0; pushed_queue = 0;
}

typedef struct { int ms; int via_group; uint32_t queue, port; } late_bind;
static void* late_binder(void* p)
{
    late_bind* b = (late_bind*)p;
    struct timespec ts = { 0, b->ms * 1000000L };
    nanosleep(&ts, NULL);
    if (b->via_group) bind_group(b->queue, b->port); else bind_thread(b->queue, b->port);
    return NULL;
}

/* One send_event on `port` with data 0xBEEF; returns the SPU's answer, and how long the delivery took. */
static uint32_t send_event(uint32_t port, double* took_ms)
{
    spu_channel_write(&spu.ch_out_mbox, 0xBEEFu);
    const double t0 = now_ms();
    assert(spu_deliver_user_event(&spu, (port << 24) | 0x000001u) == 1);
    *took_ms = now_ms() - t0;
    return spu_channel_read(&spu.ch_in_mbox);
}

int main(void)
{
    vm_base = calloc(1, 1u << 20); assert(vm_base);
    ppu_vm_size = 1u << 20;
    grp = spu_alloc_group(); thr = spu_alloc_thread();
    assert(grp && thr);
    grp->thread_indices[0] = (uint32_t)(thr - s_spu_threads); grp->num_threads = 1;
    memset(&spu, 0, sizeof spu);
    spu.spu_group_id = grp->id; spu.spu_id = thr->tid;
    double ms;
    uint32_t r;

    reset(); bind_thread(0x77, 0x2A);
    r = send_event(0x2A, &ms);
    CHECK(r == CELL_OK && pushes == 1 && pushed_queue == 0x77 && pushed_data == 0xBEEF,
          "a port bound with sys_spu_thread_connect_event: answer 0x%08X, %d pushes, queue 0x%X", r, pushes, pushed_queue);

    reset(); bind_group(0x88, 0x05);
    r = send_event(0x05, &ms);
    CHECK(r == CELL_OK && pushes == 1 && pushed_queue == 0x88,
          "a port bound for the group: answer 0x%08X, %d pushes, queue 0x%X", r, pushes, pushed_queue);

    for (int via_group = 0; via_group < 2; via_group++) {
        reset();
        late_bind b = { 40, via_group, 0x99, 0x2A };
        pthread_t th; pthread_create(&th, NULL, late_binder, &b);
        r = send_event(0x2A, &ms);
        pthread_join(th, NULL);
        CHECK(r == CELL_OK && pushes == 1 && pushed_queue == 0x99,
              "a port bound %s 40 ms after the event: answer 0x%08X, %d pushes, queue 0x%X",
              via_group ? "for the group" : "for the thread", r, pushes, pushed_queue);
        CHECK(ms >= 25.0 && ms < 150.0, "the event waited %.0f ms for a binding 40 ms away", ms);
    }

    reset();
    r = send_event(0x11, &ms);
    CHECK(r == CELL_ENOTCONN && pushes == 0, "a port nobody binds: answer 0x%08X, %d pushes", r, pushes);
    CHECK(ms >= 150.0 && ms < 1000.0, "the wait for a port nobody binds took %.0f ms (bounded, about 200)", ms);

    reset();
    spu.spu_id = 0x7FFFFF;                       /* no such thread: nothing will ever bind its port */
    r = send_event(0x2A, &ms);
    CHECK(r == CELL_ENOTCONN && ms < 50.0, "an SPU with no thread: answer 0x%08X after %.0f ms (no wait)", r, ms);

    printf("[spu_user_event_port] %s (%d failed)\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    free(vm_base);
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spurs_job_stack.c =====
/*
 * A SPURS job's first stack frame must not overlap its cache buffer
 * (runtime/spu/spurs_job.c).
 *
 * spu_run_spurs_job lays the job's memory out as binary, I/O, output,
 * scratch + stack, then the cache-hinted read-only inputs. The stack top is
 * therefore the first byte of cacheBuffer[0]. Under the SPU ABI a function
 * saves its link register in its CALLER's frame, at 16($sp), so the job's
 * entry runs "stqd $lr, 16($sp)" first thing. With $sp at stack_top - 16 that
 * quadword is the first 16 bytes of the cache buffer.
 *
 * Twisted Metal's Edge geometry jobs keep their viewport (x, y, width,
 * height) there. After the save it read x = 0x3FF00 (the return address the
 * runner puts in $lr) and width = height = 0, so the screen-space scale was
 * zero, every triangle of a skinned mesh had zero area, and the job culled
 * them all: the character in the main menu was never drawn.
 *
 * The job here is a C entry function that does what a lifted job's prologue
 * does, then checks that its cache buffer still holds what the cache DMA list
 * pointed at, and that it can push one more frame without leaving its stack.
 *
 * Build:
 *   clang -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime/spu -I runtime/platform \
 *         -o /tmp/test_spurs_job_stack \
 *         runtime/spu/tests/test_spurs_job_stack.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_drain.c runtime/spu/spu_lockstep.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_coherency.c runtime/spu/spu_workload.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spurs_policy.c runtime/spu/spurs_job.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spu_tsp_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_vm_pagemap.c \
 *         runtime/spu/spurs_policy_blob_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_interp.c \
 *         runtime/platform/win32_compat.c -lpthread -lm
 *
 * Exit code: 0 if all passed, 1 if any failed. Final line prints a summary.
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Guest memory: the runner copies the binary, descriptor and cache inputs
 * out of it. */
static uint8_t g_guest_mem[1u << 20];
uint8_t* vm_base = g_guest_mem;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;

/* spu_run_with_halt and the channel layer the runner needs. */
#include "../spu_channels.c"
#include "spu_workload.h"   /* spu_run_spurs_job */

static int g_pass, g_fail;
static const char* g_current = "(none)";

#define TEST(name) g_current = (name)

#define CHECK(cond) do {                                          \
    if (cond) { g_pass++; }                                       \
    else {                                                        \
        g_fail++;                                                 \
        fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s\n  at %s:%d: %s\n",             \
                g_current, __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond);            \
    }                                                             \
} while (0)

#define JOB_EA     0x00010000u   /* CellSpursJob256 */
#define BIN_EA     0x00020000u   /* job binary (never executed here) */
#define CACHE_EA   0x00030000u   /* cache-hinted input */
#define BIN_SIZE   0x400u
#define CACHE_SIZE 0x80u

static void put32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    g_guest_mem[ea] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); g_guest_mem[ea + 1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16);
    g_guest_mem[ea + 2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); g_guest_mem[ea + 3] = (uint8_t)v;
}
static void put16(uint32_t ea, uint16_t v)
{
    g_guest_mem[ea] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); g_guest_mem[ea + 1] = (uint8_t)v;
}
static uint32_t ls_get32(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa)
{
    const uint8_t* p = ctx->ls + (lsa & SPU_LS_MASK);
    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
}

/* A job with no I/O, the default stack and one 128-byte cache input. */
static void build_job(uint16_t stack_qw, uint16_t scratch_qw)
{
    memset(g_guest_mem, 0, sizeof g_guest_mem);
    put32(JOB_EA + 0x00, 0);                    /* eaBinary, high word */
    put32(JOB_EA + 0x04, BIN_EA);
    put16(JOB_EA + 0x08, BIN_SIZE >> 4);        /* sizeBinary, quadwords */
    put16(JOB_EA + 0x0A, 0);                    /* no input DMA list */
    put16(JOB_EA + 0x1C, stack_qw);             /* sizeStack, quadwords */
    put16(JOB_EA + 0x1E, scratch_qw);           /* sizeScratch, quadwords */
    put32(JOB_EA + 0x24, 8);                    /* one cache DMA entry */
    put32(JOB_EA + 0x30, CACHE_SIZE);           /* entry: size ... */
    put32(JOB_EA + 0x34, CACHE_EA);             /* ... and address */
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < CACHE_SIZE; i += 4)
        put32(CACHE_EA + i, 0xC0DE0000u | i);
}

/* What the entry saw. */
static int      g_ran, g_cache_intact, g_frames_in_stack;
static uint32_t g_cache_ls, g_sp;

/* The prologue every SPU function starts with: save $lr in the caller's
 * frame, then push a frame of its own and store the back chain. */
static void job_entry(spu_context* ctx)
{
    const uint32_t sp = ctx->gpr[1]._u32[0];
    g_ran = 1;
    g_sp = sp;
    memcpy(ctx->ls + ((sp + 16u) & SPU_LS_MASK), &ctx->gpr[0], 16);   /* stqd $lr,16($sp) */
    const uint32_t nsp = sp - 0x40u;                                   /* stqu $sp,-64($sp) */
    memcpy(ctx->ls + (nsp & SPU_LS_MASK), &ctx->gpr[1], 16);

    /* r3 = CellSpursJobContext2*; cacheBuffer[0] is at +4. */
    g_cache_ls = ls_get32(ctx, ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0] + 4u);
    g_cache_intact = g_cache_ls != 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; g_cache_intact && i < CACHE_SIZE; i += 4)
        if (ls_get32(ctx, g_cache_ls + i) != (0xC0DE0000u | i)) g_cache_intact = 0;
    /* Both frames, and the caller's save area above the first, lie below the
     * cache buffer. */
    g_frames_in_stack = sp + 32u <= g_cache_ls && nsp < sp;
}

static void run_case(const char* name, uint16_t stack_qw, uint16_t scratch_qw)
{
    TEST(name);
    build_job(stack_qw, scratch_qw);
    g_ran = g_cache_intact = g_frames_in_stack = 0;
    spu_run_spurs_job(job_entry, 7, JOB_EA, 256);
    CHECK(g_ran);
    CHECK(g_cache_intact);
    CHECK(g_frames_in_stack);
    if (!g_cache_intact || !g_frames_in_stack)
        fprintf(stderr, "  $sp=0x%05X cacheBuffer[0]=0x%05X\n", g_sp, g_cache_ls);
}

int main(void)
{
    run_case("default stack (sizeStack 0)", 0, 0);
    run_case("explicit stack, no scratch", 0x100, 0);
    run_case("stack and scratch", 0x80, 0x40);

    printf("spurs job stack: %d passed, %d failed\n", g_pass, g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}

===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spurs_signalled_atomic.c =====
/*
 * SPURS taskset `signalled` bitset: the host's read-modify-write of a task's
 * bit against an SPU commit to the same line (runtime/spu/spu_workload.c).
 *
 * A task's signal is one bit in the taskset's signalled bitset (+0x40). The
 * host sets it in spu_taskset_signal_task and clears it when the task consumes
 * it in spu_taskset_wait_signal. SPU tasks set bits in the same word with
 * GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under the lock-line lock: a task signalling another, or the
 * last task to reach a cellSpursBarrier releasing the others. If the host reads
 * the word outside that lock and writes it back inside it, an SPU commit landing
 * between the two is overwritten with the stale word and that task never wakes.
 * Twisted Metal's post-FX barrier lost a wake exactly so and stopped for good.
 *
 * The interleaving is built with the lock rather than raced for, as in
 * test_spu_lockline_peer.c. The line is reserved by a peer SPU, so a host store
 * to it is a coherent store that takes the lock-line lock. The main thread takes
 * the lock, a second thread starts the host operation and is held at the lock,
 * the SPU commit is applied under the lock, and only then is the host operation
 * let through. Afterwards both bits must be right: the host's own change and
 * the SPU's commit.
 *
 * spu_channels.c is compiled in, as in the other SPU fixtures, for the symbols
 * spu_workload.c needs.
 *
 * Build:
 *   cc -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime/spu -I runtime/platform \
 *      -o /tmp/test_spurs_signalled_atomic \
 *      runtime/spu/tests/test_spurs_signalled_atomic.c \
 *      runtime/spu/spu_drain.c runtime/spu/spu_lockstep.c \
 *      runtime/spu/spu_coherency.c runtime/spu/spu_workload.c \
 *      runtime/spu/spurs_policy.c runtime/spu/spurs_job.c \
 *      runtime/spu/spu_tsp_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_vm_pagemap.c \
 *      runtime/spu/spurs_policy_blob_weak.c runtime/spu/spu_interp.c \
 *      runtime/platform/win32_compat.c -lpthread -lm
 *
 * Exit code: 0 if all passed, 1 if any failed. Final line prints a summary.
 */

#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

static uint8_t g_guest_mem[1u << 20];
uint8_t* vm_base = g_guest_mem;
uint32_t ppu_vm_size = 0;

#include "../spu_channels.c"

/* The runtime beyond the SPU layer, stubbed as in test_spu_mfc_slots.c. None
 * of it is on the path this test drives. */
void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea)                 { (void)ea; }
void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w)
{
    (void)a; (void)v; (void)w;
}

uint32_t g_ww_lo = 0xFFFFFFFFu, g_ww_hi = 0;

void (*g_spurs_kernel_hook)(uint32_t) = 0;
uint32_t g_ydkj_spurs_ctx_ea = 0;

{
    (void)c; (void)a; (void)b; (void)d;
}
uint32_t g_spu_image_src_ea, g_spu_image_ls_start, g_spu_image_span;
void spu_thread_publish_ctx(uint32_t tid, void* ctx) { (void)tid; (void)ctx; }

int  spu_taskset_wait_signal(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);
void spu_taskset_signal_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId);

static int g_pass, g_fail;
static const char* g_current = "(none)";

#define TEST(name) g_current = (name)

#define CHECK_EQ_U32(actual, expected) do {                       \
    uint32_t _a = (uint32_t)(actual), _e = (uint32_t)(expected);  \
    if (_a == _e) { g_pass++; }                                   \
    else {                                                        \
        g_fail++;                                                 \
        fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s\n  at %s:%d: %s\n"              \
                        "  actual   0x%08X\n  expected 0x%08X\n", \
                g_current, __FILE__, __LINE__, #actual, _a, _e);  \
    }                                                             \
} while (0)

#define TASKSET   0x00030000u                 /* 128-byte aligned */
#define SIG_WORD  (TASKSET + 0x40u)           /* signalled bitset, tasks 0..31 */
#define BIT(t)    ((1u << 31) >> (t))

static spu_context g_peer;                    /* holds the reservation */

static uint32_t rd_be32(uint32_t ea)
{
    const uint8_t* p = g_guest_mem + ea;
    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
}

static void wr_be32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    uint8_t* p = g_guest_mem + ea;
    p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16);
    p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8);  p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}

static void sleep_ms(long ms)
{
    struct timespec ts = { ms / 1000, (ms % 1000) * 1000000L };
    nanosleep(&ts, NULL);
}

static void* do_signal_task4(void* arg)  { (void)arg; spu_taskset_signal_task(TASKSET, 4); return NULL; }
static void* do_wait_task3(void* arg)    { (void)arg; spu_taskset_wait_signal(TASKSET, 3); return NULL; }

/* The host operation runs on its own thread while the main thread holds the
 * lock-line lock; the SPU commit (`spu_bit` set in the word) is applied under
 * the lock, then the lock is released and the host operation completes. */
static void interleave(void* (*host_op)(void*), uint32_t spu_bit)
{
    pthread_t t;
    spu_lockline_lock();
    pthread_create(&t, NULL, host_op, NULL);
    sleep_ms(100);                            /* the host op reaches the lock */
    wr_be32(SIG_WORD, rd_be32(SIG_WORD) | spu_bit);   /* the SPU's PUTLLC */
    spu_lockline_unlock();
    pthread_join(t, NULL);
}

int main(void)
{
    /* A peer SPU has the bitset line reserved, as a task in GETLLAR does. */
    spu_lockline_lock();
    spu_coh_reserve(&g_peer, SIG_WORD);
    spu_lockline_unlock();

    TEST("host signal vs SPU commit: neither bit is lost");
    wr_be32(SIG_WORD, 0);
    interleave(do_signal_task4, BIT(3));
    CHECK_EQ_U32(rd_be32(SIG_WORD), BIT(3) | BIT(4));

    TEST("host consume vs SPU commit: the other task's bit survives");
    wr_be32(SIG_WORD, BIT(3));                /* task 3 has a pending signal */
    interleave(do_wait_task3, BIT(4));
    CHECK_EQ_U32(rd_be32(SIG_WORD), BIT(4));

    printf("%d passed, %d failed\n", g_pass, g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_spurs_taskset_bits_atomic.c =====
/*
 * SPURS taskset ready/enabled bitsets: the host's updates against a task exit
 * (or an SPU commit) changing the same line (libs/spurs/spurs_taskset.c).
 *
 * cellSpursCreateTask found a free task id by reading the enabled bitset (+0x30)
 * and later set the enabled and ready bits (+0x10) with spurs_bitset_set: a
 * vm_read32 outside the lock-line lock and a vm_write32 inside it. The host's
 * task exit clears the exiting task's enabled bit, and SPU tasks update the same
 * line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC. A clear landing between the read and the write was
 * undone: the exited task's enabled bit came back with no task behind it, and
 * cellSpursJoinTask2 on that id never returned (Killzone 3: Havok's thread-pool
 * destructor at quit to menu).
 *
 * The interleaving is built with the lock, as in test_spurs_signalled_atomic.c:
 * a peer SPU has the line reserved (so a host store takes the lock-line lock),
 * the main thread holds the lock, a second thread starts the host operation and
 * is held at the lock, the exit's clear is applied under the lock, and only then
 * is the host operation let through.
 *
 * Build:
 *   cc -std=gnu17 -I include -I runtime/spu -I runtime/platform \
 *      -o /tmp/test_spurs_taskset_bits_atomic \

/* libs/spurs/spurs_taskset.c (its header's PM prototypes clash with the stubs above). */
void     spurs_taskset_add_task(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t taskId, uint64_t elf_ea, uint64_t context,
                                const uint32_t arg[4], const uint32_t ls_pattern[4]);
uint32_t spurs_taskset_take_slot(uint32_t taskset_ea, uint32_t max_tasks);

static int g_pass, g_fail;
static const char* g_current = "(none)";

#define TEST(name) g_current = (name)

#define CHECK_EQ_U32(actual, expected) do {                       \
    uint32_t _a = (uint32_t)(actual), _e = (uint32_t)(expected);  \
    if (_a == _e) { g_pass++; }                                   \
    else {                                                        \
        g_fail++;                                                 \
        fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s\n  at %s:%d: %s\n"              \
                        "  actual   0x%08X\n  expected 0x%08X\n", \
                g_current, __FILE__, __LINE__, #actual, _a, _e);  \
    }                                                             \
} while (0)

#define TASKSET     0x00030000u               /* 128-byte aligned */
#define READY_WORD  (TASKSET + 0x10u)         /* ready bitset, tasks 0..31 */
#define EN_WORD     (TASKSET + 0x30u)         /* enabled bitset, tasks 0..31 */
#define BIT(t)      ((1u << 31) >> (t))

static spu_context g_peer;                    /* holds the reservation */

static uint32_t rd_be32(uint32_t ea)
{
    const uint8_t* p = g_guest_mem + ea;
    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
}

static void wr_be32(uint32_t ea, uint32_t v)
{
    uint8_t* p = g_guest_mem + ea;
    p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16);
    p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8);  p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}

static void sleep_ms(long ms)
{
    struct timespec ts = { ms / 1000, (ms % 1000) * 1000000L };
    nanosleep(&ts, NULL);
}

static uint32_t g_slot;
static void* do_add_task2(void* arg)
{
    (void)arg;
    spurs_taskset_add_task(TASKSET, 2, 0x00040000u, 0, NULL, NULL);
    return NULL;
}
static void* do_take_slot(void* arg)  { (void)arg; g_slot = spurs_taskset_take_slot(TASKSET, 128); return NULL; }

/* The host operation runs on its own thread while the main thread holds the
 * lock-line lock; task 0's exit (its enabled bit cleared) is applied under the
 * lock, then the lock is released and the host operation completes. */
static void interleave(void* (*host_op)(void*))
{
    pthread_t t;
    spu_lockline_lock();
    pthread_create(&t, NULL, host_op, NULL);
    sleep_ms(100);                            /* the host op reaches the lock */
    wr_be32(EN_WORD, rd_be32(EN_WORD) & ~BIT(0));     /* task 0 exits */
    spu_lockline_unlock();
    pthread_join(t, NULL);
}

static void reserve_line(void)
{
    /* A peer SPU has the bitset line reserved, as a task in GETLLAR does. A
     * host write drops every reservation on the line, so take it again. */
    spu_lockline_lock();
    spu_coh_reserve(&g_peer, EN_WORD);
    spu_lockline_unlock();
}

int main(void)
{
    TEST("add_task vs task exit: the exited task's enabled bit stays clear");
    wr_be32(EN_WORD, BIT(0) | BIT(1));
    wr_be32(READY_WORD, 0);
    reserve_line();
    interleave(do_add_task2);
    CHECK_EQ_U32(rd_be32(EN_WORD), BIT(1) | BIT(2));
    CHECK_EQ_U32(rd_be32(READY_WORD), BIT(2));

    TEST("take_slot vs task exit: the freed id is taken, the others kept");
    wr_be32(EN_WORD, BIT(0) | BIT(1));
    reserve_line();
    interleave(do_take_slot);
    CHECK_EQ_U32(g_slot, 0);
    CHECK_EQ_U32(rd_be32(EN_WORD), BIT(0) | BIT(1));

    TEST("take_slot: the lowest clear bit, then none when all are taken");
    memset(g_guest_mem + EN_WORD, 0xFF, 16);
    g_guest_mem[EN_WORD + 5] = 0xEF;          /* task 43 free */
    CHECK_EQ_U32(spurs_taskset_take_slot(TASKSET, 128), 43);
    CHECK_EQ_U32(spurs_taskset_take_slot(TASKSET, 128), 128);

    printf("%d passed, %d failed\n", g_pass, g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_sum_main.c =====
/*
 * Integration test #1: sum loop.
 *
 * Drives test_sum.elf's lifted output. The SPU program reads N values from
 * the inbound mailbox, sums them, writes the result to the outbound mailbox.
 *
 * We provide our own spu_rdch / spu_wrch (overriding spu_channels.c) so we
 * can serve a queue of inbound values without modelling real PPU/SPU
 * scheduling. The lifter only knows about the externs declared in
 * spu_recomp.h, so linking these definitions instead of spu_channels.c is
 * how we plug in the test harness.
 */

#include "spu_recomp.h"
#include "spu_helpers.h"   /* for spu_zero() */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Required by spu_dma.h (referenced via spu_helpers.h chain). Unused here. */
uint8_t* vm_base = 0;

/* ---- harness state ---- */
static const uint32_t kInputs[] = { 10, 20, 30, 40 };
static const int      kNumInputs = (int)(sizeof(kInputs) / sizeof(kInputs[0]));
static int            g_in_idx = 0;
static uint32_t       g_out = 0;
static int            g_wrote = 0;

/* ---- channel overrides ---- */
u128 spu_rdch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel) {
    (void)ctx;
    uint32_t v = 0;
    if (channel == SPU_RdInMbox) {
        if (g_in_idx < kNumInputs) v = kInputs[g_in_idx++];
        else { fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: rdch underflow\n"); return spu_zero(); }
    }
    u128 r = spu_zero(); r._u32[0] = v; return r;
}
uint32_t spu_rchcnt(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel) {
    (void)ctx; (void)channel; return 1;
}
void spu_wrch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel, u128 value) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (channel == SPU_WrOutMbox) { g_out = value._u32[0]; g_wrote = 1; }
}

/* The lifter emits these as externs; this test has no indirect branches
 * so the bodies are unreachable, but the symbols must exist. */
void spu_indirect_branch(spu_context* ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: unexpected spu_indirect_branch\n");
}
void spu_register_function(uint32_t addr, void (*fn)(spu_context*)) {
    (void)addr; (void)fn;   /* not used in this test */
}

/* diagnostics externs referenced from spu_dma.h in the full runtime */
int g_cri_video_dma = 0;
/* stop/halt hooks required by current lifter output */
void spu_stop(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }
void spu_halt(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }

int main(void) {
    spu_context ctx;
    spu_context_init(&ctx, 0);
    spu_func_00000000(&ctx);

    uint32_t expected = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kNumInputs; i++) expected += kInputs[i];

    int ok = 1;
    if (!g_wrote)        { printf("FAIL: no wrch to outbound mailbox\n"); ok = 0; }
    if (g_in_idx != kNumInputs)
        { printf("FAIL: consumed %d/%d inbound values\n", g_in_idx, kNumInputs); ok = 0; }
    if (g_out != expected)
        { printf("FAIL: outbound = %u (expected %u)\n", g_out, expected); ok = 0; }

    if (ok) {
        printf("OK: consumed %d values, sum = %u (matches %u)\n",
               g_in_idx, g_out, expected);
    }
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}


===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_taskset_main.c =====
/* SPU bring-up rung 4 — cellSpurs taskset / job-queue throughput (host side).
 *
 * Brings rungs 1-3 together under the SPURS work-engine model: a cellSpurs-style
 * taskset drains a real cellSync LFQueue of N work items and invokes a single
 * lifted SPU task body once per item; each invocation DMAs the item, produces a
 * result, and raises a completion event delivered to the taskset's event queue.
 *
 * This is the bridge the lv2 SPU-thread-group layer (lv2_register.c: create ->
 * start -> join -> sys_event_queue_push_by_id) and a real cellSpurs taskset would
 * drive: lifted SPU execution as the task body, fed by an LFQueue, completing via
 * events. Here the taskset runner is a minimal host stand-in for cellSpurs; the
 * integration rung promotes it into cellSpurs.c + the lv2 thread-group path.
 */
#include "spu_recomp.h"
#include "spu_helpers.h"
#include "spu_dma.h"
#include "cellSync.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { uint64_t source, data1; } ev_t;
typedef struct { ev_t buf[16]; int head, tail, count, active; } ev_queue;
static int evq_push(ev_queue* q, uint64_t s, uint64_t d1) {
    if (!q->active || q->count == 16) return -1;
    q->buf[q->tail].source = s; q->buf[q->tail].data1 = d1;
    q->tail = (q->tail + 1) % 16; q->count++; return 0;
}
static int evq_receive(ev_queue* q, ev_t* o) {
    if (!q->active || q->count == 0) return -1;
    *o = q->buf[q->head]; q->head = (q->head + 1) % 16; q->count--; return 0;
}

static uint8_t  g_mem[2048];
uint8_t*        vm_base = g_mem;
static mfc_engine g_mfc;
static ev_queue g_taskset_evq;     /* taskset completion event queue */

#define WORK_EA   0x180            /* SPU task input slot  */
#define RESULT_EA 0x1C0            /* SPU task output slot */
#define QUEUE_BUF 0x100            /* LFQueue data buffer  */
#define EV_SOURCE_SPU_GROUP 0x7ULL

u128 spu_rdch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) { (void)ctx; (void)ch; return spu_zero(); }
uint32_t spu_rchcnt(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) { (void)ctx; (void)ch; return 1; }
void spu_wrch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel, u128 value) {
    if (channel == SPU_WrOutIntrMbox) { evq_push(&g_taskset_evq, EV_SOURCE_SPU_GROUP, value._u32[0]); return; }
    mfc_channel_write(&g_mfc, ctx, channel, value._u32[0]);
}
void spu_indirect_branch(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: unexpected indirect branch\n"); }
void spu_register_function(uint32_t addr, void (*fn)(spu_context*)) { (void)addr; (void)fn; }

static uint32_t be32(const uint8_t* p) {
    return ((uint32_t)p[0]<<24)|((uint32_t)p[1]<<16)|((uint32_t)p[2]<<8)|(uint32_t)p[3];
}
static void wbe32(uint8_t* p, uint32_t v) { p[0]=v>>24; p[1]=v>>16; p[2]=v>>8; p[3]=v; }

/* ---- minimal cellSpurs-style taskset: runs the lifted SPU task body over a
 *      cellSync LFQueue of work items, collecting per-item completion events. ---- */
typedef struct { CellSyncLFQueue* work_q; ev_queue* evq; int done; } spurs_taskset;

static void taskset_run(spurs_taskset* ts) {
    uint8_t item[16];
    /* non-blocking drain: cellSyncLFQueuePop BLOCKS when empty (it's the
     * blocking variant); TryPop returns an error so the taskset stops when the
     * workload queue is exhausted. */
    while (cellSyncLFQueueTryPop(ts->work_q, item) == CELL_OK) {
        memcpy(&g_mem[WORK_EA], item, 16);                 /* deliver workload to the SPU task input */
        spu_context ctx; spu_context_init(&ctx, 0);
        mfc_engine_init(&g_mfc);
        spu_func_00000000(&ctx);                           /* run the lifted SPU task body           */
        ts->done++;
    }
}

/* diagnostics externs referenced from spu_dma.h in the full runtime */
int g_cri_video_dma = 0;
/* stop/halt hooks required by current lifter output */
void spu_stop(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }
void spu_halt(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }

int main(void) {
    memset(g_mem, 0, sizeof(g_mem));
    memset(&g_taskset_evq, 0, sizeof(g_taskset_evq)); g_taskset_evq.active = 1;

    /* PPU: a real cellSync LFQueue feeding the taskset, buffer in shared memory. */
    CellSyncLFQueue q;
    cellSyncLFQueueInitialize(&q, &g_mem[QUEUE_BUF], 16, 8, 0, 0);

    /* PPU enqueues 3 workloads. */
    const uint32_t kWork[3] = { 0x1111AAAA, 0x2222BBBB, 0x3333CCCC };
    int pushed = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        uint8_t item[16] = {0}; wbe32(item, kWork[i]);
        if (cellSyncLFQueuePush(&q, item) == CELL_OK) pushed++;
    }

    /* Run the taskset: it drains the queue, invoking the lifted SPU task per item. */
    spurs_taskset ts = { &q, &g_taskset_evq, 0 };
    taskset_run(&ts);

    /* Verify: 3 workloads processed, 3 completion events, each result == its input. */
    int events = 0; ev_t e;
    while (evq_receive(&g_taskset_evq, &e) == 0) { if (e.data1 == 0x7A5C) events++; }
    uint32_t last_result = be32(&g_mem[RESULT_EA]);

    int all_ok = (pushed == 3) && (ts.done == 3) && (events == 3)
                 && (last_result == kWork[2]);
    printf("  [TASKSET] enqueued=%d  processed=%d  completion events=%d\n", pushed, ts.done, events);
    printf("  [RESULT ] last task result = 0x%08X (expected 0x%08X)  %s\n",
           last_result, kWork[2], (last_result == kWork[2]) ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    if (all_ok)
        printf("  PASS: cellSpurs-style taskset ran a lifted SPU job over an LFQueue of workloads.\n");
    return all_ok ? 0 : 1;
}

static const unsigned TORTURE_EXPECTED[] = { 0x0AA10001u, 0x0AA10002u, 0x0AA10003u, 0x0AA10004u, 0x0AA10005u, 0x0AA10006u, 0x0AA10007u, 0x0AA10008u };

===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_torture_main.c =====
/* SPU lifter torture-KAT harness. See gen_test_torture.py for the KAT list --
 * each targets a bug class the LBP Bink bring-up hit in the wild (preferred-
 * halfword branches, ila-continuations, computed-branch stack growth).
 *
 * Run with clang (GCC=clang ./run_tests.sh): K6's 100k-iteration bi-loop needs
 * guaranteed-flat dispatch (musttail); under gcc the fallback relies on
 * sibling-call optimization and may fail for harness reasons, not lifter bugs.
 */
#include "spu_recomp.h"
#include "spu_helpers.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "test_torture_expected.h"

uint8_t* vm_base = 0;

/* ---- marker collection (SPU_WrOutMbox) ---- */
static uint32_t g_marks[64];
static int g_nmarks = 0;
static int g_stopped = 0;

u128 spu_rdch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) { (void)ctx; (void)ch; return spu_zero(); }
uint32_t spu_rchcnt(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) { (void)ctx; (void)ch; return 1; }
void spu_wrch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel, u128 value) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (channel == SPU_WrOutMbox && g_nmarks < 64)
        g_marks[g_nmarks++] = value._u32[0];
}
void spu_stop(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; g_stopped = 1; }
void spu_halt(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; g_stopped = 1; }

/* ---- minimal real dispatch: registry + (musttail) resolver ---- */
typedef void (*fnp)(spu_context*);
static struct { uint32_t addr; fnp fn; } g_reg[4096];
static int g_nreg = 0;
void spu_register_function(uint32_t addr, fnp fn) {
    if (g_nreg < 4096) { g_reg[g_nreg].addr = addr; g_reg[g_nreg].fn = fn; g_nreg++; }
}
void spu_indirect_branch(spu_context* ctx) {
    uint32_t pc = ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nreg; i++) {
        if (g_reg[i].addr == pc) {
#if defined(__clang__)
            __attribute__((musttail)) return g_reg[i].fn(ctx);
#else
            g_reg[i].fn(ctx);
            return;
#endif
        }
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: unresolved indirect branch to 0x%05X "
            "(missing lifted function -- discovery bug?)\n", pc);
    exit(3);
}

void spu_recomp_register(void);
void spu_func_00000000(spu_context* ctx);

/* diagnostics externs referenced from spu_dma.h in the full runtime */
int g_cri_video_dma = 0;

int main(void) {
    spu_context* ctx = (spu_context*)calloc(1, sizeof(spu_context));
    if (!ctx) { printf("FAIL: oom\n"); return 2; }
    spu_context_init(ctx, 0);
    spu_recomp_register();

    spu_func_00000000(ctx);

    int bad = 0;
    if (!g_stopped) { printf("FAIL: guest never reached stop\n"); bad = 1; }
    if (g_nmarks != TORTURE_EXPECTED_N) {
        printf("FAIL: %d markers, expected %d\n", g_nmarks, TORTURE_EXPECTED_N);
        bad = 1;
    }
    int n = g_nmarks < TORTURE_EXPECTED_N ? g_nmarks : TORTURE_EXPECTED_N;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (g_marks[i] != TORTURE_EXPECTED[i]) {
            printf("FAIL: KAT %d -> 0x%08X (expected 0x%08X)\n",
                   i + 1, g_marks[i], TORTURE_EXPECTED[i]);
            bad = 1;
        }
    }
    if (bad) return 1;
    printf("OK: %d/%d torture KATs (halfword branches, gate reduction, "
           "ila-continuation, 100k bi-loop)", g_nmarks, TORTURE_EXPECTED_N);
    free(ctx);
    return 0;
}

===== FILE: \runtime\spu\tests\test_workload_main.c =====
/* SPU workload-dispatch test — host (PPU-side) harness.
 *
 * Validates runtime/spu/spu_workload.c, the cellSpurs dispatch brick:
 *   - cross-language fingerprint agreement (C hash == the Python extractor's),
 *   - the SPU ELF -> local-store LOADER (a marker baked into the image is read
 *     back by the SPU job, proving the LS was loaded and not just zeroed),
 *   - the SPURS task ABI (the job's arg EA propagates into r3),
 *   - a registry MISS for an unregistered image returns 0 (caller can fall back).
 *
 * The SPU job (gen_test_workload.py) forwards both r3 and the LS marker to main
 * memory via DMA PUT; we register its lifted entry under the image fingerprint,
 * dispatch the raw image, and check the results.
 */
#include "spu_recomp.h"
#include "spu_helpers.h"
#include "spu_dma.h"
#include "spu_workload.h"
#include "test_workload_image.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

/* SPU "main memory" view (DMA dereferences vm_base + ea). */
static uint8_t g_mem[1024];
uint8_t* vm_base = g_mem;
static mfc_engine g_mfc;

u128 spu_rdch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) {
    (void)ctx;
    u128 r = spu_zero();
    if (ch == 24) r._u32[0] = 0xFFFFFFFFu;   /* MFC_RdTagStat: DMA synchronous -> done */
    return r;
}
uint32_t spu_rchcnt(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ch) { (void)ctx; (void)ch; return 1; }
void spu_wrch(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t channel, u128 value) {
    mfc_channel_write(&g_mfc, ctx, channel, value._u32[0]);
}
void spu_indirect_branch(spu_context* ctx) {
    (void)ctx; fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: unexpected indirect branch\n");
}
void spu_register_function(uint32_t addr, void (*fn)(spu_context*)) { (void)addr; (void)fn; }

static uint32_t be32(const uint8_t* p) {
    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) |
           ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8)  |  (uint32_t)p[3];
}

/* diagnostics externs referenced from spu_dma.h in the full runtime */
int g_cri_video_dma = 0;
/* stop/halt hooks required by current lifter output */
void spu_stop(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }
void spu_halt(spu_context* ctx) { (void)ctx; }

int main(void) {
    mfc_engine_init(&g_mfc);
    int ok = 1;

    /* 1) Fingerprint: C hash must match the Python extractor's value. */
    uint64_t fp = spu_workload_fingerprint(kWorkloadElf, kWorkloadElfSize);
    int fp_ok = (fp == kWorkloadFP);
    printf("  [FINGERPRINT] C=0x%016llX  py=0x%016llX  %s\n",
           (unsigned long long)fp, (unsigned long long)kWorkloadFP,
           fp_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= fp_ok;

    /* 2) MISS before registration: dispatch must report no handler. */
    memset(g_mem, 0, sizeof(g_mem));
    int miss = spu_workload_dispatch(kWorkloadElf, kWorkloadElfSize, 0);
    int miss_ok = (miss == 0);
    printf("  [MISS       ] unregistered image -> dispatch=%d            %s\n",
           miss, miss_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= miss_ok;

    /* 3) Register the lifted entry under the image fingerprint, then dispatch
     *    the raw image with a task arg. The job forwards r3 + the LS marker. */
    spu_workload_register(fp, spu_func_00000000, "test_workload");
    printf("  [REGISTER   ] count=%u\n", spu_workload_count());

    const uint32_t kArg = 0x0000ABCDu;
    memset(g_mem, 0, sizeof(g_mem));
    int hit = spu_workload_dispatch(kWorkloadElf, kWorkloadElfSize, kArg);

    uint32_t got_arg    = be32(&g_mem[0]);    /* LS[0x100] word0 = r3 (task arg)  */
    uint32_t got_marker = be32(&g_mem[16]);   /* LS[0x110] word0 = baked-in marker */
    int hit_ok    = (hit == 1);
    int arg_ok    = (got_arg == kArg);
    int marker_ok = (got_marker == kWorkloadMarker);

    printf("  [DISPATCH   ] hit=%d                                       %s\n",
           hit, hit_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    printf("  [TASK ARG   ] r3 -> main_mem = 0x%08X (expected 0x%08X)  %s\n",
           got_arg, kArg, arg_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    printf("  [LS LOADED  ] marker         = 0x%08X (expected 0x%08X)  %s\n",
           got_marker, kWorkloadMarker, marker_ok ? "OK" : "FAIL");
    ok &= hit_ok & arg_ok & marker_ok;

    if (ok)
        printf("  PASS: fingerprint + ELF->LS load + task-arg ABI + dispatch all correct.\n");
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}

===== FILE: \runtime\syscalls\lv2_lock_line.c =====
/*
 * ps3recomp - sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address (14)
 *
 * Classification for syscall 14. Split out of lv2_register.c so the
 * contract can be unit-tested without linking the whole syscall layer.
 *
 * Contract from RPCS3's sys_process.cpp
 * (process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address):
 *  - the flags must be non-zero and contain only the two SPU bits
 *    (SPU_THR 0x2, RAW_SPU 0x1) or EINVAL -- the mask is a set of access
 *    rights, so both bits together is a valid request;
 *  - the main-memory (0x0/0x1), user-64K/sys_memory (0x2), RSX-local (0xC)
 *    and RawSPU-MMIO (0xE) segments are reservation-capable;
 *  - this runtime's configured primary/spill sys_memory arenas keep those
 *    rights when relocated outside the usual user-memory segment;
 *  - private SPU MMIO (0xF) refuses RawSPU access with EPERM, and allows
 *    SPU threads;
 *  - the PPU stack segment (0xD) refuses with EPERM;
 *  - everything else: a sys_vm mapping answers EPERM, an uncovered hole in
 *    a sys_vm-mapped 256 MB region answers EINVAL (the mapping reserves
 *    the whole region), and anything unmapped answers EINVAL.
 */

#include "lv2_lock_line.h"

#include "sys_vm.h"                       /* SYS_VM_REGION_*, g_sys_vm_maps */
#include "sys_memory.h"                   /* configured sys_memory arenas */

#include "../../include/ps3emu/error_codes.h"

int64_t lv2_spu_lock_line_classify(uint32_t addr, uint64_t flags)
{
    if (!flags || (flags & ~0x3ull)) {        /* SPU_THR 0x2 | RAW_SPU 0x1 */
        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EINVAL;
    }

    switch (addr >> 28) {
    case 0x0:                                 /* main memory */
    case 0x1:                                 /* main memory (the 256 MB
                                                 VM_MAIN window is only the
                                                 bottom of the segment) */
    case 0x2:                                 /* user 64K (sys_memory) */
    case 0xC:                                 /* RSX local memory */
    case 0xE:                                 /* RawSPU MMIO */
        return 0;

    case 0xF:                                 /* private SPU MMIO */
        if (flags & 0x1ull) {
            /* RawSPU may not reserve lock lines on its own MMIO */
            return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EPERM;
        }
        return 0;

    case 0xD:                                 /* PPU stack area */
        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EPERM;

    default:
        /* The flat runtime can relocate sys_memory outside PS3 segment 0x2.
         * Those arenas retain the same SPU access rights as user memory.
         * In particular, P5's debug port uses 0x30200000..0x40000000: treating
         * it as an unmapped segment makes libsre reject a valid SPURS area.
         * As with segment 0x2 above, classify the arena, not individual pages. */
        if ((addr >= SYS_MEM_ALLOC_BASE && addr < SYS_MEM_ALLOC_END) ||
            (addr >= SYS_MEM_ALLOC_SPILL_BASE && addr < SYS_MEM_ALLOC_SPILL_END)) {
            return 0;
        }
        /* sys_vm mappings live in the one 256 MB window sys_vm.h tracks.
         * RPCS3 answers EPERM for an address a mapping covers, EINVAL for
         * a hole in that region (a mapping reserves all of it), and EINVAL
         * for anything else, since no other mapping lives in these
         * segments. */
        if (addr >= SYS_VM_REGION_BASE && addr < SYS_VM_REGION_END) {
            int mapped = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < SYS_VM_MAX; i++) {
                const sys_vm_map_info* m = &g_sys_vm_maps[i];
                if (!m->active) {
                    continue;
                }
                mapped = 1;
                if (addr >= m->addr && addr - m->addr < m->vsize) {
                    return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EPERM;
                }
            }
            if (mapped) {
                return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EINVAL;   /* hole in the region */
            }
        }
        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EINVAL;           /* unmapped */
    }
}

 * ps3recomp - sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address (14)

 * The address/flags contract of syscall 14, split out of lv2_register.c so

#ifndef LV2_LOCK_LINE_H

/* Answer whether SPUs may place lock-line reservations (GETLLAR/PUTLLC) on
 * the guest address `addr` with the access-right `flags` (bit 0 = RawSPU,
 * bit 1 = SPU threads). Returns 0 when reservations are allowed, or the
 * negative-encoded CELL error the syscall must return (CELL_EPERM /
 * CELL_EINVAL, in this runtime's (int64_t)(int32_t) convention). The
 * contract is RPCS3's process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address
 * (Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_process.cpp). */

}
#endif

#endif /* LV2_LOCK_LINE_H */

/*
 * ps3recomp - LV2 syscall registration
 *
 * Calls all sys_X_init functions to populate the syscall dispatch table
 * with real HLE handlers.
 *
 * Registration order matters for conflicting syscall numbers:
 * timers are registered before events, so event handlers take precedence
 * for the colliding numbers (141, 142, 145). Timer sleep/time functions
 * remain available as direct C calls for the runtime to use.
 */

#include <stdlib.h>   /* calloc, free */
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include "ps3emu/nid.h"   /* ps3_compute_nid (static inline) */

extern void sys_raw_spu_init(lv2_syscall_table* tbl);   /* runtime/spu/spu_raw.c */
extern void spu_raw_note_image(uint32_t src_ea, uint32_t entry);

/* Guest scratch for an SPU ELF staged by sys_spu_image_open, which reads the
 * file in and then re-enters the import path with it. Shares the 16 MB region
 * below the TLS block (0x0E000000) with the segment tables built by
 * sys_spu_image_import: those grow up from 0x0D000000, these from the halfway
 * mark, so the two only meet after ~350k segment records. */
#define SPU_IMAGE_STAGE_BASE 0x0D800000u
#define SPU_IMAGE_STAGE_END  0x0E000000u

#include "../spu/spu_context.h"       /* the architectural context that runs it */

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * TTY syscalls (used by PS3 CRT for debug output)
 *
 * sys_tty_read  (402) — read from TTY (stdin)
 * sys_tty_write (403) — write to TTY (stdout/stderr)
 *
 * These are among the most commonly called syscalls in CRT startup.
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

extern uint8_t* vm_base;

static int64_t sys_tty_write(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    /* s32 sys_tty_write(s32 ch, const void* buf, u32 len, u32* pwritelen) */
    uint32_t ch     = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
    uint32_t buf_ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4];
    uint32_t len    = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5];
    uint32_t pwr_ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[6];

    if (buf_ea && len > 0 && vm_base) {
        /* Keep guest diagnostics out of the host warning/error stream. */
        ps3_console_write_tty(ch, vm_base + buf_ea, len);
        /* TTY_BT=<substring>: dump the guest LR back-chain whenever the title
         * prints a line containing it. The two hooks below do exactly this for
         * one hardcoded string each, which only ever helped the title they were
         * written for. A title's own error message is the cheapest breakpoint
         * there is -- it fires exactly when the thing went wrong, in the thread
         * it went wrong on -- so make it a knob rather than an edit.
         *
         * Virtua Fighter 5: TTY_BT="Command Buffer Overflow" names the AMGL
         * function whose free-space check is failing. */
        { static const char* pat = (const char*)1;
          if (pat == (const char*)1) pat = getenv("TTY_BT");
          if (pat && *pat && len < 4096) {
              char tmp[512]; uint32_t n = len < 511 ? len : 511;
              memcpy(tmp, vm_base + buf_ea, n); tmp[n] = 0;
              if (strstr(tmp, pat)) {
                  static int _n = 0;
                  if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 4)) {
                      uint32_t sp = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[1];
                      fprintf(stderr, "[TTY_BT] \"%.70s\" tid=%llu cia=0x%08X lr=0x%08X chain:",
                              tmp, (unsigned long long)ctx->thread_id,
                              (uint32_t)ctx->cia, (uint32_t)ctx->lr);
                      for (int i = 0; i < 24 && sp && sp < 0x10000000u; i++) {
                          uint32_t nsp; memcpy(&nsp, vm_base + sp, 4);
                          nsp = ((nsp>>24)&0xFF)|((nsp>>8)&0xFF00)|((nsp<<8)&0xFF0000)|((nsp<<24)&0xFF000000);
                          if (nsp <= sp || nsp >= 0x10000000u) break;
                          uint32_t lr; memcpy(&lr, vm_base + nsp + 0x10, 4);
                          lr = ((lr>>24)&0xFF)|((lr>>8)&0xFF00)|((lr<<8)&0xFF0000)|((lr<<24)&0xFF000000);
                          fprintf(stderr, " %08X", lr); sp = nsp;
                      }
                      fprintf(stderr, "\n"); fflush(stderr);
                  }
              }
          } }

        /* CRI error back-chain (YDKJ_CRIBT=1): dump the guest LR chain when a CRI
         * null-pointer / criFs error is printed, to locate the failing call. */
        if (getenv("YDKJ_CRIBT") && len < 4096) {
            char tmp[256]; uint32_t n = len < 255 ? len : 255;
            memcpy(tmp, vm_base + buf_ea, n); tmp[n] = 0;
            if (strstr(tmp, "NULL pointer") || strstr(tmp, "E2004090") || strstr(tmp, "CRICRS")) {
                static int _cb = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_cb, 4)) {
                    uint32_t sp = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[1];
                    fprintf(stderr, "[CRIBT] \"%.60s\" cia=0x%08X lr=0x%08X chain:", tmp,
                            (uint32_t)ctx->cia, (uint32_t)ctx->lr);
                    for (int i = 0; i < 24 && sp && sp < 0x10000000u; i++) {
                        uint32_t nsp; memcpy(&nsp, vm_base + sp, 4);
                        nsp = ((nsp>>24)&0xFF)|((nsp>>8)&0xFF00)|((nsp<<8)&0xFF0000)|((nsp<<24)&0xFF000000);
                        if (nsp <= sp || nsp >= 0x10000000u) break;
                        uint32_t lr; memcpy(&lr, vm_base + nsp + 0x10, 4);
                        lr = ((lr>>24)&0xFF)|((lr>>8)&0xFF00)|((lr<<8)&0xFF0000)|((lr<<24)&0xFF000000);
                        fprintf(stderr, " %08X", lr); sp = nsp;
                    }
                    fprintf(stderr, "\n"); fflush(stderr);
                }
            }
        }
        /* YDKJ_ASSERTBT: the libspurs _cellSpursIsLaunchedFromTuner assertion (which
         * aborts the SPURS task subsystem) prints through here. Dump the guest LR +
         * back-chain to locate the asserting function so it can be suppressed. */
        if (getenv("YDKJ_ASSERTBT") && len < 4096) {
            char tmp[256]; uint32_t n = len < 255 ? len : 255;
            memcpy(tmp, vm_base + buf_ea, n); tmp[n] = 0;
            if (strstr(tmp, "ASSERT") || strstr(tmp, "Tuner") || strstr(tmp, "usertrace") ||
                strstr(tmp, "libspurs")) {
                static int _ab = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_ab, 4)) {
                    uint32_t sp = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[1];
                    fprintf(stderr, "\n[ASSERTBT] \"%.70s\" cia=0x%08X lr=0x%08X chain:", tmp,
                            (uint32_t)ctx->cia, (uint32_t)ctx->lr);
                    for (int i = 0; i < 28 && sp && sp < 0x10000000u; i++) {
                        uint32_t nsp; memcpy(&nsp, vm_base + sp, 4);
                        nsp = ((nsp>>24)&0xFF)|((nsp>>8)&0xFF00)|((nsp<<8)&0xFF0000)|((nsp<<24)&0xFF000000);
                        if (nsp <= sp || nsp >= 0x10000000u) break;
                        uint32_t lr; memcpy(&lr, vm_base + nsp + 0x10, 4);
                        lr = ((lr>>24)&0xFF)|((lr>>8)&0xFF00)|((lr<<8)&0xFF0000)|((lr<<24)&0xFF000000);
                        fprintf(stderr, " %08X", lr); sp = nsp;
                    }
                    fprintf(stderr, "\n"); fflush(stderr);
                }
            }
        }
        /* POOL CORRUPTION TRACE: when the game's debug allocator reports a bad
         * block / wrong pool / zeroed sentinel, dump the host call chain (resolved
         * to guest funcs) to find who passed/corrupted the block. */
        if (len < 4096) {
            char ptmp[256]; uint32_t pn = len < 255 ? len : 255;
            memcpy(ptmp, vm_base + buf_ea, pn); ptmp[pn] = 0;
            if (strstr(ptmp, "Pool possibly") || strstr(ptmp, "Bad signature") ||
                strstr(ptmp, "double-deallocate") ||
                strstr(ptmp, "out of memory on request")) {
                extern void ppu_log_host_chain(const char*);
                static int _pn = 0;
                if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_pn, 3)) { fprintf(stderr, "[POOLTRACE] %.90s\n", ptmp); ppu_log_host_chain("pool-corrupt"); }
            }
        }
        /* DIAGNOSTIC (FLOW_PSSGTRACE=1): when the title logs a PhyreEngine
         * init failure, dump the guest back-chain so we can locate the failing
         * function (the message itself goes through here, not _sys_printf). */
        if (getenv("FLOW_PSSGTRACE") && len < 4096) {
            char tmp[256]; uint32_t n = len < 255 ? len : 255;
            memcpy(tmp, vm_base + buf_ea, n); tmp[n] = 0;
            /* The PhyreEngine failure message is written in fragments, so no
             * single buffer holds "PSSG". Dump the back-chain for any fragment
             * carrying init/error/Phyre keywords. */
            if (strstr(tmp, "PSSG") || strstr(tmp, "Init") || strstr(tmp, "App") ||
                strstr(tmp, "fail") || strstr(tmp, "Error") || strstr(tmp, "rror") ||
                strstr(tmp, "PSpu") || strstr(tmp, "ation") || strstr(tmp, "Mystery")) {
                uint32_t sp = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[1];
                fprintf(stderr, "[pssg-bt] tty_write \"%.50s\" lr=0x%08X\n", tmp, (uint32_t)ctx->lr);
                /* The back-chain below is unreliable under the DRAIN/fragment
                 * model (LR slots read 0); the host-backtrace mapper is not. */
                { extern void ppu_guest_callstack(const char*); ppu_guest_callstack("tty"); }
                for (int i = 0; i < 28 && sp && sp < 0x10000000u; i++) {
                    uint32_t nsp; memcpy(&nsp, vm_base + sp, 4);
                    nsp = ((nsp>>24)&0xFF)|((nsp>>8)&0xFF00)|((nsp<<8)&0xFF0000)|((nsp<<24)&0xFF000000);
                    if (nsp <= sp || nsp >= 0x10000000u) break;
                    uint32_t lr; memcpy(&lr, vm_base + nsp + 0x10, 4);
                    lr = ((lr>>24)&0xFF)|((lr>>8)&0xFF00)|((lr<<8)&0xFF0000)|((lr<<24)&0xFF000000);
                    fprintf(stderr, "[pssg-bt]   #%d lr=0x%08X\n", i, lr);
                    sp = nsp;
                }
                fflush(stderr);
            }
        }
    }

    /* Write back the number of bytes written */
    if (pwr_ea && vm_base) {
        uint32_t be_len = ((len >> 24) & 0xFF) | ((len >> 8) & 0xFF00) |
                          ((len << 8) & 0xFF0000) | ((len << 24) & 0xFF000000);
        memcpy(vm_base + pwr_ea, &be_len, 4);
    }

    return 0; /* CELL_OK */
}

static int64_t sys_tty_read(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    /* s32 sys_tty_read(s32 ch, void* buf, u32 len, u32* preadlen) */
    uint32_t prd_ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[6];

    /* No TTY input available — return 0 bytes read */
    if (prd_ea && vm_base)
        memset(vm_base + prd_ea, 0, 4);

    return 0;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Registration
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

#define SYS_TTY_READ   402
#define SYS_TTY_WRITE  403

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Stateful SPU thread group tracker
 *
 * We don't execute SPU programs — SPURS job queues, SPU tasks, and raw SPU
 * threads all resolve to an empty "thread completed normally" result. But
 * the PPU-side wrappers (PhyreEngine's SPURS wrapper in particular) check
 * returned IDs, out-param cause/status fields, and per-thread exit codes
 * after every call. A flat "return 0" stub leaves the out-params as heap
 * garbage and the wrapper then throws a C++ exception.
 *
 * This tracker assigns monotonically-increasing IDs, walks a small state
 * machine, and writes all the out-params each syscall is documented to
 * set. It doesn't try to emulate actual SPU work — the group transitions
 * straight from STARTED to STOPPED with exit code 0.
 *
 * Cause values match the public Sony SDK headers:
 *   GROUP_EXIT       = 0x0001 — sys_spu_thread_group_exit() was called
 *   ALL_THREADS_EXIT = 0x0002 — all threads completed their entry fn
 *   TERMINATED       = 0x0004 — sys_spu_thread_group_terminate() fired
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/

#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_INITIALIZED  0
#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_READY        1
#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_RUNNING      2
#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_STOPPED      3
#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_DESTROYED    4
#define SPU_GROUP_STATE_SUSPENDED    5

#define SPU_GROUP_CAUSE_GROUP_EXIT        0x0001u
#define SPU_GROUP_CAUSE_ALL_THREADS_EXIT  0x0002u
#define SPU_GROUP_CAUSE_TERMINATED        0x0004u

#define MAX_SPU_GROUPS   32

/* RPCS3_REFERENCE_REVIEWED: group-event types and keys follow the LV2 ABI
 * contract in RPCS3 sys_spu.h. No RPCS3 implementation body is copied. */
#define SYS_SPU_THREAD_GROUP_EVENT_RUN           1u
#define SYS_SPU_THREAD_GROUP_EVENT_EXCEPTION     2u
#define SYS_SPU_THREAD_GROUP_EVENT_SYSTEM_MODULE 4u
#define SYS_SPU_THREAD_GROUP_EVENT_RUN_KEY UINT64_C(0xFFFFFFFF53505500)
#define SYS_SPU_THREAD_GROUP_TYPE_COOPERATE_WITH_SYSTEM 0x20u
#define MAX_SPU_THREADS  (MAX_SPU_GROUPS * 8)
#define MAX_SPU_QUEUE_BINDINGS 32

#ifdef _WIN32
#  include <windows.h>
typedef HANDLE spu_thread_handle_t;
typedef HANDLE spu_thread_event_t;
#else
#  include <pthread.h>
#  include <errno.h>
typedef pthread_t spu_thread_handle_t;
typedef struct {
    pthread_mutex_t mu;
    pthread_cond_t  cv;
    int             done;
